findings.headline: Full 100% shortfall owed instead of a fraction, with no affiliate revenue credit
findings.finding_text: The contract requires Group to pay the entire F&B shortfall dollar-for-dollar, far exceeding CD's standard of 35% of the difference. It also contains no provision counting affiliate organization or exhibitor F&B spend toward the minimum, which would help Group meet it.
findings.cd_standard: Shortfall billed at 35% of the gap, not the full difference; affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue counts toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If Group's actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum guarantee, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's Event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: If Group's actual food and beverage consumption during the Event Period falls short of the minimum guarantee, Group shall pay the shortfall in full. The Hotel shall calculate the shortfall based on the final invoice and supporting documentation from Hotel food service records. The shortfall payment rate shall be one hundred percent (100%) of the difference between the minimum guarantee and actual consumption.
findings.exposure_basis: Shortfall amount not calculable without a stated F&B minimum dollar figure, which is absent from the contract.

findings.headline: Outside vendors barred entirely, with a $2,500 penalty per violation
findings.finding_text: The contract mandates exclusive use of Hotel-appointed vendors for all services and imposes a flat $2,500 surcharge for each unauthorized outside vendor engagement, contrary to CD's position that Group should be free to use its vendor of choice at no surcharge.
findings.cd_standard: Group may use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge; in-house vendors are not mandatory.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house or exclusively appointed vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage for all services at the Hotel only vendors appointed exclusively by the Hotel or operating as part of the Hotel's in-house service divisions, and Group shall not retain, contract with, or permit on the Hotel's premises any outside vendor, supplier, decorator, caterer, audiovisual provider, florist, musician, photographer, or other service provider without the Hotel's prior written consent. Group's use of any outside vendor in violation of this requirement shall incur a surcharge of $2,500.00 for each such engagement.
findings.exposure_basis: Flat surcharge stated per unauthorized vendor engagement.

findings.headline: Night-by-night measurement, 90% threshold, full rate damages, no audit rights
findings.finding_text: The attrition clause departs sharply from CD's standard across every dimension: it measures shortfalls night-by-night rather than cumulatively; sets the liability trigger at 90% occupancy rather than 70%; charges 100% of the nightly rate rather than 70% lost profit; declares the Hotel's records final/binding and expressly bars Group from any audit or verification; and includes no rebooking credit provision.
findings.cd_standard: Cumulative measurement across the block, 70% pickup trigger, 70% lost-profit damages on unsold rooms only, audit rights, and rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block (340 rooms). For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $289.00 (plus tax, if required by applicable law). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation, and such records shall be open to Group for audit and verification. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, with shortfalls calculated by comparing actual rooms occupied to the block size on each night of the event period. Group shall be deemed in attrition if actual occupancy falls below the attrition threshold of ninety percent (90%) on any night. The Hotel shall calculate attrition based on the Hotel's registration records and room records, which constitute the final and binding record of occupancy for purposes of this agreement. Should Group's occupancy fall below ninety percent (90%) on any night during the event period, Group shall be liable for attrition damages at the rate of one hundred percent (100%) of the nightly room rate for each unoccupied room within the block. The Hotel's determination of occupancy, calculation of attrition damages, and assessment of liability shall be final and binding upon Group. The Hotel's occupancy records, registration cards, and room-by-room occupancy logs shall not be open to Group for audit, verification, or inspection, and Group waives any right to independently verify the Hotel's calculations or to contest the Hotel's occupancy records on any basis.
findings.exposure_basis: Full block is 680 room nights (170 rooms x 4 nights) at $289; at 90% threshold, a single night falling to e.g. 80% occupancy (34 unsold rooms) would cost 34 x $289 = $9,826 under the contract's 100% rate versus 70% under CD's standard; over the 4-night pattern the exposure could reach roughly $39,304 per similar shortfall night, compounding since night-by-night measurement (rather than cumulative) removes the offset from strong nights.

findings.headline: Epidemics, travel advisories excluded; deposits kept even after cancellation
findings.finding_text: The clause expressly excludes epidemics, pandemics, government travel advisories/restrictions, and attendee health/safety concerns from force majeure — the opposite of CD's position that these should qualify. It also requires physical impossibility (a narrower standard than commercial impracticability or inadvisability), gives only 48 hours' notice, and states the Hotel retains all deposits and prior payments even when force majeure excuses performance, with no refund.
findings.cd_standard: Either party may cancel without liability for causes making performance illegal, impossible, impracticable or inadvisable, or causing/anticipating 20%+ attendee cancellations, explicitly including epidemics, disease, travel advisories, and government restrictions; deposits refunded promptly.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including, but not limited to, acts of God; war; curtailment or interruption of transportation facilities; strikes; threats or acts of terrorism; disease or epidemic; a CDC advisory, or a State Department or other governmental or international agency travel advisory; full or partial government closure; declaration of a national, state, or local emergency; prohibition or limitation of travel by any government employees; corporate or educational institution travel restrictions; civil disturbance; earthquakes, floods, or similar extraordinary natural events; or any other cause beyond the parties' control — in that party's reasonable judgment make it commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), illegal, or impossible to perform, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel their attendance. The party seeking to invoke this clause will provide written notice within a reasonable time of the occurrence. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events are limited to occurrences such as war, acts of terrorism, earthquakes, floods, or similar extraordinary natural events that render performance of this agreement objectively impossible without regard to economic hardship, inconvenience, or increased cost. Notwithstanding any other provision of this agreement, the following shall not constitute force majeure: government-issued travel restrictions, travel advisories, or governmental directives limiting group gatherings or travel, regardless of the reason such restrictions or advisories are issued; epidemics, pandemics, or declarations of public health emergency, including any government responses thereto; or concerns among Group members regarding attendee safety, willingness to travel, or health considerations. The invocation of force majeure by either party shall not relieve Group of its obligations to remit the deposit and initial payment to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel despite any termination of this agreement resulting from force majeure. The Hotel's only obligation upon occurrence of force majeure shall be to release Group from performance obligations prospectively; no refund or credit shall be issued for payments previously made.
findings.exposure_basis: Security deposit of $25,000 would be forfeited to Hotel even if event is cancelled for a qualifying force majeure event under CD's broader standard.

findings.headline: Hotel can add undisclosed fees anytime; resort fee not waived
findings.finding_text: The clause allows the Hotel to impose new fees and surcharges at any time after signing, and requires Group to pay them 'whether or not such fees were disclosed prior to Group's signature' — the reverse of CD's requirement that undisclosed charges be waived. It also imposes a $35/night resort fee on every room, including complimentary rooms, with no waiver and no requirement of Group's written approval for post-signature add-ons.
findings.cd_standard: All fees must be disclosed in writing before signing; undisclosed charges are waived; post-signature add-ons need Group's written approval; resort fees waived for attendees while resort services are honored.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges that may be associated with the Event, including but not limited to facility fees, energy surcharges, sustainability fees, labor surcharges, and other operational charges. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Should Group require additional services or equipment after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will waive the resort fee for all attendees, including those in complimentary rooms, while continuing to honor the resort fee services.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose additional fees, surcharges, and service charges upon Group at any time, including without limitation after the execution of this Agreement. Group shall pay all such fees as added to its bills, whether or not such fees were disclosed prior to Group's signature on this Agreement. A resort fee of $35.00 per occupied room per night shall be charged to all rooms in the block. This resort fee is in addition to all room rates and shall be applied to every room night, including complimentary room nights that Group may receive.
findings.exposure_basis: $35/night resort fee x 680 total room nights (170 rooms x 4 nights x average block) across the block = approximately $23,800 minimum, doubled-order-of-magnitude range if additional undisclosed fees are added; base calculation: 340 peak rooms average x 4 nights x $35 ≈ $47,600.

findings.headline: Comp ratio only 1-per-75, discretionary, and forfeited on any shortfall
findings.finding_text: The ratio offered (1 per 75 paid room nights) is worse than CD's 1-per-40 standard, is explicitly labeled a non-binding 'guideline' subject to the Hotel's sole discretion, and is entirely forfeited if the block is not 100% met — far more punitive than CD's position that comps should not be forfeited due to attrition already compensated elsewhere. Complimentary internet is also conditioned on exclusive in-house AV use elsewhere in the contract, contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: 1 complimentary room per 40 occupied room nights, cumulative, not forfeited due to attrition, all occupied rooms counted, and complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status or vendor choice.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup. Complimentary room credits earned under this clause will not be forfeited due to any shortfall in Group's room block commitment. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms regardless of Group's choice of audio-visual provider.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide complimentary room nights to Group based on a ratio of one (1) complimentary room per seventy-five (75) paid room nights occupied during the Event Period. The complimentary room ratio of seventy-five (75) stated above is a guideline only and does not create an entitlement in Group. The award and allocation of any complimentary rooms shall be at the sole and absolute discretion of the Hotel, and the Hotel may elect to award fewer complimentary rooms than the guideline ratio would suggest or may decline to award complimentary rooms altogether. Should Group fail to meet its room block commitment during the Event Period, all complimentary room credits earned under this clause shall be forfeited in their entirety.
findings.exposure_basis: Comp room value depends on actual pickup, which is not yet known.

findings.headline: Hotel may refuse assignment for any reason, even to a successor association manager
findings.finding_text: The clause gives Hotel absolute, unreviewable discretion to withhold consent to any assignment, including to a successor management company or affiliated entity, contrary to CD's position that such assignments should proceed without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.cd_standard: Group may assign to a successor management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent where the event is substantially unchanged; other assignments require consent not unreasonably withheld.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all. Hotel shall have no obligation to provide reasons for refusing consent or to negotiate the terms upon which consent might be granted.

findings.headline: Group indemnifies Hotel for Hotel's own negligence; Hotel indemnifies nothing
findings.finding_text: The clause requires Group to indemnify the Hotel even for claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence (carving out only gross negligence/willful misconduct), while expressly stating the Hotel will not indemnify Group under any circumstance. Only Group is required to carry insurance. This is a one-sided allocation contrary to CD's standard of mutual, negligence-based indemnification and mutual insurance obligations.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct; group never indemnifies hotel's own negligence; insurance is a mutual obligation.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and independent contractors against all claims, losses, or damages to persons or property, governmental charges or fines, and costs (including reasonable attorney's fees), arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party, its employees, agents, or contractors. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence. This provision survives the termination or expiration of this Agreement. Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall indemnify, defend with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Hotel, and hold harmless the Hotel, its owners, managers, employees, and agents from and against all claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from Group's performance of this Agreement, Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel facilities, Group's events and activities, or any act or omission by Group, its officers, employees, agents, or invitees. This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises, provided that Group's indemnity shall not extend to claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The Hotel shall not indemnify Group and makes no commitment to defend Group against any claim, and Group waives any right to claim indemnification from the Hotel under this Agreement or under applicable law, except as expressly modified by the indemnity limitations set forth herein.

findings.headline: Cause-based termination still triggers full cancellation damages scale
findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly deems any Group termination — for cause or otherwise — a cancellation subject to the liquidated damages scale, contrary to CD's requirement that termination for cause carry no liability at all. The contract also omits most of CD's listed termination triggers (epidemic determination, labor dispute, facility/service reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) entirely.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause (including epidemic determination, labor dispute, brand/ownership change, renovation interference, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) should allow Group to walk away with no liability, separate from the cancellation scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) the adoption of state or local legislation that permits discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the grounds upon which Group effects termination, whether for cause, convenience, or otherwise, any and all termination by Group shall be deemed and treated as a cancellation subject to the cancellation damages scale set forth in this Agreement. Group acknowledges that termination and cancellation are not distinct events but rather the same occurrence governed by a single damages regime. The cancellation scale shall apply to every termination regardless of its cause, and Group waives any argument that termination for cause stands outside the cancellation framework. The Hotel's right to cancellation damages shall not be diminished by Group's assertion that the Hotel committed a material breach.

findings.headline: Notice up to 90 days late; bankruptcy/foreclosure excluded from any right
findings.finding_text: CD requires notice within 30 days and a 30-day termination window; here the Hotel need only notify 'no later than 90 days prior' and only 'to the extent practicable,' Group gets just 10 days to terminate, and bankruptcy/foreclosure/receivership are expressly carved out of any notice or termination right at all.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel notifies within 30 days of change; Group may terminate without liability within 30 days of notice; refund within 5 days; includes bankruptcy/foreclosure.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide written notice to the Group in the event of a change in the Hotel's brand affiliation, management company, ownership, or controlling interest; provided, however, that the Hotel shall provide such notice no later than ninety (90) days prior to the effective date of any such change, to the extent practicable and permitted by the Hotel's corporate counsel and applicable law. Upon receipt of notice of a material change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group shall have the right to terminate this Agreement by providing written notice to the Hotel within ten (10) days of receipt of such notice, and such termination shall be effective upon receipt by the Hotel. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, the Group acknowledges that the Hotel may be subject to bankruptcy, foreclosure, receivership, or other insolvency proceedings, and that such events shall not trigger any notice requirement, termination right, or remedy available to the Group.
findings.location_section: 23. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership

findings.headline: 90-day refund window and deposit applied to attrition and F&B shortfalls
findings.finding_text: The deposit is refundable only within 90 days rather than CD's 30-day standard, and is expressly permitted to be applied against attrition charges, F&B shortfalls, and other unrelated obligations, contrary to CD's position that the deposit should not offset those items.
findings.cd_standard: Deposit refunded within 30 days absent itemized documented damage; not applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit collected under this Agreement will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless the Hotel provides Group with an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may apply the security deposit, or such portion thereof as necessary, against any attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damages to the Hotel's premises, incidental costs, outstanding room charges, service failures, cancellation penalties, or any other sum that the Group owes to the Hotel under this Agreement or arising from the Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel's facilities. Any remaining balance of the security deposit shall be refunded to the Group within ninety (90) days following the last day of the Event, provided that all invoices have been paid in full, all obligations have been satisfied, and no claims for damages are then pending.
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit stated in the contract.

findings.headline: No periodic pickup reports, 90-day post-event report, and audit rights waived
findings.finding_text: The contract provides pickup reports only on request 'at the Hotel's convenience' with no weekly cadence, sets the post-event report deadline at 90 days rather than 30, and explicitly denies Group any right to audit room block records or verify occupancy — the opposite of CD's audit-rights standard, including credit for miscoded rooms.
findings.cd_standard: Written 24/12-month block reviews with adjustment rights; weekly pickup reports from a set point before cutoff; final reports within 10 days of departure; post-event report within 30 days; no-cost audit rights with miscoded-room credit.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date, and final room pickup reports with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. Within thirty (30) days of departure, Hotel will provide a full post-event report, including rooms actualized, revenue by rate category, and itemized charges for all services rendered. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a representative of Group or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide pickup reports to Group showing room occupancy, rate structure, and charges incurred under the room block only upon Group's written request and at the Hotel's convenience, and no regular or periodic reporting shall be deemed a condition of this Agreement. Group shall not have a right to receive weekly, daily, or real-time updates on room block performance, and the Hotel reserves the right to provide such information in summary form and at intervals it deems appropriate. Within ninety (90) days following the conclusion of Group's event on April 16, 2027, the Hotel shall provide Group with a comprehensive post-event report detailing final room block results, attendee counts, revenue by rate category, and itemized charges for all services rendered. Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or verify the Hotel's room block records, reservation systems, or internal accounting related to Group's event, and Group waives any audit rights it might otherwise possess under applicable law or contract principles.

findings.headline: Hotel disclaims all ADA responsibility and shifts every accessibility cost to Group
findings.finding_text: The clause disclaims any Hotel warranty or representation of ADA compliance and requires Group to fund all auxiliary aids anywhere in the Hotel, including guest rooms and common areas — contrary to CD's standard dividing responsibility, with the Hotel funding guest room and common area accommodations.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel warrants ADA compliance of guest rooms, common areas, and function space; each party funds auxiliary aids in its own area (Group in function space, Hotel in guest rooms/common areas), with mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act, as amended, or any state or local accessibility law, and Group assumes sole responsibility for assessing the suitability of the Hotel's premises for Group's attendees and event purposes. Should Group require auxiliary aids, services, modifications, or accommodations to make any portion of the Hotel accessible or usable by Group's attendees, Group shall fund and arrange for all such auxiliary aids and accommodations, including but not limited to interpreters, readers, accessible transportation, specialized signage, or technology enhancements, regardless of where within the Hotel such aids or accommodations are required or how they are deployed.

findings.headline: Maryland venue/law, punitive damages, and skewed prevailing-party fees favor Hotel
findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are set to Maryland (the Hotel's location) rather than Group's location, the clause allows Hotel to recover punitive damages, and it awards attorney's fees to whichever party the Hotel deems 'prevailing' (defined to favor the Hotel), contrary to CD's standard of each party bearing its own fees with no punitive damages.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue in Group's state; no punitive damages; each party bears its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will be responsible for its own attorney's fees and expenses.
findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the Hotel is located, without regard to its conflict of law principles, and the parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Maryland for the resolution of any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the event, or the performance or breach hereof. In any action or proceeding brought by the Hotel to enforce its rights or to recover damages for breach of this Agreement, the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law. In the event of any dispute, claim, or proceeding arising from or relating to this Agreement, including any action for breach, enforcement, or interpretation, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover reasonable attorney's fees, court costs, and all other expenses of litigation, including expert fees and investigation costs, from the non-prevailing party as part of the judgment or award. The Hotel shall be deemed the prevailing party if it recovers any material relief, whether by judgment, settlement, or otherwise.

findings.headline: Full deposit forfeited even when cancelling under the named storm right
findings.finding_text: The named storm clause requires cancellation notice within a very tight 24-hour window and, unlike a standard no-liability cancellation, forces Group to forfeit its entire deposit even when properly invoking the right, contrary to CD's position that qualifying storm cancellation should carry no liability.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm cancellation right should permit cancellation without liability, with its own notice window; deposit should not be forfeited for validly invoking the right.
findings.proposed_language: Should the National Weather Service issue a hurricane watch or named tropical storm warning that affects the Baltimore, Maryland area within seventy-two (72) hours of any event date, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice, and Hotel will refund all deposits paid by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of cancellation.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Group shall forfeit the deposit paid to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel as partial compensation for the Hotel's lost revenue and costs incurred in preparation for the event.
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit forfeited upon invoking named storm cancellation.

findings.headline: Attendee data usable for Hotel's own marketing and shared with third parties
findings.finding_text: The clause explicitly permits the Hotel to use attendee data for its own marketing/promotional purposes and to share it with affiliates, brand partners, and third-party marketers without further Group consent — contrary to CD's standard limiting use to reservation fulfillment.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list/attendee data used solely to fulfill reservations; no Hotel marketing use or third-party disclosure without Group's prior written consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: Group acknowledges that the Hotel may utilize such attendee data for the Hotel's own marketing, promotional, and business development purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email marketing, targeted advertising, and future event solicitation directed to attendees or their affiliated organizations. Group consents to the Hotel's use of such data and waives any objection to such use. In addition to the Hotel's own use, Group authorizes the Hotel to share and disclose attendee data with the Hotel's corporate affiliates, brand partners, and third-party marketing service providers who assist the Hotel in analyzing market trends, identifying corporate event opportunities, and promoting the Hotel's services and facilities to potential group customers.

findings.headline: No CBA notice and no cancellation right for labor disputes
findings.finding_text: The contract expressly relieves the Hotel of any obligation to disclose CBA expiration dates or notify Group of labor disputes, and denies Group any right to cancel due to a strike, lockout, or labor action, contrary to CD's standard providing advance CBA notice and an unconditional cancellation right for disputes within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel provides CBA expiration list a year in advance and prompt notice of disputes; Group may cancel without liability if a strike/lockout/expired contract arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One (1) year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform, and any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not be obligated to provide the Group with advance written notice regarding the expiration date, renewal status, or proposed modification of any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor accord to which the Hotel is a party. In the event of a labor dispute, strike, work stoppage, lockout, labor action, or other labor-related event affecting the Hotel or its operations, no cancellation window or notice period is defined herein, and the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement based upon the occurrence or threatened occurrence of any such labor-related event.

findings.headline: 24% charge undefined, with Hotel free to keep it all instead of paying staff
findings.finding_text: The contract treats 'gratuity' and 'service charge' as interchangeable and undefined, and gives the Hotel sole discretion to retain the full 24% as its own revenue rather than distributing it to staff, contrary to CD's standard requiring gratuity be fully distributed to staff with the service charge separately disclosed as Hotel revenue.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge separately defined and confirmed with distinct percentages; gratuity fully distributed to staff who worked the event; service charge disclosed as Hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: Eighteen percent (18%) of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of six percent (6%), plus applicable tax, is distinct from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: A service charge and gratuity shall be added to all food and beverage, banquet, and room charges, and the terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' shall be used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and are not separately defined. The combined gratuity and service charge shall be automatically applied at the rate of twenty-four percent (24%) of the subtotal of all covered charges before tax. The Hotel shall determine in its sole discretion the allocation and distribution of any gratuity and service charge collected from Group. The Hotel may retain the gratuity and service charge as its own revenue or may distribute a portion or all of it to service staff at the Hotel's election. No representation is made regarding the destination of these funds, and Group waives any right to direct, approve, or inquire into the allocation thereof.
findings.exposure_basis: Percentage is stated (24% of covered charges) but total covered charges are not stated in the contract.

findings.headline: No dispute window, 1.5% finance charge, and unlimited prepayment discretion
findings.finding_text: The contract denies Group any right to dispute charges after receipt of invoice, imposes a compounding 1.5%/month finance charge (above CD's 1% cap), and gives the Hotel unfettered discretion to set any prepayment amount if credit is not approved rather than the staged schedule CD requires.
findings.cd_standard: Payable on invoice with a real dispute window before finance charges apply; finance charge capped at 1%/month or legal maximum, whichever is less; staged deposit schedule (25%/25%/50%) if credit denied.
findings.proposed_language: If Group's credit is approved, the master account is payable upon receipt of invoice. If payment of all undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: All invoiced charges to the master account shall be due in full upon presentation, and the Group waives any right to dispute or withhold payment of billed amounts after receipt of an invoice from the Hotel. Should the Group fail to remit full payment of undisputed invoiced amounts by the date due, a monthly finance charge of 1.5% shall accrue on the unpaid balance, calculated from the due date until payment is received in full by the Hotel. This finance charge shall compound monthly and shall be added to the master account statement without further notice. Where the Hotel has not approved credit for the Group, the Hotel may require prepayment in such amount as the Hotel determines to be appropriate before rooms are held, facilities are reserved, or services are rendered.

findings.headline: Walked guests bear all costs; no rebate, no return upgrade, no pickup credit
findings.finding_text: The contract places all costs of relocation (lodging, transportation) on the walked guest instead of the Hotel, provides no per-room-night rebate to Group, denies any upgrade or welcome amenity on return, and excludes relocated nights entirely from pickup, occupancy, and commission calculations — the opposite of CD's standard, which requires Hotel-funded relocation and preserved pickup/commission credit with no attrition liability for walked nights.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel pays for comparable/better accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity on return; Group receives a per-room-night rebate and pickup/commission credit for relocated nights, with no attrition liability for those nights; extra compensation for large-scale walks.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate any member of Group holding a confirmed reservation, Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable or better hotel as close as possible, at no charge to the guest, for each night the guest is displaced; (b) provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel; (c) forward the displaced guest's telephone messages, mail, and packages; and (d) when the guest returns, provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity. Hotel will credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable at the group rate, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is walked. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: In the event the Hotel is unable to provide accommodations to any guest for whom a reservation has been guaranteed under this Agreement, the Hotel shall make a reasonable effort to secure alternative lodging at the guest's sole expense and cost. All transportation to and from any alternative hotel, including airport transfers, shall be the guest's own responsibility and expense, and the Hotel shall have no obligation to arrange, provide, or reimburse for any transportation costs incurred by the guest. Upon the Group's return to the Harborview Grand Hotel following any relocation, the relocated guest shall be assigned to a standard guest room without any upgrade, suite premium, room enhancement, or additional amenity as compensation for the inconvenience of relocation. The guest shall receive no reduction in room rate, no complimentary services, and no credit toward future stays. Each night during which a guest's guaranteed reservation was relocated to an alternative hotel shall not be credited toward the Group's room pickup, occupancy count, or commission calculation, and such nights shall be excluded entirely from all metrics used to measure the Group's performance under the terms of this Agreement.

findings.headline: Hotel has no duty to resell rooms and keeps all resale revenue without credit
findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly disclaims any obligation for the Hotel to attempt resale of released rooms, allows it to retain all resale revenue as pure additional profit with no credit against Group's damages, and denies Group any right to review resale records or challenge the Hotel's mitigation efforts, contrary to CD's requirement of an affirmative, documented mitigation duty with credit and transparency.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel has an affirmative, documented duty to attempt resale of canceled rooms/space and credit proceeds against damages owed; records available to Group; cancellation damages due only after showing of mitigation effort.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel will document in writing its efforts to market the dates proactively through all group and transient channels. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold. All Hotel records relating to mitigation will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of any room inventory or function space by Group, whether through attrition, cancellation, or other reduction of Group's commitment, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory or function space, nor shall the Hotel be required to undertake any specific actions, marketing efforts, or promotional activities directed toward filling released space. Any revenue generated by the Hotel from the resale or release of rooms or function space originally committed to Group shall be retained in full by the Hotel as additional revenue beyond what Group owes under the terms of this agreement, including without limitation attrition charges, cancellation damages, or any other fees or charges assessed herein. The Hotel's resale efforts, the terms at which resale accommodations are offered to other customers, the identity of parties to whom space is resold, the rate at which such space is resold, and the complete records related to all resale transactions shall not be open to Group for inspection, audit, or verification of any kind.

findings.headline: Hotel may undercut Group's rate freely with no retroactive fix or pickup credit
findings.finding_text: The contract lets the Hotel sell rooms to the public below Group's negotiated rate without restriction, applies any correction only prospectively to future reservations (not retroactively), and strips commission and pickup credit from any adjusted rate — contrary to CD's rate parity standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel guarantees it will not sell rooms below Group's contracted rate (except qualified rates); if it does, rate is adjusted (including retroactively) or all attendee bookings count toward block, with commission and pickup credit preserved.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees. Commission will be paid on the contracted rate regardless of any rate adjustment, and such rooms remain creditable toward Group's pickup, complimentary-room credits, attrition, and any other concession based on pickup.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains the absolute right to sell rooms to the general public at any rate, including rates below the rate offered to Group. Should the Hotel identify that it has sold rooms to the general public at a rate lower than Group's negotiated rate, any rate adjustment applied to Group's block shall be effective only for future reservations made after the Hotel has identified and approved the lower rate. No retroactive adjustment to Group's rate shall apply to reservations already confirmed prior to the date on which the lower rate is identified. Any rate adjustment determined by the Hotel to apply to Group's block shall be treated as a non-commissionable rate for purposes of Group's commission or rebate structure under this Agreement. An adjusted rate shall not count toward Group's room block pickup calculations, occupancy targets, or any other metric used to measure Group's performance against block commitments.

findings.headline: 45-day cutoff with rack-rate reversion, no post-cutoff group rate protection
findings.finding_text: The cutoff date of 45 days prior to arrival exceeds CD's 21-day maximum, and after cutoff attendees revert entirely to rack rate rather than continuing to receive the group rate while the Hotel is still selling rooms; released rooms are also handled at the Hotel's sole discretion without consultation with Group.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival; group rate continues post-cutoff while Hotel sells to the public; unassigned rooms held on prepayment or released after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type. After consultation with Group, Hotel may offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the block committed for the National Association of Coastal Engineers event shall be accepted by the Hotel only when received on or before forty-five (45) days prior to the arrival date of April 12, 2027. Any reservation request received after the cutoff date of forty-five (45) days prior to arrival shall be offered accommodations, if available, only at the Hotel's prevailing rack rate in effect at the time of booking, with no access to the negotiated group rate regardless of the reason for the late request. The Hotel shall have no obligation to hold inventory beyond the cutoff date, and rooms not reserved by that date shall be released to the Hotel's general inventory for sale at the Hotel's sole discretion.

findings.headline: Hotel liability capped at deposit refund even for wrongful cancellation
findings.finding_text: If the Hotel wrongfully cancels, its liability is limited solely to refunding deposits paid, with an express exclusion of consequential damages — contrary to CD's standard requiring the Hotel to cover all direct, indirect, and consequential damages Group incurs, including relocation and rebooking costs.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel that cancels without contractual right owes all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, including staff time/travel, rate/airfare differentials, function space rental, attorney's fees, and printing/communication costs.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.
findings.quoted_text: In the event the Hotel wrongfully cancels this Agreement, the Hotel's sole obligation and the Group's exclusive remedy shall be the refund of any deposits paid by the Group to the Hotel, without interest and without liability for any other costs, losses, or damages incurred by the Group in connection with the event. The Hotel shall not be liable for any consequential, incidental, indirect, or special damages, including but not limited to lost profits, reputational harm, or costs associated with event rescheduling or venue relocation.

findings.headline: No named rooms, reassignment at will, rental fees charged with no included AV
findings.finding_text: No function room is actually named or assigned minimum square footage/ceiling height in the Agreement itself (Exhibit A lists space only tentatively pending signature and confirms nothing binding); the Hotel may reassign space unilaterally by notice alone; and the contract requires payment of standard rental charges with no provision for complimentary meeting space or in-room AV items (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC) at no charge.
findings.cd_standard: Named function rooms with minimum square footage/ceiling height, no changes without both parties' written consent, complimentary meeting space with rental waived, and each room comes with wired mic/podium/power/lighting/HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Exhibit A, with room rental charges waived, specifying each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall assign all function space for the Group's use during the Event at the Hotel's sole discretion, and no function room is named or reserved in this Agreement. The Group acknowledges that the Hotel retains the right to change any function space assignment at any time by written notice to the Group's authorized representative, provided that such reassignment shall not materially diminish the aggregate square footage or suitability of space made available to the Group. The Group shall pay all applicable rental charges for meeting rooms and function space utilized during the Event, calculated according to the Hotel's standard pricing schedule in effect at the time of booking. The Hotel shall provide no credit, reduction, or waiver of function space rental fees regardless of Group's use of in-house audio-visual services, catering packages, or other Hotel services.
findings.exposure_basis: Rental fee amount not specified in the contract.

findings.headline: No remedy if Hotel materially cuts facilities, services, or staffing
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially reduces restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, contracted meeting space, or staffing ratios. Instead, the construction/renovation clause affirmatively bars Group from any remedy for disruption to facilities or services, leaving Group without recourse if service levels are cut.
findings.cd_standard: If Hotel closes/limits facilities by more than 25% or materially reduces staffing ratios, it must first offer equal alternatives at its expense; if unresolved within 30 days, Group may cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, or safety and security services in a manner a hotel industry executive would agree is material, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services, mutually agreeable and solely at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to Hotel, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.headline: No cap on future rate increases or reduction if market rates decline
findings.finding_text: The contract sets fixed rates for the confirmed event dates but contains no provision at all addressing a cap on future rate increases or a reduction if market rates decline before arrival, which CD's standard calls for as a hedge in the event rates are later revisited.
findings.cd_standard: Any future-year rate increase capped at 2% per year over quoted rates; group rate reduced if market average or hotel's published rate declines before arrival; rates finalized in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over the rates quoted in this Agreement for any future contract year. Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.headline: Name changes charged rate differential; harsh 72-hour cancellation and no-show rules
findings.finding_text: Name changes are treated as new reservations at the prevailing (not group) rate with the attendee bearing any differential; individual cancellations must be made more than 72 hours before arrival (versus CD's 6pm-day-of-arrival standard) or a one-night charge applies; a no-show cancels the attendee's entire remaining stay with no reinstatement for the following night; and there is no provision crediting individual cancellation charges against Group's attrition liability.
findings.cd_standard: Name changes at group rate up to arrival; cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival (or 24 hrs, waived for emergencies); no-shows reinstated for the following night at same rate; individual cancellation money credited against Group's attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.
findings.quoted_text: A name change on any individual reservation shall be treated as a new reservation at the Hotel's prevailing rate for comparable accommodations on the relevant dates, and the attendee shall be responsible for any rate difference between the Group rate and the prevailing rate. An attendee who fails to arrive on the first night of his or her reservation shall be deemed to have no-showed, and the Hotel shall cancel the whole remaining reservation for that attendee without further notice or obligation to the attendee or the Group. Individual reservations may be cancelled by the attendee or by the Group, without penalty or charge, only if written notice of cancellation is received by the Hotel's group reservations department more than seventy-two hours prior to the scheduled arrival date of the attendee. Individual reservations cancelled within seventy-two hours of arrival are charged one night's room and tax, which charge shall be non-refundable and shall be the sole remedy available to the Hotel for such late cancellation.

findings.headline: Damages based on gross revenue at steep tiers, no resale credit or rebooking credit
findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated against gross room revenue (rate x full block) rather than 70% lost profit, at tiers reaching as high as 100% at 30 days or fewer, with an express provision that Group receives no credit for any resale revenue the Hotel later earns, and no rebooking credit if a CD client later rebooks the Hotel — all contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Damages as percentage of room profit (70% of net group rate x adjusted block less allowable attrition), disclosed tiers, hotel must mitigate via resale with credit, and rebooking credit for CD clients.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit on the sliding scale below, where one hundred percent (100%) of room profit is defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $289.00, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition: 365 days or more prior to arrival – 25%; 364 through 181 days – 50%; 180 through 91 days – 75%; 90 through 31 days – 90%; 30 days or fewer – 100%. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group cancel this agreement at any time after execution by the parties, Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned by the Hotel for all guest rooms for all nights within the event period of April 12-16, 2027, based upon the negotiated room rate and the full room block size. Group shall not receive credit toward damages owed for any revenue the Hotel subsequently earns from reselling cancelled rooms or function space, as the Hotel's ability to generate such resale revenue is contingent on market conditions beyond the Hotel's control and shall be retained entirely by the Hotel. Should Group elect to rebook with the Hotel at a later date following cancellation of this agreement, such rebooking shall constitute a new and separate commitment and shall earn Group no credit, offset, or other financial benefit against damages that accrued under this cancellation provision prior to the rebooking.
findings.exposure_basis: Full block gross revenue = 680 room nights x $289 = $196,520; at 100% tier this full amount would be owed on gross revenue basis versus CD's 70% lost-profit basis, which would be roughly $137,564.

findings.headline: No staffing ratios guaranteed; labor and bartender fees charged on all functions
findings.finding_text: The contract leaves server/bartender staffing entirely to Hotel discretion with no guaranteed ratios, and charges labor and bartender fees on all Group functions regardless of size, rather than limiting such fees to functions under 25 people as CD's standard requires.
findings.cd_standard: Guaranteed staffing ratios (1 server per 25/20 plated, 40/30 buffet; 1 bartender per 75 hosted/100 cash) at no extra labor charge, with a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.
findings.quoted_text: Staffing at food and beverage functions, including the assignment of servers, bartenders, runners, and other service personnel, is at the Hotel's discretion and shall be determined by the Hotel based on the number of attendees, the complexity of the menu, the duration of the function, and the Hotel's operational requirements. The Hotel shall ensure adequate staffing to provide professional service, but the Hotel's determination of adequate staffing levels shall not be subject to challenge by the Group and shall be final. The Hotel charges labor and bartender fees on Group's food and beverage functions, calculated on the basis of estimated attendance, the scope of service, and the Hotel's then-current labor rates, which fees shall be itemized separately on the Group's invoice and shall be payable as part of the total food and beverage charges due under this Agreement.

findings.headline: No renovation disclosure, notice, or termination right for interference
findings.finding_text: The contract disclaims any representation about current renovation plans, any obligation to notify Group of future work, and any Group remedy or termination right if construction interferes with the event — contrary to CD's standard requiring representation, 30-day notice with mitigation plan, and a termination right for material interference.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel represents no current renovation plans, promises no interference, gives 30 days' written notice with scope/schedule/mitigation plan for later-confirmed work, and Group may terminate without liability if it determines the work will interfere.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the planned scope, schedule, anticipated impact on areas Group will use, and Hotel's plan for minimizing that impact. Hotel promises that any such construction or remodeling will not interfere with Group's use of the Hotel. If Group determines the construction or remodeling will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or guarantee regarding the status, scope, timing, or impact of any construction, renovation, maintenance, or capital improvement work that may be planned, in progress, or completed during the dates of the Event or at any time during the term of this Agreement. The Hotel reserves the right to commence, continue, or complete any construction, renovation, or maintenance work at any time without providing the Group with advance written notice, and without restriction as to timing, scope, noise level, dust, disruption to guest services, or impact on guest experience. In the event that any construction, renovation, maintenance, or capital improvement work interferes with, disrupts, diminishes, or otherwise affects the Group's occupancy, the use and enjoyment of the Hotel's facilities, or the quality of service or accommodations provided to the Group's guests, such work shall not constitute grounds for the Group to terminate this Agreement, to claim damages or loss of value, to demand a rate reduction or credit, or to pursue any other remedy or relief against the Hotel.

findings.headline: No commission clause for ConferenceDirect anywhere in the contract
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision at all addressing payment of commission to ConferenceDirect on actualized room revenue, leaving CD's standard 10% commission, timing, non-cancelability, and survival-of-brand-change protections entirely unaddressed.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel pays ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue (including outside-block, miscoded, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation-fee credited nights) within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable/non-transferable, surviving brand/management change, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.headline: Commitment limited to bare legal minimum; no termination right for hostile legislation
findings.finding_text: The clause limits the Hotel's nondiscrimination obligation strictly to what applicable law requires, disclaims any broader voluntary commitment, and expressly denies Group any right to cancel, terminate, or reduce its block if hostile discriminatory legislation is later adopted — contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel commits that it and staff will not discriminate on listed grounds even where law would allow it; Group may terminate without liability if legislation permits such discrimination or bars local nondiscrimination measures.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city in which Hotel is located adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, or prohibits the adoption of nondiscrimination measures on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's obligations with respect to nondiscrimination, equal treatment, and protected-class accommodations shall be limited to compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local civil rights laws and public accommodations statutes in effect at the time of the Event. The Hotel makes no commitment to any standard, policy, or practice beyond what such applicable law expressly requires, and the Group shall not be entitled to invoke any nondiscrimination clause, covenant, or principle not grounded in enforceable legal requirement. In the event that any change, amendment, or new enactment of state or local law relating to discrimination, equal treatment, or the provision of services occurs after the date of this Agreement and before or during the Event, the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement, terminate the group block, reduce the room block commitment, or claim any modification to the terms hereof.

findings.headline: AV/internet repriced anytime; discounts conditioned on exclusive in-house AV use
findings.finding_text: The Hotel may reprice audio-visual and internet services up to the time of the event with no honoring of any pre-contract quote, and complimentary internet and any AV discounts are expressly conditioned on Group's exclusive use of the in-house AV provider, with all concessions forfeited if Group brings its own equipment or an outside vendor — contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel honors attached AV/internet quotes at contracting with a 20% discount on additions, and use of the in-house AV provider is never a condition for discounted or complimentary services like internet.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of any audio-visual quote prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the internet bandwidth quote provided at contracting, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.
findings.quoted_text: All audio-visual equipment, services, and technology provided by the Hotel or contracted through the Hotel's approved vendors shall be priced according to the Hotel's standard rates and pricing schedule in effect at the time of the Event. The Group shall have no entitlement to pricing quoted prior to the date of this Agreement, and any quotation for audio-visual or internet services shall be deemed valid only for the date on which it was provided. Complimentary internet access and any discounted or complimentary services relating to audio-visual provision, including concessions, upgrades, or technical support at no charge, shall be conditioned upon the Group's exclusive use of the Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider for all function space during the Event. Should the Group elect to contract with an outside audio-visual vendor or bring its own equipment into any function room, the Group shall forfeit all complimentary internet services, discounted rates, and any other concessions the Hotel has offered in connection with in-house provision, and the Group shall pay the Hotel's then-current rate for internet access and technical support.

clause_review.basis: CD requires pricing locked no earlier than 12 months out and only 35% of shortfall owed; contract locks pricing 24 months out (fine, more favorable) but requires 100% of shortfall and no affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting provision.
CD requires free choice of outside vendors at no surcharge; contract mandates Hotel-appointed vendors only and imposes a $2,500 surcharge per unauthorized outside vendor engagement.

CD requires cumulative measurement, 70% threshold, 70% lost-profit damages, audit rights, rebooking credit; contract uses night-by-night measurement, 90% threshold, 100% of nightly rate, no audit rights (records final/binding, no audit), no rebooking credit.

CD requires broad triggers including epidemics/pandemics/travel advisories and 20% attendee cancellation anticipation, prompt refunds; contract expressly excludes epidemics/pandemics/travel advisories/health concerns, requires physical impossibility only, retains deposits despite FM cancellation, no refund.

CD requires all fees disclosed pre-signature and waiver of undisclosed fees, no resort fee or waived/discounted, no early check-in/bag fees; contract allows Hotel to add fees anytime post-signature, charges undisclosed fees, and imposes a $35/night resort fee with no waiver.

CD requires 1 comp per 40 room nights, cumulative, guaranteed regardless of attrition, comp internet regardless of loyalty; contract sets 1 per 75 as mere guideline at Hotel's sole discretion, forfeited entirely if block not 100% met, and complimentary internet not addressed as unconditional (AV clause ties internet to in-house AV use).

CD allows assignment to successor management/affiliated entity without unreasonably withheld consent; contract requires Hotel's consent in its sole and absolute discretion for any assignment, with no carve-out for successor entities.

CD requires mutual indemnification limited to each party's own negligence, mutual insurance; contract makes Group indemnify Hotel even for Hotel's own negligence, Hotel indemnifies Group for nothing, and only Group must carry insurance.

CD requires termination for cause (epidemic, labor dispute, brand change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) without liability, separate from cancellation scale; contract's termination for cause still triggers full cancellation damages scale and excludes most listed causes (no epidemic, no labor dispute, no facility-reduction termination right).

CD requires 30-day notice and Group termination right without liability, refund within 5 days; contract gives Hotel up to 90 days to notify 'to the extent practicable,' only 10 days for Group to terminate, and excludes bankruptcy/foreclosure entirely from notice/termination rights.

CD requires deposit refunded within 30 days absent itemized documented damage, not applied to attrition/F&B shortfalls; contract allows 90-day refund window and expressly permits applying deposit to attrition, F&B shortfalls, and other unrelated charges.

CD requires 24/12-month block reviews with adjustment rights, weekly pickup reports, 10-day final report, 30-day post-event report, and audit rights with miscoded-room credit; contract provides pickup reports only on request 'at Hotel's convenience,' no periodic reviews or adjustment rights, 90-day post-event report, and expressly denies Group any audit rights.

CD requires Hotel warranty of ADA compliance and Hotel funding of auxiliary aids in guest rooms/common areas; contract disclaims any ADA representation/warranty and places all auxiliary aid costs on Group everywhere in the Hotel.

CD requires governing law/venue in Group's state, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees; contract sets Maryland (Hotel's location) as governing law/venue, allows Hotel punitive damages, and awards prevailing-party fees skewed toward Hotel (deemed prevailing on any material relief).

CD calls for cancellation without liability and no deposit forfeiture for named storm; contract requires notice within 24 hours of NWS warning and Group forfeits its deposit entirely upon invoking this right.

CD requires attendee data used only for reservation fulfillment, no Hotel marketing/third-party disclosure without consent; contract expressly permits Hotel's own marketing use and sharing with affiliates/third parties without further consent.

CD requires 1-year advance CBA expiration notice, prompt dispute notice, and unconditional cancellation right within 90 days of event for labor disputes; contract expressly denies any notice obligation and denies Group any cancellation right for labor disputes.

CD requires gratuity and service charge separately defined with gratuity distributed to staff; contract uses the terms interchangeably/undefined, gives Hotel sole discretion to retain the entire 24% as its own revenue with no distribution to staff required.

CD requires payment on invoice with real dispute window before finance charges, capped finance charge at 1%/month, and staged deposit schedule if credit denied; contract denies any dispute right, imposes 1.5%/month compounding finance charge, and gives Hotel unfettered discretion over prepayment amount if credit not approved.
