CD requires Hotel to pay for relocation (comparable/better hotel, transportation, message forwarding, return upgrade/amenity), per-night rebate, pickup/commission credit, no attrition liability for walked nights, extra compensation for large walks; contract puts all costs and arrangement burden on the walked guest, denies any upgrade on return, and excludes relocated nights from pickup/commission credit entirely.

CD requires an affirmative documented mitigation/resale duty with credit against damages and no audit denial; contract explicitly disclaims any resale obligation, lets Hotel keep all resale revenue without credit, and denies Group any right to review resale records.

CD requires no lower public rate than Group's during event dates, retroactive/prospective correction with pickup/commission credit preserved; contract allows Hotel to sell below Group's rate freely, applies corrections only prospectively, and strips commission/pickup credit from any adjusted rate.

CD requires cutoff no earlier than 21 days out and continued group rate post-cutoff while Hotel still sells rooms, plus prepay/refund or consultation before release; contract sets a 45-day cutoff, reverts fully to rack rate after cutoff with no continued group-rate obligation, and releases rooms without consultation with Group.

CD requires Hotel to pay all direct/indirect/consequential damages if it wrongfully cancels; contract limits Hotel's liability solely to deposit refund with no interest and expressly excludes consequential damages.

CD requires named function rooms with min sq ft/ceiling height, no changes without mutual written consent, complimentary space with room rental waived, and in-room AV amenities at no charge; contract assigns no named space, gives Hotel sole discretion to reassign, and charges rental fees per standard schedule with no complimentary meeting space or included AV items.

CD requires equal alternatives if facilities/staffing are materially reduced, with cancellation right if unresolved in 30 days; contract has no facilities/services reduction provision at all — instead construction clause disclaims any remedy for disruption.

CD requires a 2% cap on future rate increases and rate reduction if market declines, with rates finalized 12 months out; the contract has fixed single-year rates already confirmed and contains no provision addressing this at all.

CD requires free name changes at group rate, cancellation without penalty until 6pm day of arrival (or 24 hrs), no-show reinstatement, and individual cancellation credit against attrition; contract charges rate differential for name changes, requires 72-hr cancellation notice or one-night charge, cancels entire remaining stay on no-show without reinstatement, and no credit of individual cancellation fees against attrition.

CD requires damages based on 70% lost-profit formula, mitigation duty with credit, and rebooking credit; contract charges against gross room revenue (not profit) at very steep tiers up to 100%, denies any resale credit, and denies rebooking credit.

CD requires specific server/bartender staffing ratios at no extra labor charge except for small functions; contract leaves staffing entirely to Hotel discretion and charges labor/bartender fees on all functions regardless of size.

CD requires representation of no current renovation plans, 30-day notice with mitigation plan, and Group's right to terminate if interference; contract disclaims any representation, notice, or termination right regarding construction/renovation at all.

CD requires 10% commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized revenue including walked/miscoded rooms, paid within 30 days, non-cancelable, surviving brand change, plus 10% of cancellation damages; the contract contains no commission clause addressing ConferenceDirect at all.

CD requires a nondiscrimination commitment beyond bare legal minimum and a termination right if discriminatory legislation is adopted; contract expressly limits Hotel's obligation to legal minimum, disclaims any broader commitment, and denies Group any termination/reduction right for legislative changes.

CD requires honoring quoted AV/internet pricing with a discount on additions and prohibits conditioning discounts on using in-house AV; contract allows the Hotel to reprice AV/internet up to event time and explicitly conditions complimentary internet/discounts on exclusive use of in-house AV provider.

analysis.document_notes: This contract is heavily one-sided in the Hotel's favor across nearly every clause examined, with unusually consistent language disclaiming Group audit rights, mitigation duties, and remedies throughout (attrition, cancellation, resale, reporting). No commission clause for ConferenceDirect appears anywhere, and no future-rate-cap or facilities/services-reduction clause is present at all. Exhibit A function space is listed only on a tentative basis pending signature, and the room rental/AV/staffing terms elsewhere in the document effectively negate any benefit of that tentative allocation. Signature blocks are unsigned/undated in the copy provided.

findings.headline: Shortfall penalty stacks full shortfall plus 35% surcharge, not 35% of gap
findings.finding_text: CD's standard caps shortfall liability at 35% of the gap between actual and minimum F&B revenue. This contract requires Group to pay the full shortfall amount AND an additional 35% surcharge on top of that shortfall — effectively 135% of the gap rather than 35%. The clause is also silent on whether affiliate/exhibitor F&B spend counts toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group pays only 35% of the shortfall, not the full difference, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue counts toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the minimum, the Group shall pay the Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual food and beverage revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall, within thirty (30) days of the Hotel's invoice. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum. The Hotel shall calculate the shortfall based on its standard accounting records. Any dispute regarding the calculation must be raised in writing within fourteen (14) days of the invoice; absent a timely dispute, the calculation is deemed accepted.
findings.quoted_text: If the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the minimum, the Group shall pay the Hotel the shortfall amount within thirty (30) days of the Hotel's invoice. The Hotel shall calculate the shortfall based on its standard accounting records. Any dispute regarding the calculation must be raised in writing within fourteen (14) days of the invoice; absent a timely dispute, the calculation is deemed accepted. The shortfall rate shall apply to any shortfall amount, assessed at thirty-five percent (35%) in addition to the base shortfall.
findings.exposure_basis: If F&B revenue fell $40,000 short of a $40,000 minimum (i.e., zero actual F&B revenue), Group would owe $40,000 (full shortfall) plus $14,000 (35% surcharge) = $54,000, versus $14,000 under CD's 35%-of-gap standard — a difference of up to $40,000 depending on actual shortfall size.

findings.headline: Attrition threshold set at 75% instead of CD's 70%, and formula doesn't credit sold rooms properly
findings.finding_text: CD's standard triggers attrition liability only if pickup falls below 70% of the block, and calculates damages as the lesser of unsold hotel rooms that night or the shortfall between block and pickup. This contract triggers liability at a higher 75% threshold (worse for Group, since liability starts sooner) and calculates damages simply as unoccupied committed rooms x rate x 70%, without the 'lesser of' cap tied to the hotel's actual unsold inventory. It also lacks the rebooking credit-back for future ConferenceDirect client bookings and does not mention crediting excess F&B revenue against attrition damages.
findings.cd_standard: Liability triggers only below 70% of block; damages equal 70% of the single group rate applied only to the lesser of unsold hotel rooms or shortfall; damages paid should be credited back if a ConferenceDirect client rebooks the hotel.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group fail to occupy at least seventy percent (70%) of committed rooms, Group shall pay the Hotel liquidated damages equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of the room rate, applied to the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's committed rooms and actual pickup, for each night the threshold is not met. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's F&B minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of committed rooms, Group shall pay the Hotel liquidated damages equal to the room rate applicable to the unoccupied rooms, multiplied by seventy percent (70%), for each night the threshold is not met.
findings.exposure_basis: 90-room commitment x 4 nights = 360 room-nights; at 70% threshold, 108 room-nights of cushion vs 90 room-nights cushion at 75% threshold — the 5-point difference in threshold exposes Group to liability on an additional 18 room-nights x $199 x 70% = approximately $2,507.40 in incremental exposure per this event alone, not counting the cap/formula gap on 'lesser of unsold rooms' which could be materially larger.

findings.headline: No fallback relief if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling
findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause covers illegality/impossibility/impracticability, epidemics, and travel advisories, and sets the 20% attendee-cancellation threshold, but omits several qualifying causes CD requires (terrorism, government closures/emergency declarations, corporate/educational travel restrictions) and does not state that Group's right survives even where the condition was known at signing. It also lacks the fallback that if Group elects to hold a smaller meeting rather than cancel, Hotel will waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate offered to anyone else.
findings.cd_standard: Qualifying causes should explicitly include terrorism, disease/epidemics, government advisories/closures/emergency declarations, and travel restrictions; the right should survive even if known at signing; and if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling, Hotel should waive attrition/F&B/rental fees and offer its lowest rate.
findings.proposed_language: Force majeure events include, without limitation, acts of terrorism, government-imposed travel restrictions and official travel advisories that restrict or discourage travel to Portland, Oregon, epidemics and pandemics affecting public health or travel, full or partial government closures, declarations of national, state, or local emergency, corporate or educational institution travel restrictions, and conditions of public safety, health, or infrastructure that render it unsafe or imprudent for Group's attendees to travel to or gather at the Hotel or in Portland. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition at the time this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances at a reduced size, Hotel will waive any attrition, food and beverage minimum, and function space rental fees related to the reduced size, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events include, without limitation, government-imposed travel restrictions and official travel advisories that restrict or discourage travel to Portland, Oregon, epidemics and pandemics affecting public health or travel, and conditions of public safety, health, or infrastructure that render it unsafe or imprudent for Group's attendees to travel to or gather at the Hotel or in Portland.

findings.headline: No requirement for Group's written approval before post-signature add-on charges are posted
findings.finding_text: The clause requires pre-signature disclosure of mandatory fees and waives undisclosed charges, which meets part of CD's standard. However, it does not require the Hotel to obtain Group's written approval before providing additional services or posting new charges to the master account after signature, nor does it address waiving early check-in or checked-bag fees for attendees.
findings.cd_standard: Later add-ons need the group's written approval before they are provided or posted; attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group require additional services or equipment after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel charges no resort fee for the event. All fees required under this agreement, including room charges, food and beverage charges, gratuity, and service charge, are set forth in this agreement or in the pre-signature fee disclosure. Group shall not be billed for any charge outside this agreement except as expressly provided in writing.

findings.headline: Hotel consent still required for assignment, plus added 'same industry' condition
findings.finding_text: CD's standard allows Group to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent where the event is unchanged. This contract requires Hotel's consent for any assignment (even to a successor/affiliate), and adds a 'same industry' qualifier and joint-and-several liability requirement not contemplated by CD's position.
findings.cd_standard: Group may assign to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations and the event remains substantially unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld, and the Hotel shall respond to any assignment request within ten (10) business days of receiving written notice from Group.
findings.quoted_text: Group may assign this agreement to a successor or affiliated management entity provided that the assignee is in the same industry as Group, is capable of performing all obligations under the agreement, and assumes all of Group's liabilities and duties in writing.

findings.headline: Insurance obligation is detailed for Group but only vague for Hotel
findings.finding_text: Indemnification is properly mutual and limited to each party's own negligence, meeting that part of CD's standard. However, the insurance obligation is asymmetric: Group must carry specific, itemized general liability coverage ($1M/$2M) and name Hotel as additional insured, while Hotel commits only to vague 'adequate insurance coverage' with no defined limits or additional-insured reciprocity, undermining the mutuality CD requires.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on the group alone.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event, with Group maintaining a policy of general liability insurance covering bodily injury, property damage, and personal injury with minimum limits of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence and $2,000,000.00 in the aggregate, naming the Hotel as an additional insured, and Hotel maintaining commercial general liability insurance with comparable minimum limits naming Group as an additional insured. Each party shall provide the other with certificates of insurance evidencing the required coverage at least fourteen (14) days prior to the Event dates.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall maintain a policy of general liability insurance covering bodily injury, property damage, and personal injury with minimum limits of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence and $2,000,000.00 in the aggregate, naming the Hotel as an additional insured. The Hotel shall maintain adequate insurance coverage to protect its own operations and activities during the Event.

findings.headline: Termination-for-cause clause omits convention-center/overflow-hotel dependency trigger
findings.finding_text: The contract provides scattered no-liability termination rights across several clauses (epidemic/pandemic, brand/ownership change, labor dispute, facilities reduction, discriminatory legislation, construction interference), which cover most of CD's required list. However, it is entirely silent on a termination right where a convention center or overflow hotels the event depends on are not available, open, and fully operational for the event dates — one of the causes CD's standard requires.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should include, among other triggers, a convention center or overflow hotels the event relies on not being available.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments, if the convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends are not open, available, and fully operational over the Event dates.

findings.headline: Block review dates and adjustment percentage sit off CD's 24/12-month, 10%/20% standard
findings.finding_text: Reviews occur July 1 2026, October 1 2026, and February 1 2027 — roughly 11, 8, and 4 months before the June 2, 2027 arrival — rather than CD's benchmark of approximately 24 and 12 months out, and the block may be adjusted by up to 15% per review rather than CD's 10% per review / 20% cumulative cap. The contract is also silent on final pickup reports with supporting documentation within 10 days of departure and on crediting miscoded rooms booked at brand-associate or business rates.
findings.cd_standard: Room block reviewed at approximately 24 and 12 months out, adjustable by up to 10% per review (20% cumulative); final pickup report with documentation within 10 days of departure; miscoded rooms, including brand-associate/business rate rooms, credited to pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival. At Group's discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at each review and twenty percent (20%) cumulatively, at the group rate. Hotel will provide final room pickup reports with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system — including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates — will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: The parties acknowledge that the room block shall be subject to written review at the following dates: July 1, 2026, October 1, 2026, and February 1, 2027, and at each such review date the Group may increase or decrease the block by no more than fifteen percent (15%) of the then-current commitment.

findings.headline: Auxiliary aid costs are split between Group and Hotel rather than clearly divided by location
findings.finding_text: CD's standard divides responsibility for auxiliary aids clearly: Group funds aids needed in its function space, Hotel funds aids required in guest rooms and common areas. This contract instead says the cost of auxiliary aids requested by Group or attendees 'shall be divided between Group and the Hotel,' an undefined cost-sharing arrangement that could impose costs on Group beyond function space.
findings.cd_standard: Group is responsible for funding auxiliary aids in function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for funding auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Group shall notify the Hotel of any such requirements at least fourteen (14) days prior to the event, and the parties shall promptly coordinate procurement of auxiliary aids.
findings.quoted_text: The cost of any auxiliary aids or services requested by Group or its attendees, including but not limited to interpreters, transcription services, specialized audio equipment and accessible transportation, shall be divided between Group and the Hotel.

findings.headline: Storm-notice window is only 12 hours after a warning, and geographically implausible
findings.finding_text: The named storm clause requires Group to provide written notice within twelve (12) hours of the National Weather Service issuing a hurricane or tropical storm warning for the Portland, Oregon area — an unusually short window given Portland's inland Pacific Northwest location rarely subject to such warnings, which risks making the clause practically inoperable when needed. CD's standard imposes no such tight notice-of-warning trigger, only a 72-hour forecast window for cancellation.
findings.cd_standard: Either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice if a named storm is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date.
findings.proposed_language: If a named storm is forecast to directly impact the Portland, Oregon area within seventy-two (72) hours of the event start date, Group may cancel this agreement without liability for attrition or liquidated damages upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice to the Hotel's Director of Sales, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.
findings.quoted_text: Group must provide written notice of cancellation to the Hotel's Director of Sales within twelve (12) hours of the National Weather Service's issuance of a hurricane or tropical storm warning for the Portland area.

findings.headline: Cancellation right for labor disputes requires proof of 'material interference'
findings.finding_text: CD's standard allows Group to cancel with no liability whenever a strike, lockout, or expired union contract arises within 90 days of the event, regardless of whether the hotel can still technically perform. This contract adds a qualifier that the labor dispute must 'materially interfere with Group's ability to conduct its event,' which is a narrower, more fact-dependent trigger that could be disputed by the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: If a strike, lockout, or expired contract with union employees arises within 90 days of the event, the group should be able to cancel with no liability at all, regardless of whether the hotel can technically still perform.
findings.proposed_language: Should any strike, work stoppage, job action, picket line, or other labor dispute occur at the Hotel during the Event dates or during the ninety (90) days preceding the event, Group may cancel this agreement by providing written notice to Hotel within ninety (90) days of the occurrence of such labor dispute, with no liability, penalty, or obligation to pay any fees or charges associated with this agreement, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform. Any such cancellation shall entitle Group to the return of all deposits and advance payments within fifteen (15) business days.
findings.quoted_text: Group may cancel with no liability, penalty, or obligation to pay any fees or charges associated with this agreement if a labor dispute materially interferes with Group's ability to conduct its event or enjoy the services, amenities, and accommodations reserved.

findings.headline: Gratuity percentage is never stated, and service charge sits well above typical benchmark
findings.finding_text: CD's standard requires both the gratuity and service charge percentages to be confirmed in the contract. This agreement confirms only the service charge (22%, calculated on the F&B subtotal before tax) but never states what percentage constitutes 'gratuity,' leaving that figure open-ended even though it is described as fully distributed to staff. The 22% service charge is also well above CD's benchmark of 6% service charge alongside an 18% gratuity.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined, with both percentages confirmed in the contract.
findings.proposed_language: Eighteen percent (18%) of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the service staff who worked the event. A separate service charge of [X]%, plus applicable tax, calculated on the subtotal of food and beverage charges before tax, is retained by Hotel as its own revenue and is not distributed as a tip. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall pay a service charge of twenty-two percent (22%) calculated on the subtotal of food and beverage charges before tax.

findings.headline: Denied-credit prepayment percentage is left undefined, not staged as CD requires
findings.finding_text: If credit is not approved, the contract requires Group to prepay 'an amount equal to the stated percentage of anticipated charges, as calculated by Hotel,' leaving the actual percentage and payment timeline entirely to the Hotel's discretion. CD's standard requires a defined staged schedule (25% at 14 business days after denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before the event) or, at minimum, a fixed percentage, not an open-ended one set unilaterally by the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: If credit is denied, Group should pay on a staged deposit schedule (25% within 14 business days of denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before event), not an open-ended prepayment percentage.
findings.proposed_language: Where credit approval is not granted to Group, Group shall remit twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Where credit approval is not granted to Group, Group shall remit as prepayment an amount equal to the stated percentage of anticipated charges, as calculated by Hotel based on the room block, projected food and beverage revenue, and anticipated additional services.

findings.headline: Walked-guest credit is half CD's rate, and no do-not-walk list or advance notice protections
findings.finding_text: The relocation clause provides comparable/better accommodations, transportation, upgrade, and welcome amenity on return, and full pickup/commission credit, meeting several of CD's requirements. However, the per-night rebate is only $100 versus CD's $200 standard; the clause omits the Hotel's obligation to contact Group in advance of any walk, to walk Group's attendees only after transient guests and other groups, to honor a do-not-walk list of key attendees, to forward messages/mail, and to provide additional compensation if 10 or more guests or 10% of the peak-night block are walked. It also does not state that Group incurs no attrition liability for any night a guest is walked.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should contact Group in advance, walk Group's attendees last, honor a do-not-walk list, forward messages, credit $200 per relocated room-night, and pay additional compensation for walking 10+ guests or 10% of peak block; no attrition liability accrues for walked nights.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate any member of Group holding a confirmed reservation, Hotel will contact Group in advance, will not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked under any circumstances. The Hotel shall relocate the affected guest to a comparable or better hotel selected by the Hotel, all relocation expenses to be borne solely by the Hotel, and shall arrange and pay for round-trip transportation between the alternative accommodation and the venue of the Event, and shall forward the displaced guest's telephone messages, mail, and packages. Upon the guest's return, the Hotel shall place the guest in an upgraded room category at no additional charge and shall provide a welcome amenity. Each night a guest is relocated shall be fully credited toward Group's room pickup guarantee and remain commissionable, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is walked. The Hotel shall credit Group's master account $200.00 per night of relocation. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall credit Group's master account in the amount of $100.00 per night of relocation as compensation for the inconvenience and administrative burden imposed by the relocation.

findings.headline: Cutoff set at 35 days, exceeding CD's 21-day maximum, with no post-cutoff group rate protection
findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is 35 days prior to arrival, later than CD's maximum of 21 days, cutting off attendees' access to the block earlier relative to arrival than CD's standard allows for the group rate window. Additionally, after cutoff the Hotel has no obligation to hold inventory and may sell released rooms 'at its sole discretion at any rate,' rather than either holding rooms for Group on prepayment, refunding advance payments, or releasing rooms for resale only after consultation with Group to reduce attrition damages, and there is no guarantee attendees continue to get the group rate after cutoff as long as the Hotel is selling to the public.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival; after cutoff, attendees should still get the group rate as long as the hotel sells rooms to the public, and unassigned rooms should be held on prepayment, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms within the group block must be made on or before thirty-five (35) days prior to arrival. This cutoff date is firm and applies to all reservations made through the Hotel's group reservation desk or online portal.

findings.headline: No commitment to complimentary in-room AV basics (mic, podium, power, lighting, HVAC)
findings.finding_text: Function space assignments, square footage, ceiling height, and room rental waiver are all addressed, meeting most of CD's standard. However, the contract is silent on the Hotel providing, at no charge, a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC in each meeting room, and the rental waiver is conditioned on Group's 'compliance with all terms herein,' an added condition not contemplated by CD's standard that could allow Hotel to revoke the waiver for unrelated technical breaches.
findings.cd_standard: Each meeting room should come with a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge; the room rental waiver should not carry added conditions beyond the standard agreement terms.
findings.proposed_language: Meeting room rental charges are waived for Group in connection with the use of the assigned function spaces during the Event dates. This waiver applies only to the spaces listed in Exhibit A and only to standard rental fees; charges for setup, breakdown, or staffing remain the responsibility of Group unless separately waived in writing. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power (including existing power outlets), proper lighting, and HVAC.
findings.quoted_text: The waiver is conditioned on Group's execution of this Agreement and compliance with all terms herein.

findings.headline: 2% rate cap and market-decline protection apply only to a later rebooking, not clearly to the contracted event
findings.finding_text: CD's standard requires a 2% annual increase cap and market-decline protection to apply to the rates for the contracted event itself where final rates are not yet confirmed. This clause instead frames the 2% cap and 60-day notice/30-day decline provisions as applying only 'in the event Group books a room block with the Hotel in any calendar year following 2027' — i.e., to a future, separate booking — rather than protecting the currently contracted June 2027 group rate, which is already fixed at $199 in Section 1 and needs no such cap since it's already final. This creates ambiguity about whether the market-decline discount would ever apply to the current contracted rate before arrival.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, the contract should cap any increase at 2% per year, reduce the rate if market averages decline before arrival, and fix final rates in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival on June 2, 2027, the negotiated group rate for the Event shall be reduced by the same percentage as the market decline, as measured by the Hotel's standard market survey. Group shall have the right to request documentation of the market decline. For any future room block booked with the Hotel in a calendar year following 2027, the group room rate shall not increase by more than two percent (2%) per year over the rate in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The group room rate for the Event dates shall not increase by more than two percent (2%) per year in the event Group books a room block with the Hotel in any calendar year following 2027.

findings.headline: No confirmation-turnaround deadline, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund terms
findings.finding_text: Name change and 6pm-day-of-arrival cancellation terms meet CD's standard, but the contract is silent on sending reservation confirmations within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival), on reinstating no-shows for the following night at the same rate, on refunding individual deposits with 3 working days' notice, and on crediting any individual cancellation money the Hotel keeps against Group's attrition damages.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival); no-shows reinstated for the following night at the same rate; individual deposits refundable with 3 working days' notice; individual cancellation money credited against Group's attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.headline: Two conflicting damages schedules, and rebooking credit window shorter than CD's standard
findings.finding_text: The contract sets out two different cancellation damages schedules that conflict with each other: a narrative sliding scale (0% at 12+ months, 25% at 9-12 months, 50% at 6-9 months, 75% at 3-6 months, 100% under 3 months) and a separate table (None at 365+ days, 35% at 364-181 days, 52% at 180-91 days, 63% at 90-31 days, 70% at 30 days or fewer). These produce materially different damages at the same notice period (e.g., 9-12 months prior yields 25% under the narrative text but 35% under the table), creating ambiguity that could be resolved in the Hotel's favor. Additionally, the rebooking credit-back for a new event applies only if Group itself rebooks the same Hotel within 12 months, whereas CD's standard extends this credit to any ConferenceDirect client rebooking within 3 years.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a single, clearly disclosed sliding scale; damages paid should be credited back if a ConferenceDirect client rebooks the hotel within 3 years, not limited to the original group rebooking within 12 months.
findings.proposed_language: If Group cancels this Agreement, Group shall pay to Hotel cancellation damages calculated according to the following single sliding scale, based on the date notice of cancellation is received prior to the Event dates of June 2-5, 2027: 365 days or more prior to arrival — None; 364 through 181 days prior to arrival — 35%; 180 through 91 days prior to arrival — 52%; 90 through 31 days prior to arrival — 63%; 30 days or fewer prior to arrival — 70%; each percentage applied to Room Profit as defined below. Room profit is calculated as seventy (70) percent of the single net group rate applied to the room block less allowable attrition. Any revenue Hotel earns reselling cancelled rooms is credited against Group's damage obligation. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years of the cancellation, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid.
findings.quoted_text: If Group cancels this Agreement, Group shall pay to Hotel cancellation damages calculated as a percentage of lost room profit based on the date notice of cancellation is received prior to the Event dates of June 2-5, 2027. Damages are assessed on a sliding scale: if notice is given twelve (12) months or more before June 2, 2027, damages equal zero percent of lost room profit; if notice is given between nine (9) and twelve (12) months before June 2, 2027, damages equal twenty-five (25) percent of lost room profit; if notice is given between six (6) and nine (9) months before June 2, 2027, damages equal fifty (50) percent of lost room profit; if notice is given between three (3) and six (6) months before June 2, 2027, damages equal seventy-five (75) percent of lost room profit; if notice is given fewer than three (3) months before June 2, 2027, damages equal one hundred (100) percent of lost room profit.
findings.exposure_basis: The narrative scale and table scale diverge (e.g., 25% vs 35% at 9-12 months out, 100% vs 70% under 3 months), creating a swing that could be tens of thousands of dollars depending on which is enforced against a room block of 90 rooms x 4 nights x $199 x 70%; exact figure depends on which schedule controls and cannot be fixed without clarification.

findings.headline: Only one server ratio given, no plated/buffet distinction, and no fixed under-25 labor fee
findings.finding_text: CD's standard requires distinct staffing ratios for plated versus buffet service (1:25/1:20 for plated breakfast/lunch-dinner, 1:40/1:30 for buffet) and separate hosted vs. cash bar bartender ratios (1:75 hosted, 1:100 cash). This contract provides only a single blended server ratio (1:20) and a single bartender ratio (1:75) regardless of service style or bar type, and does not specify the $150 labor fee CD's fallback sets for under-25 functions, leaving that fee to be set unilaterally by the Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: One server per 25 guests at plated breakfasts and 20 at plated lunches/dinners, one per 40/30 for buffets; one bartender per 75 at hosted bars and 100 at cash bars; a defined labor fee (CD uses $150) for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: For all food and beverage functions held during the Group event, the Hotel shall maintain minimum staffing ratios as follows: one (1) server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one (1) server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner; one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars. No labor fees, service fees, or bartender charges shall be assessed to the Group for any food and beverage functions with twenty-five (25) or more attendees. Functions with fewer than twenty-five (25) attendees may incur a labor fee of $150.
findings.quoted_text: For all food and beverage functions held during the Group event, the Hotel shall maintain minimum staffing ratios as follows: one (1) server for every twenty (20) guests and one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests.

findings.headline: Commission clause silent on miscoded/walked rooms, rate escalation, survival, and cancellation-damages share
findings.finding_text: The contract establishes a base 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, including outside-block rooms, payable within 30 days regardless of master account payment status, meeting CD's core rate. However it is silent on: commission covering rooms identified through a room-block audit or miscoding, rooms credited from walked guests or no-show/cancellation fees, the commission being non-cancelable and non-transferable, an increase if the Hotel's or brand's standard commission rises before the event, survival of the commission terms through a change of management or brand, ConferenceDirect receiving 10% of any cancellation damages collected, and the acknowledgment that Group could not have negotiated better terms booking direct.
findings.cd_standard: Commission should apply to all actualized room revenue including audited miscoded rooms, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation-fee credited nights; be non-cancelable/non-transferable; rise if Hotel's standard commission rises; survive brand/management change; and Hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall be paid a commission equal to ten percent (10%) of all room revenue actualized during the event, including revenue from rooms booked outside the block, rooms credited to Group through a room block audit, walked rooms, and room nights credited from no-show or cancellation fees. This commission is non-cancelable and non-transferable, and commission on any additional rooms or amendments will be no less than ten percent (10%). Should the standard hotel or brand commission percentage increase before the Event, the higher percentage will apply; should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. The commission shall be calculated by the Hotel from its records of room charges, and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the event conclusion, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall be paid a commission equal to ten percent (10%) of all room revenue actualized during the event, including revenue from rooms booked outside the block. The commission shall be calculated by the Hotel from its records of room charges, and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the event conclusion.

clause_review.basis: CD wants shortfall billed at 35% of the gap; this contract bills the full shortfall PLUS an additional 35% penalty on top, and is silent on affiliate/exhibitor F&B counting toward minimum.
Group may use outside AV, decorating, security and transportation vendors of its choice at a $0.00 surcharge.

Threshold is 75% (should be 70%), damages already cumulative and use 95% credit and audit rights as required, but liability triggers at unoccupied rooms x rate x 70% rather than lesser of unsold rooms/shortfall, no rebooking credit-back to CD client, and dispute window (30 days) not clearly tied to formula; also no explicit F&B/attrition dollar-for-dollar cross-credit.

Covers illegality/impossibility/impracticability, epidemics, travel restrictions/advisories, and 20% attendee cancellation threshold, and refunds deposits in 30 days; but omits explicit terrorism/civil disturbance/strikes list items, doesn't state right survives even if condition was known at signing, and does not include the fallback obligation to waive attrition/F&B/rental fees and offer lowest rate if Group holds a smaller meeting instead.

Pre-signature written disclosure requirement and waiver of undisclosed fees are present, and no resort fee is charged; however contract is silent on requiring Group's written approval before post-signature add-on charges are posted, and silent on early check-in/checked-bag fee waivers.

1 comp room per 40 paid room nights, no forfeiture on shortfall, no-show/cancellation fees credited toward pickup and comp ratio; though internet-regardless-of-loyalty-status point is not addressed, comp room formula matches CD's core position.

CD wants assignment to successor/affiliated entity without hotel consent where event unchanged; this contract requires Hotel consent (even if not unreasonably withheld) and additional conditions like 'same industry' and joint/several liability of assignee not contemplated by CD standard.

Indemnification is mutual and limited to own negligence (meets); but insurance obligation is imposed heavily on Group (specific $1M/$2M limits, naming Hotel additional insured) while Hotel only commits to vague 'adequate insurance' - not a mutual, comparably defined obligation.

Only epidemic/pandemic cause is included (clause 10); missing labor dispute (though covered elsewhere as cancellation right, not exempted from damages schedule explicitly - actually separate clause 27 provides no-liability cancellation, so covered), missing brand/ownership change explicit no-liability tie-in (though clause 26 provides it separately), missing convention-center/overflow-hotel dependency and state/local discriminatory legislation as termination-for-cause triggers under this specific clause; though these appear scattered, clause 10 titled Termination for Cause only recognizes epidemic/pandemic, not the full list CD requires under one termination-for-cause umbrella - other termination rights exist but are separate clauses each with own scope, functionally covering most items except convention-center/overflow dependency which is entirely absent.

30 day notice of change and 30 day termination window with deemed acceptance if not exercised; refund provision not explicit in this clause but termination for cause generally refunds deposits per clause 10 pattern - actually clause 26 doesn't state refund timing explicitly, only clause 10/24/27 do so; check further
No deposit required; if damage occurs it's billed to master account, itemized within 30 days, and not offset against room charges/F&B minimums.

Review dates are July 1 2026, Oct 1 2026, Feb 1 2027 (~11, 8, 4 months out) rather than ~24/12 months; block adjustment is 15% per review rather than 10%/20% cumulative; weekly pickup reports present but no start date specified (should start 60 days before cutoff); final pickup report within 10 days of departure not clearly matching (report is due only after cutoff period, final reconciliation within 30 days, not final pickup w/in 10 days); no explicit miscoded-room audit crediting brand-associate/business rate rooms.

Hotel warrants ADA compliance and covers structural mods (meets that part), but auxiliary aids cost is to be 'divided between Group and Hotel' rather than Group funding function-space aids and Hotel funding guest room/common area aids as CD requires.
Governed by law and venue of Group's principal offices, no punitive damages, each party bears own attorney's fees.

Named storm clause exists with 72-hour forecast trigger, but requires Group to give notice within 12 hours of NWS hurricane/tropical storm warning issuance - a narrow, burdensome condition not contemplated by CD's simpler standard, and Portland OR is an unusual/inapplicable location for hurricane warnings, creating a practically unusable right; refund is 14 days (CD doesn't specify exact days here but general fallback uses no such tight notice requirement).
Hotel will not use attendee data for own marketing, will not sell/share with third parties, complies with privacy laws.

CBA expiration notice is required 12 months prior to expiration (meets 1-year advance requirement) but labor dispute notice/cancellation right requires the dispute to be within 90 days and 'materially interferes' - adding a materiality qualifier not in CD's standard, which allows cancellation regardless of hotel's ability to perform once trigger occurs.

Gratuity/service charge are separately itemized and gratuity fully distributed (meets that), but service charge is 22% (no specific CD threshold, but CD standard's benchmark is 6%; well above typical) - contract doesn't state gratuity percentage at all, leaving gratuity % undefined, and CD requires both percentages confirmed in contract.

Finance charge capped at 1%/month matches; payable upon invoice with 30-day dispute window meets; but if credit denied, prepayment is an undefined 'stated percentage' not the specific staged 25/25/50 schedule CD requires, and no fallback credit-extension-by-default language if Hotel fails to send/follow up on credit application.

Provides comparable/better hotel, transportation, upgrade, welcome amenity, and per-night credit ($100 vs CD's $200), full pickup/commission credit, but omits contacting Group in advance of walk, walking Group's guests only after transient/other groups, honoring a do-not-walk list, message-forwarding, and additional compensation for 10+ walked guests/10% of peak block; also does not state no attrition liability for walked nights.
Active resale efforts required, proceeds credited dollar-for-dollar, records available on request, damages due only after event dates with documentation of mitigation and unsold inventory.

Rate parity, retroactive adjustment, commission/pickup credit preserved, and 7-day before/after no-higher-rate rule are present; however no carve-out for qualified rates (government/airline/corporate) is stated, which could be read as broader than CD standard but is not itself a deviation reducing exposure - actually contract's version is stricter than CD's fallback (no carve-outs) so this does not fall short; reconsidered as meets.

Cutoff is 35 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's max of 21 days; also after cutoff hotel is under no obligation to hold inventory and may sell released rooms 'at its sole discretion at any rate' rather than the required post-cutoff group-rate/hold-or-release-after-consultation process.
Hotel wrongful cancellation triggers indemnification for direct, indirect, consequential damages including relocation costs and attorney's fees.

Function space named with sq footage/ceiling height in Exhibit A, room rental waived, no change without consent (meets most); but silent on hotel providing complimentary wired microphone, podium, power, lighting and HVAC in each meeting room, and rental waiver is conditioned on 'compliance with all terms herein' which is an added condition not in CD standard.

25% reduction threshold, offer of equal alternatives at Hotel expense, and cancellation right if no agreement reached, though CD's specific 30-day resolution window is replaced with a general process without a stated deadline for negotiation before cancellation is available - actually contract doesn't give 30-day window, just immediate right if no agreement is reached, which meets or exceeds CD's standard.

2% cap and rate confirmed 12 months out and market decline reduction all present; however 2% cap applies only 'if Group books ... in any calendar year following 2027' i.e. only for a future renewed booking, not clearly the current contracted rate itself, and doesn't specify that decline is measured against comparable-hotel market average versus Hotel's own published rate as alternative - minor gap, but rate cap timing/triggers otherwise largely meet; flagging the narrow scope as a gap since 'future rate' provisions appear to apply to rebooking rather than currently uncertain rates for this event.

Confirmation-within-4-days requirement is not stated at all; name changes at group rate until arrival, 6pm-day-of-arrival cancellation, individual deposit refund and no-show reinstatement partially covered but no-show reinstatement for following night not addressed, and individual deposit refund with 3 working days' notice and crediting cancellation money against Group's attrition is not addressed.

There are two conflicting cancellation schedules in the contract text (a percentage-based narrative schedule with 0/25/50/75/100% and a table with None/35/52/63/70%), an internal inconsistency; also rebooking credit-back applies only to a rebooking at the same Hotel within 12 months (CD wants 3 years) and is narrower than CD's 3-year ConferenceDirect-client standard, and doesn't specify rebooking credit applies broadly to any CD client, only to Group itself.

Server ratios present (1:20, no separate plated/buffet distinction, missing 1:25 for plated breakfast and 1:40/1:30 buffet ratios) and bartender ratio only states 1:75 without distinguishing hosted (1:75) vs cash bar (1:100); no labor fee amount stated for under-25 functions (CD's fallback specifies $150).

No current renovation representation, 30-day notice of future plans, termination right if interference, hotel needs Group consent before implementing construction affecting Group's space - matches or exceeds CD standard; new-build/reopening-specific provisions not applicable here since this is an existing operating hotel.

10% commission on all actualized room revenue including outside-block rooms, payable within 30 days regardless of master account payment status (meets many elements); however contract is silent on commission covering audited miscoded rooms, walked rooms, no-show/cancellation-fee-credited nights, non-cancelable/non-transferable status, rate increases if hotel's standard commission rises, survival through brand/management change, 10% of cancellation damages paid to CD, and the 'could not have negotiated better direct' acknowledgment.
Broad nondiscrimination covenant with termination right if state/city legislation permits discrimination, matching CD's standard categories and remedy.
Honors quoted AV/internet pricing, discount negotiated in good faith for additions, in-house AV not a condition for discounts, and 10 Mbps/1 Mbps minimum bandwidth guaranteed.

analysis.document_notes: The contract contains an internal inconsistency in the cancellation clause (Section 5): a narrative sliding-scale schedule (0/25/50/75/100% of lost room profit at 12mo/9-12mo/6-9mo/3-6mo/<3mo) is immediately followed by a table with different percentages (None/35%/52%/63%/70% at overlapping but not identical time bands). These two schedules do not reconcile and should be clarified with the property before signature. Otherwise the document is a complete, readable, single-hotel single-event agreement with no illegible sections.

findings.headline: Attrition measured nightly at 90% threshold, not cumulative 70%, with gross-rate penalty
findings.finding_text: The contract measures attrition night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, and sets the pickup threshold at 90% instead of CD's 70% floor — meaning liability attaches much sooner and more often. Unsold rooms are charged at 90% of the full nightly group rate rather than 70% of lost profit, a materially harsher damages formula. There is also no audit right beyond documentation review, no dollar-for-dollar F&B credit against attrition, and no rebooking credit if a CD client later rebooks the hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be cumulative across the block, triggered only below 70% pickup, with damages of 70% lost profit on the single net group rate, formula-based audit rights, and a rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block of 95 rooms. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of the $168.00 group rate (plus tax, if required by applicable law). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night, as already provided in this Agreement. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation. After receipt of this payment, Hotel will not seek additional damages from Group related to the room block commitment. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and the Group's block commitment is deemed satisfied only to the extent that occupied rooms meet or exceed ninety percent (90%) of the rooms reserved for each night of the Event. The Hotel shall calculate attrition by reference to the occupancy records maintained in the Hotel's standard reservation system, and the Group shall be notified in writing of any shortfall within thirty (30) days following the Event. Any rooms within the Group's block that remain unoccupied and were not released in accordance with this Agreement shall be charged at ninety percent (90%) of the nightly group rate, with such charges due within forty-five (45) days of the Event conclusion.
findings.exposure_basis: 95 rooms x 90% threshold means up to ~9.5 rooms/night could trigger liability vs 70% (28.5 rooms) under CD standard; at $168/night x 90% charge over 3 nights for the ~19-room gap between thresholds: 19 rooms x 3 nights x $151.20 ≈ $8,618, though actual exposure depends on pickup and could be higher given gross-rate (not lost-profit) billing basis.

findings.headline: Force majeure lacks attendee-cancellation trigger, full cause list, and reduced-meeting fee waivers
findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause covers illegality, impossibility, and commercial impracticability, and lists some pandemic/travel-restriction causes, but omits CD's required 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger (actual or reasonably anticipated), omits express references to terrorism, government closures/emergency declarations, and corporate/educational travel restrictions, and does not address what happens if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling (no waiver of attrition/F&B/rental fees or best-rate offer). The 5-business-day notice window is also far shorter than CD's standard of allowing notice at any time before the event.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should allow cancellation for a broad list of causes including terrorism, disease, government advisories/closures, and corporate/educational travel restrictions, triggered also by 20% or greater anticipated attendee cancellations, with no bar based on foreknowledge, and with fee waivers if Group holds a reduced-size meeting instead.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including, but not limited to, acts of God; war; curtailment or interruption of transportation facilities; strikes (except those involving Hotel's employees) or the imminent threat thereof; threats or acts of terrorism; disease or epidemic; a CDC advisory, or a State Department or other governmental or international agency travel advisory; full or partial government closure; declaration of a national, state, or local emergency; prohibition or limitation of travel by any government employees; corporate or educational institution travel restrictions; civil disturbance; or any other cause beyond the parties' control — in that party's reasonable judgment: (a) make it commercially impracticable for either party or its members to perform; (b) make it inadvisable, including from a health or safety standpoint, for either party or its members to perform; (c) cause twenty percent (20%) or more of Group's attendees to cancel their attendance; (d) cause Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel; (e) make it illegal for either party or its members to perform; or (f) make it impossible for either party or its members to perform. Notice of cancellation may be sent at any time before the Event, whether or not the circumstances remain in effect at the time of the Event. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition when this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances, Hotel will waive any fees related to a reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates. Upon termination for force majeure, all deposits paid by Group shall be refunded promptly in accordance with the timeline specified in this agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The party seeking to invoke force majeure must provide written notice within five (5) business days of the event or restriction, accompanied by reasonable evidence of its occurrence and material impact on performance.

findings.headline: No protection against early check-in or checked-bag fees, or unapproved post-signature add-ons
findings.finding_text: Disclosure and waiver-of-undisclosed-fees provisions are present and resort fees are waived. However, the contract does not address whether attendees will be charged early check-in or checked-bag fees, and does not require Group's written approval before Hotel posts charges for any additional services or equipment requested after signature.
findings.cd_standard: Attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees, and any post-signature add-on charges require Group's written approval before being provided or posted.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group require additional services or equipment after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel charges no resort fee to Group for rooms occupied during the event. All other mandatory fees and surcharges due from Group are limited to those disclosed in writing before this agreement is executed.

findings.headline: Complimentary room formula omits miscoded rooms, no-show credits, and internet access
findings.finding_text: The 1:40 complimentary room ratio and non-forfeiture provision match CD's standard, but the clause does not credit miscoded rooms found through an audit, does not count no-show or cancellation fees as one room night toward pickup, and does not guarantee complimentary in-room internet for attendees regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: All occupied rooms, including miscoded rooms and rooms credited via no-show/cancellation fees, should count toward pickup for complimentary room calculations, and attendees should receive complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit. Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup and used in calculating complimentary rooms and rebates. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) rooms the Hotel occupies during the event dates of October 19-21, 2027.

findings.headline: No right to assign the agreement to a successor management company
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision allowing Group to assign the agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, where the event is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

findings.headline: Insurance obligation runs only against Group, not mutually
findings.finding_text: Indemnification is properly mutual and limited to each party's own negligence. However, the insurance requirement applies only to Group; the Hotel is not required to carry or evidence its own liability insurance for its activities.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, rather than a requirement imposed on Group alone.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall procure and maintain general liability insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, with Hotel named as an additional insured. Such insurance shall be maintained throughout the term of this Agreement and for thirty (30) days thereafter. Group shall provide Hotel with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage prior to the Event. If Group fails to maintain required insurance, Hotel may, at its option and at Group's expense, procure such insurance on Group's behalf. Hotel shall likewise procure and maintain general liability insurance adequate to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall procure and maintain general liability insurance with limits of not less than $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, with Hotel named as an additional insured.

findings.headline: Termination for cause omits pandemic, labor, ownership-change, and other no-liability triggers
findings.finding_text: The contract provides termination for cause only on the basis of an uncured material breach. It does not extend no-liability termination rights to Group's own determination that a pandemic affects its ability to hold the meeting, a labor dispute affecting Hotel's workforce, a material change in Hotel's ownership/management/brand, interfering renovation, facility/service reductions, unavailability of a relied-upon convention center, or discriminatory state/local legislation.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should include force majeure, Group's own pandemic determination, labor disputes, ownership/brand changes, renovation interference, facility reductions, convention center unavailability, and discriminatory legislation — all without triggering cancellation damages.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) unavailability of any convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends; or (h) the adoption of state or local legislation that permits discrimination against attendees. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation set forth in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: When either party terminates this agreement for cause — due to material breach by the other party that remains uncured for ten (10) business days after written notice — the breaching party shall have no right to make a claim for damages, and the terminating party shall receive prompt refund of all deposits.

findings.headline: No notice or termination right if hotel changes brand, ownership, or goes bankrupt
findings.finding_text: The contract does not require Hotel to notify Group of a material change in ownership, management, or brand affiliation, or of bankruptcy/foreclosure, and does not give Group a termination right in that event.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel changes brand, management, or ownership, or files for bankruptcy/foreclosure, it should notify Group within 30 days, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of notice with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) days of the notice of termination.

findings.headline: No scheduled block reviews, pickup reporting, post-event report, or audit rights
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no 24/12-month written review of the block, no weekly pickup reporting, no final pickup report timeline, no post-event report requirement, and no no-cost room-block audit right comparing the hotel's guest list to Group's registration list.
findings.cd_standard: Room block should be reviewed at 24 and 12 months with adjustment rights, weekly pickup reports before cutoff, final pickup reports within 10 days, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right with miscoded rooms credited to pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival. At Group's sole discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at each review at the group rate. Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date, and final room pickup reports with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. Within thirty (30) days of departure, Hotel will provide a full post-event report, including rooms actualized, food and beverage revenue recap, outlet spend, audio-visual spend, internet bandwidth usage, and exhibitor fees and revenue. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a representative of Group or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.

findings.headline: No ADA compliance warranty or allocation of auxiliary-aid funding responsibility
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no warranty that Hotel's guest rooms, function space, and transportation comply with the ADA, no mutual ADA indemnification, and no division of responsibility for funding auxiliary aids in event space versus guest rooms/common areas.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should warrant ADA compliance of its facilities, with mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations, and a clear division of auxiliary-aid funding responsibility.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA. Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.

findings.headline: No separate named-storm cancellation provision for this coastal-region market
findings.finding_text: The property is located in San Antonio, Texas, within a hurricane-prone region, yet the contract has no named-storm clause distinct from general force majeure to address a storm forecast to affect the area without necessarily causing physical hotel damage.
findings.cd_standard: Coastal/hurricane-belt contracts should include a separate named-storm clause with its own notice period and cancellation window.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.

findings.headline: No restriction on hotel's use of rooming list or attendee data
findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision preventing Hotel from using rooming list or attendee data for its own marketing, or from disclosing it to third parties without Group's consent.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should be used only for fulfilling reservations, not for hotel marketing or third-party disclosure without consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.

findings.headline: No advance notice of union contract expirations or labor-dispute cancellation right
findings.finding_text: The contract has no requirement that Hotel disclose collective bargaining agreement expiration dates or notify Group of labor disputes, and no right for Group to cancel without liability if a strike, lockout, or expired union contract arises near the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and notice of labor disputes, and Group should be able to cancel with no liability if a labor dispute arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One (1) year in advance, or within thirty (30) days of signing this Agreement if that is later, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform. Any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.

findings.headline: No gratuity or service charge percentages disclosed anywhere in the agreement
findings.finding_text: The contract references food and beverage minimums and shortfall charges but nowhere states gratuity or service charge percentages, nor distinguishes gratuity (staff pay) from a service charge (hotel revenue), leaving Group exposed to undisclosed or ambiguous add-on charges on the F&B spend.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge percentages should be clearly and separately defined and confirmed in the contract, with gratuity fully distributed to staff and service charge disclosed as hotel revenue; neither added to room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: Eighteen percent (18%) of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any service charge of six percent (6%), plus applicable tax, is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement. Hotel will not add a gratuity or service charge to meeting room rental fees or to any rented equipment that also carries a labor fee.
