findings.headline: No default credit-extension protection and no defined deposit schedule for denied credit
findings.finding_text: The finance charge cap of 1% per month and 30-day dispute window match CD's standard, but finance charges compound monthly rather than accruing simply, there is no provision extending credit automatically if Hotel fails to send or follow up on a credit application, and the prepayment schedule for denied credit is left undefined ('as specified in the Hotel's proposal') rather than fixed at CD's 25%/25%/50% staged schedule.
findings.cd_standard: If credit is denied, Group should pay on a defined staged schedule (25% within 14 business days of denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before event); if hotel never sends/follows up on a credit application, credit should be extended automatically; finance charges should be capped, not compounding.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will review its own credit files and credit reporting services to confirm Group's credit. If Hotel fails to send Group a credit application, or fails to send a written reminder to complete it, Hotel will extend credit to Group. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event. In the event any balance remains unpaid after thirty (30) days from invoice date, the Hotel shall assess a finance charge of one percent (1%) per month, not compounding, on the unpaid, undisputed balance.
findings.quoted_text: If Group does not provide advance credit approval, Group shall remit prepayment equal to a stated percentage of the anticipated room and food and beverage charges, as specified in the Hotel's proposal to Group. Any remaining balance due shall be paid upon receipt of the final invoice. In the event any balance remains unpaid after thirty (30) days from invoice date, the Hotel shall assess a monthly finance charge of one percent (1%) on the unpaid balance, compounding monthly until paid in full.

findings.headline: No protections at all if attendees are walked to another hotel
findings.finding_text: The contract is entirely silent on what happens if Hotel cannot accommodate a confirmed Group reservation — no requirement to contact Group in advance, no do-not-walk list, no comparable accommodations/transportation/message-forwarding for displaced guests, no per-room rebate, no pickup/commission credit, and no protection from attrition liability for walked nights.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should contact Group before any walk, walk Group's guests only after others, honor a do-not-walk list, provide comparable accommodations and transportation for walked guests, credit Group a per-room-night rebate and pickup/commission credit, exempt Group from attrition liability for walked nights, and pay additional compensation for large-scale walks.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate any member of Group holding a confirmed reservation, Hotel will contact Group in advance, will not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked under any circumstances. For each displaced guest, Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable hotel as close as possible, at no charge to the guest, for each night the guest is displaced; (b) provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel; (c) forward the displaced guest's telephone messages, mail, and packages; and (d) when the guest returns, provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity. Hotel will credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable at the group rate, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages if any guest is walked on any night. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.

findings.headline: Hotel keeps all resale revenue with no credit against Group's cancellation damages
findings.finding_text: The contract expressly denies Group any benefit from Hotel's resale of cancelled rooms — Hotel retains all resale revenue with no credit against liquidated damages, and rebooking by Group does not reduce damages owed. This directly contradicts CD's mitigation-and-credit standard and increases Group's exposure to the full liquidated damages amount even if Hotel resells the rooms at full price.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have an affirmative duty to mitigate by reselling cancelled rooms/functions and crediting proceeds against damages owed, with damages not due until 30 days after the event and only upon evidence of mitigation efforts and unsold inventory.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel will document in writing its efforts to market the dates proactively through all group and transient channels. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold. If the Group subsequently rebooks rooms with the Hotel for a different date or event, such rebooking may reduce damages owed by Group for the cancelled Event as agreed between the parties.
findings.quoted_text: Any revenue the Hotel generates by reselling rooms within the cancelled portion of the Group's block shall be retained by the Hotel with no credit applied against the Group's liquidated damages obligation. If the Group subsequently rebooks rooms with the Hotel for a different date or event, such rebooking shall not reduce or eliminate any damages already owed by the Group for the cancelled Event.

findings.headline: No guarantee the group rate won't be undercut by lower public rates
findings.finding_text: The contract does not guarantee that Hotel will avoid selling rooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted $168 rate during the event dates, and provides no remedy (rate matching or pickup credit) if it does, nor parity with other groups' rates near the event dates.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should guarantee it won't sell rooms below Group's contracted rate (except qualified rates), with a rate-match or full block-credit remedy if it does, and rate parity with other groups within 7 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate of $168.00 during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees. Commission, pickup credit, and any concession based on pickup will not be affected by such adjustment. Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.

findings.headline: Post-cutoff group rate is only conditional on availability, not on public sales continuing
findings.finding_text: The 21-day cutoff satisfies CD's minimum, but the contract's post-cutoff rate protection is narrower than CD's standard: it offers the group rate only 'if rooms in the block remain available,' rather than continuing the group rate as long as Hotel is selling that room type to the general public. There is also no provision addressing whether unassigned rooms at cutoff are held on prepayment, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group.
findings.cd_standard: After cutoff, attendees should get the group rate for as long as the hotel is selling rooms to the public (same room type once block is sold out), and unassigned rooms should be held, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations submitted after the cutoff date will be accommodated at the group rate if rooms in the block remain available at the time of booking. The availability of rooms and the continued application of the group rate are not guaranteed after the cutoff date, and the guest accepts the risk that only standard rack rates may be offered.

findings.headline: No remedy specified if the hotel itself wrongfully cancels the agreement
findings.finding_text: The contract addresses termination for cause and force majeure but contains no provision obligating Hotel to pay Group's direct, indirect, and consequential damages (staff time, rate/airfare differentials, rental, attorney's fees, printing costs) if Hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe Group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.headline: No function space assignments, square footage, or complimentary meeting-room equipment specified
findings.finding_text: The contract addresses only the guest room block and rates; it names no specific function rooms, minimum square footage, or ceiling heights, includes no room-rental waiver, and does not commit Hotel to provide a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge in each meeting room.
findings.cd_standard: Function rooms should be named with minimum square footage and ceiling height, changeable only by mutual written consent, with room rental waived and basic AV/power/HVAC provided free in each room.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement in this Agreement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power (including existing power outlets), proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.headline: No protection if the hotel closes or reduces staffing of key facilities/services
findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision addressing what happens if Hotel closes or materially reduces a restaurant, spa, fitness facility, meeting space, or service staffing ratios, and gives Group no right to cancel or renegotiate in that event.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes/limits facilities by more than 25% or materially reduces service staffing, it should first offer equal alternatives at its own expense; absent resolution within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, or safety and security services in a material manner, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services, mutually agreeable and solely at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to Hotel, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.headline: No rate cap or market-decline protection for any future-year rate adjustments
findings.finding_text: While the room rate here is already fixed for the 2027 event, the contract does not include any provision capping future rate increases at 2% or reducing the group rate if market rates decline, nor a commitment to finalize rates 12 months out, leaving Group without protection in the event rates were later renegotiated or if this were a multi-year agreement.
findings.cd_standard: Where future-year rates are unconfirmed, increases should be capped at 2% annually, group rate should decrease with market rate declines, and rates should be fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Definite room rates will be confirmed in writing no later than twelve (12) months prior to arrival. Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over the rates quoted in this Agreement. Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.headline: No attendee-favorable reservation confirmation, name-change, or cancellation procedures
findings.finding_text: The contract has no provisions on confirmation timing for individual reservations, name changes at the group rate, individual room cancellation deadlines without charge, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days), name changes allowed at group rate up to arrival, cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement for the following night, and individual deposit refunds with 3 working days' notice.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.headline: Damages based on gross room revenue, not lost profit, with no resale credit or rebooking credit
findings.finding_text: The sliding scale with disclosed percentages is present, but damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than CD's 70%-lost-profit formula, meaning Group pays for revenue the Hotel never would have had to cover its own costs to generate. The clause also expressly denies Group any credit for resold rooms and provides no rebooking credit if a CD client later books the hotel, both contrary to CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be based on 70% of lost room profit (not gross revenue) applied to the block less allowable attrition, with mandatory resale mitigation credited against damages and a rebooking credit for future CD client bookings.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit on a sliding scale based on the date written notice of cancellation is received, using the percentages stated in this Agreement. One hundred percent (100%) of room profit is defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $168.00 at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: If the Group cancels this Agreement or reduces the room block in writing before the Event, the Group shall owe liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled or reduced rooms, based on the nightly group rates in effect at the time of cancellation.
findings.exposure_basis: At the 30-days-or-fewer tier (70%), 95 rooms x $168 gross = $15,960 in potential gross-revenue-based damages if the full block cancels late, versus a materially lower figure under a 70%-lost-profit formula.

findings.headline: No minimum staffing ratios guaranteed for meal functions or bars
findings.finding_text: The contract sets an F&B minimum but includes no guaranteed server-to-guest or bartender-to-guest ratios for plated or buffet meals and hosted or cash bars, and no cap on labor fees for small functions.
findings.cd_standard: Minimum staffing ratios should be guaranteed for servers and bartenders at various function types, with no extra labor charge for meeting those ratios except for very small functions.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.

findings.headline: No representation about renovations or termination right if construction interferes
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no representation that Hotel has no current renovation plans affecting Group's space, no notice obligation for later-confirmed renovation work, and no termination right for Group if construction interferes with its event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans affecting Group's space, commit to 30 days' notice of any confirmed later renovation with mitigation plan, and let Group terminate without liability if it determines the work will interfere.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the planned scope, schedule, anticipated impact on areas Group will use, and Hotel's plan for minimizing that impact. If Group determines the construction or remodeling will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.

findings.headline: No commission obligation to ConferenceDirect anywhere in the agreement
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commission clause obligating Hotel to pay ConferenceDirect the standard 10% commission on actualized room revenue, nor any provision addressing timing, non-cancelability, or commission on cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable and non-transferable, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment or termination right for discriminatory legislation
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commitment from Hotel that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds, and no termination right for Group if the state or city adopts legislation permitting such discrimination.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should commit to nondiscrimination against attendees on a broad list of protected grounds, with a termination right if local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city in which Hotel is located adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, or prohibits the adoption of nondiscrimination measures on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.headline: No AV or internet bandwidth quote, discount, or anti-tying protection included
findings.finding_text: The contract has no attached audio-visual or internet bandwidth quote, no discount commitment on additional AV/internet needs, and no assurance that use of an in-house AV provider is not a condition for discounted or complimentary internet.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should honor attached AV and internet bandwidth quotes (minimum 10 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up), with a discount on additions, and never condition discounted/complimentary services on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

clause_review.basis: Menu pricing locked for 12 months, shortfall billed at 35% of the difference, matching CD's position; though it does not mention affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting toward the minimum.
Group may use its own AV, decorating, security and transportation vendors at no surcharge, matching CD's position.

CD requires cumulative measurement, 70% threshold, 70% lost-profit damages, audit rights, and rebooking credit; contract measures night-by-night, sets threshold at 90%, charges 90% of nightly rate (not 70% lost profit), and has no rebooking credit.

CD requires a broad list of qualifying causes (terrorism, disease, govt advisories/closures, corporate/educational restrictions), a 20% attendee cancellation trigger, no bar from foreknowledge, and a reduced-meeting fallback with fee waivers; contract's notice window of 5 business days before the event is unusually short and doesn't match CD's more flexible "any time before the Event" notice standard, and omits the reduced-attendance/20% cancellation trigger and fee-waiver fallback, and does not explicitly list terrorism or government closures/corporate travel restrictions.

Written pre-signature disclosure and waiver of undisclosed fees are present and resort fee is waived; but contract is silent on early check-in/checked-bag fee waivers for attendees and on requiring written approval before post-signature add-on charges are posted.

Complimentary room ratio of 1:40 matches, and non-forfeiture is stated; but contract doesn't address miscoded rooms, no-show/cancellation fee credits toward pickup, or complimentary internet regardless of loyalty status.
No assignment/subcontracting clause exists anywhere in the contract.
Indemnification is mutual and limited to each party's own negligence, matching CD's position; however, insurance is required only from Group, not mutually from both parties as CD's standard requires.

Termination for cause is present and separate from cancellation scale, but CD requires a broader list of no-liability termination triggers (epidemic/pandemic determination, labor dispute, ownership/brand change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) which are entirely absent here.
No clause addressing hotel brand, management, or ownership change, or bankruptcy/foreclosure notice and termination rights.
Deposit is $0, refundable within 30 days, limited to documented damage, not applied to attrition or F&B minimums, matching CD's position.
No 24/12-month block review, no weekly pickup reports, no post-event report requirement, and no room-block audit right comparing guest lists are included.
No ADA warranty, indemnification allocation, or auxiliary aid funding division appears anywhere in the contract.
Governing law and venue are Group's home jurisdiction, no punitive damages, each party bears own attorney's fees — matches CD's position.
No separate named-storm clause exists despite the property being in a Gulf Coast hurricane-prone market (San Antonio, Texas).
No provision restricting Hotel's use of rooming list/attendee data for its own marketing or third-party disclosure.
No clause requiring advance notice of CBA expirations, notice of labor disputes, or a no-liability cancellation right for labor disputes within 90 days of the event.
No gratuity or service charge percentages or definitions appear anywhere in the contract.

Finance charge is capped at 1% per month, matching CD's cap, and dispute window is 30 days; but the contract provides no fallback credit-extension-by-default provision, and the credit-denial deposit schedule is left to be 'as specified in the Hotel's proposal' rather than the defined 25/25/50 staged schedule CD requires, and finance charges compound monthly rather than being simple interest.
No walk/relocation clause covering advance contact, comparable accommodations, transportation, rebate, pickup credit, or additional compensation for mass walks.

Contract explicitly states resold room revenue is retained by Hotel with no credit against Group's damages, and rebooking does not reduce damages owed — directly contrary to CD's mitigation-and-credit requirement; also no 30-day-after-event delay condition tied to mitigation evidence.
No provision guaranteeing Hotel won't sell rooms below Group's rate, no retroactive adjustment or pickup-credit remedy, and no parity with other groups' rates within 7 days of the event.

Cutoff is 21 days (meets minimum), but post-cutoff rate protection is only 'if rooms remain available' rather than CD's standard of continued group rate as long as Hotel sells to the public of that room type; also no provision on holding/refunding/releasing unassigned rooms after consultation.
No provision addressing Hotel's own wrongful cancellation and consequential damages owed to Group.
No naming of function rooms, square footage, ceiling heights, room rental waiver, or complimentary in-room AV/podium/power/lighting/HVAC provisions appear in the contract.
No provision addressing closures or staffing reductions of hotel facilities/services and Group's termination or renegotiation rights.
No future-year rate cap, market-decline discount, or rate-finalization deadline provision appears; the rates here are already fixed at signing, but no clause addresses this contingency at all.
No provisions on confirmation timing, name changes, individual cancellation deadlines, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing appear in the contract.

Sliding scale with disclosed percentages exists, but damages are based on gross room revenue rather than 70% lost-profit room-profit formula, resale revenue is expressly not credited against damages, and no rebooking credit exists.
No staffing ratios for servers or bartenders, and no labor-fee threshold for small functions appear in the contract.
No representation regarding current or future renovation plans, notice requirements, or termination rights for interference appear in the contract.
No commission clause to ConferenceDirect appears anywhere in the contract.
No nondiscrimination commitment or termination right tied to discriminatory state/local legislation appears in the contract.
No audio-visual or internet bandwidth quote, discount on additions, or prohibition on tying discounts to in-house AV use appears in the contract.

analysis.document_notes: This is a relatively short, single-property group sales agreement lacking many clause types that typically appear in a full CD-negotiated hotel contract (e.g., function space specifics, AV/internet, banquet staffing, commission, ADA, nondiscrimination, walk/relocation, labor disputes, brand/ownership change, named storm, construction, review/audit dates, reservation procedures, rate parity, and hotel-cancellation remedies). No dollar figures are given for prepayment percentage on credit denial, so that gap could not be quantified. The document appears complete and legible; no illegible pages or structural anomalies were observed.

findings.headline: Menu pricing locked too far out and shortfall penalty too high
findings.finding_text: The contract locks menu pricing 14 months before the event, exceeding CD's 12-month ceiling, and charges a 40% shortfall penalty rather than CD's 35% benchmark. It is also silent on whether affiliate organization or exhibitor F&B revenue counts toward the minimum, and gives Hotel unilateral discretion to waive or negotiate the shortfall rather than a fixed formula.
findings.cd_standard: Menu pricing should be locked no earlier than 12 months before the event, with any shortfall billed at 35% of the gap, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked as of that date. If actual Food and Beverage expenditures fall short of the Minimum Commitment, Group shall pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual charges and the Minimum, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's Event will count toward the Minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal at least fourteen (14) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked and shall not be subject to increase or modification after that date. Should Group's actual Food and Beverage expenditures fall short of the Minimum Commitment as calculated from the Hotel's catering records, Group shall be invoiced for the difference between the actual charges and the Minimum Commitment as a shortfall charge on the final bill.

findings.headline: Outside vendor privilege still structured as a chargeable surcharge
findings.finding_text: While Group may use outside vendors, the contract imposes a formal 'outside vendor surcharge' clause (currently set at $0.00) rather than eliminating the fee category entirely. Structuring vendor access as a waivable surcharge leaves Group exposed to a fee being reinstated or negotiated upward in future dealings and does not match CD's position that no additional fee applies to outside vendor use.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors of its choice for AV, decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Notwithstanding the Group's right to engage outside vendors, no outside vendor surcharge or additional service fee shall be assessed against Group for the use of independently selected vendors, including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, or tours.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the Group's right to engage outside vendors, the Group shall remit to the Hotel an outside vendor surcharge in the amount of "$0.00". This surcharge shall be payable in full upon execution of this Agreement and represents the Hotel's sole additional compensation for the privilege of hosting outside vendors on the Hotel's premises during the Event.

findings.headline: Attrition threshold and damage rate both worse than CD's standard
findings.finding_text: CD's position triggers attrition liability only below 70% pickup and caps damages at 70% of the group's net rate. This contract triggers liability at a higher 75% threshold (meaning liability attaches sooner) and calculates damages at 75% of the average daily rate (higher than CD's 70% benchmark). The clause is also silent on crediting excess F&B revenue against attrition damages and does not include the rebooking credit that the cancellation clause separately provides.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should trigger only below 70% pickup, with damages of 70% of the group's single net rate, an F&B-to-attrition dollar-for-dollar credit, and a rebooking credit if a CD client rebooks within 3 years.
findings.proposed_language: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy percent (70%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause. The attrition liability rate shall be seventy percent (70%) of the average daily room rate applicable to the block, multiplied by the number of unoccupied room nights representing the shortfall below the threshold. Any excess food and beverage revenue above Group's Food and Beverage Minimum will be credited dollar for dollar against room attrition damages, and vice versa. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause. Attrition is measured on a cumulative basis across the entire room block, and Hotel shall calculate the shortfall by comparing actual room nights occupied to the total room nights in the block across all dates of the Event. The attrition liability rate shall be seventy-five percent (75%) of the average daily room rate applicable to the block, multiplied by the number of unoccupied room nights representing the shortfall below the threshold.

findings.headline: No 20% attendee-cancellation trigger or smaller-meeting fee waivers
findings.finding_text: The force majeure clause covers a broad range of qualifying causes including epidemics and travel restrictions, but it never states that a 20% (or anticipated 20%) attendee cancellation rate independently triggers force majeure rights, and it does not address what happens if Group elects to hold a smaller meeting rather than cancel entirely — CD requires the Hotel to waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer its lowest rate in that scenario. It also does not clarify that Group retains this right even for conditions known at signing.
findings.cd_standard: Either party may cancel without liability if a qualifying cause would cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate 20%+ attendee cancellations; the right applies regardless of conditions known at signing; if Group holds a reduced-size meeting instead, Hotel waives attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offers its lowest available rate.
findings.proposed_language: Force majeure events under this clause shall also include any circumstance that causes, or leads Group to reasonably anticipate, that twenty percent (20%) or more of Group's attendees will cancel their attendance. Group's right to invoke this clause is not limited by either party's awareness of the condition at the time this Agreement was signed. If Group elects to hold a reduced-size Event despite such circumstances, Hotel will waive any attrition, food and beverage minimum, and function space rental fees associated with the reduced-size Event, and will offer Group's attendees the lowest room rate offered to any other guest over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Epidemics and pandemics, whether declared by the World Health Organization, United States government agencies, or state or local public health authorities, shall constitute force majeure events under this Agreement. The occurrence of any epidemic or pandemic that materially impacts the ability of Group members to gather safely or to travel to the Hotel shall relieve the affected party of its obligations hereunder.

findings.headline: No written-approval requirement for post-signature add-on charges, and no fee waivers for early check-in/checked bags
findings.finding_text: The disclosure and waiver-of-undisclosed-fees provisions are strong, and resort fees are waived, but the clause never requires Hotel to obtain Group's written approval before providing additional services or posting new charges after signature, and it is silent on waiving early check-in fees or checked-bag fees for attendees.
findings.cd_standard: Later add-on charges need Group's written approval before being provided or posted; attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group require additional services or equipment after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.

findings.headline: Complimentary room ratio worse than standard and no credit for miscoded or no-show room nights
findings.finding_text: CD's benchmark ratio is 1 complimentary room per 40 occupied room nights; this contract uses a 1-per-45 ratio, which yields fewer complimentary rooms to Group at the same pickup level. It is also silent on crediting miscoded rooms or no-show/cancellation-fee room nights toward the complimentary room calculation, and silent on complimentary in-room internet.
findings.cd_standard: One complimentary room per 40 occupied room nights, counting miscoded rooms and no-show/cancellation-fee nights, plus complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: The complimentary room ratio is forty (40), meaning that for every forty (40) paid room nights generated by Group, the Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room night at no charge to Group. All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup for this purpose, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit, and each no-show fee and cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup and used in calculating complimentary rooms. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio is forty-five (45), meaning that for every forty-five (45) paid room nights generated by Group, the Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room night at no charge to Group.

findings.headline: Insurance obligation runs only against Group, not mutual
findings.finding_text: Indemnification is appropriately mutual and limited to each party's own negligence. However, the insurance requirement is imposed solely on Group ($2,500,000 CGL naming Hotel as additional insured), with no corresponding obligation for Hotel to carry insurance protecting its own activities.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities.
findings.proposed_language: The Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of $2,500,000.00 per occurrence, covering bodily injury, property damage, and contractual liability arising out of the Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel's premises, and shall provide the Hotel with a certificate of insurance evidencing such coverage at least thirty (30) days prior to the Event, naming the Hotel as an additional insured. The Hotel shall likewise obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance adequate to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event, and shall provide Group with a certificate of insurance upon request.
findings.quoted_text: The Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of "$2,500,000.00" per occurrence, covering bodily injury, property damage, and contractual liability arising out of the Group's occupancy and use of the Hotel's premises. The Group shall provide the Hotel with a certificate of insurance evidencing such coverage at least thirty (30) days prior to the Event, naming the Hotel as an additional insured, and shall ensure that such insurance remains in effect throughout the Event and for any period during which claims might arise from the Event.

findings.headline: No unified walk-away right covering convention-center or overflow-hotel unavailability
findings.finding_text: Group's termination rights are scattered across the labor, brand-change, construction, and facilities clauses and generally do not trigger cancellation damages, which aligns with CD's separation requirement. However, none of the clauses address the scenario where a convention center or overflow hotels the event depends on are not open, available, and fully operational for the event dates — a cause CD's standard specifically requires as a termination trigger.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability if the convention center or overflow hotels the event relies on are not open, available, and fully operational over the event dates, without triggering cancellation damages.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, if the convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends are not open, available, and fully operational over the Event dates. None of the causes in this clause, including this one, triggers the cancellation damages set forth in the cancellation clause of this Agreement.

findings.headline: Hotel notice window too long and Group's termination window too short
findings.finding_text: CD requires Hotel to notify Group within 30 days of a brand/ownership/management change and gives Group 30 days from that notice to terminate. This contract allows Hotel up to 35 days to notify and gives Group only 25 days to elect termination, both less favorable to Group than CD's benchmark.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a brand, management, or ownership change, and Group should have 30 days from that notice to terminate without liability, with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall notify the Group in writing of any change in the Hotel's brand affiliation, management company, or ownership within thirty (30) days following execution of this Agreement or, if such change occurs after that period, within thirty (30) days of such change becoming effective. Upon receipt of notice of a change in brand, management, or ownership, the Group shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without penalty or liability within thirty (30) days of such notice.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall notify the Group in writing of any change in the Hotel's brand affiliation, management company, or ownership within thirty-five (35) days following execution of this Agreement or, if such change occurs after that period, as promptly as commercially practicable and in no event later than the date any such change becomes effective. For purposes of this clause, a change in brand, management, or ownership includes any transaction in which a new entity assumes operational control, brand affiliation, or title to the Hotel property.

findings.headline: No 24/12-month block review, pickup reports start too late, and audit is not free
findings.finding_text: The contract does not provide a written room-block review at 24 and 12 months with Group's right to adjust the block, weekly pickup reports begin only 8 weeks (56 days) before the event rather than a longer lead time, the post-event report omits AV spend, internet bandwidth usage, and exhibitor fee/revenue detail, and Group's audit right is at its own expense rather than free, with no explicit credit for miscoded rooms at brand-associate/business rates.
findings.cd_standard: Room block reviewed in writing at 24 and 12 months with adjustment rights; weekly pickup reports starting well before cutoff; full post-event report including AV, bandwidth, exhibitor spend within 30 days; a no-cost audit right with miscoded-room credit regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival, and Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at each review at the group rate. Beginning sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date, the Hotel shall provide Group with a written weekly pickup report. Within thirty (30) days following the conclusion of the Event, the Hotel shall deliver to Group a comprehensive post-event report detailing final room pickup, actual revenue generated, audio-visual spend, internet bandwidth usage, exhibitor fees and revenue, and all charges assessed against Group's folio. Group shall have the right, at no cost to Group, to engage an independent auditor, or to have a ConferenceDirect or Group representative, to audit the room block records, billing records, and attendance records maintained by the Hotel, and any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system, including rooms booked at brand-associate or business rates, will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: Beginning eight (8) weeks prior to the Event and continuing weekly through the cutoff date established in this Agreement, the Hotel shall provide Group with a written pickup report setting forth the number of rooms booked under the room block, the number of rooms released, the number of rooms picked up by attendees, the rate breakdown by room type, and any changes to rooming arrangements or billing status.

findings.headline: Auxiliary aid cost split negotiated rather than divided by CD's clear function-space/guest-room line
findings.finding_text: The clause warrants ADA compliance and provides mutual proportionate indemnification, but instead of clearly assigning function-space auxiliary aid costs to Group and guest room/common area aid costs to Hotel, it requires open-ended negotiation of cost allocation for each aid, creating uncertainty and potential exposure for Group.
findings.cd_standard: Group funds auxiliary aids needed in event/function space; Hotel funds auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. The Group shall provide the Hotel with written notice of any required auxiliary aids no later than sixty (60) days prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: In the event that the Group requires auxiliary aids or services to ensure the accessibility and full participation of Group members or attendees with disabilities, including but not limited to interpreters, assistive listening devices, materials in alternative formats, and mobility assistance, the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be divided between the Group and the Hotel. The Group shall provide the Hotel with written notice of any required auxiliary aids no later than sixty (60) days prior to the Event, and the parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of costs for each specific auxiliary aid, with the Hotel bearing its proportionate share of expenses reasonably attributable to the Hotel's facilities or obligations under the Americans with Disabilities Act.

findings.headline: CBA expiration notice shorter than a year and cancellation window not tied to 90 days pre-event
findings.finding_text: CD requires a full year's advance notice of collective bargaining agreement expirations and a cancellation right if a labor dispute arises within 90 days of the event. This contract provides only 9 months' advance notice of CBA expirations and gives Group a 75-day window after becoming aware of a dispute to cancel, rather than tying the cancellation right to disputes arising within 90 days before or during the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel gives one year's advance notice of CBA expiration dates; if a strike, lockout, or expired contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group may cancel with no liability.
findings.proposed_language: One (1) year in advance, or within thirty (30) days of signing this Agreement if that is later, the Hotel shall provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than nine (9) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement. Such notice shall include the expiration date, the union or labor organization involved, and a brief description of any material issues known to the Hotel that may give rise to labor dispute or work stoppage.

findings.headline: Service charge rate far above typical benchmark and no protection against charges on rental/equipment
findings.finding_text: Gratuity is properly separated and fully distributed to staff, but the service charge is set at 22% of F&B subtotal, well above CD's 6% reference figure, and the clause does not state that neither gratuity nor service charge will be added to meeting room rental or to rented equipment that already carries a labor fee.
findings.cd_standard: Service charge should be clearly disclosed as separate from gratuity and confirmed in the contract; neither should be added to meeting room rental or equipment already carrying a labor fee.
findings.proposed_language: The service charge, calculated as [X]% of the subtotal of food and beverage charges before tax, constitutes the Hotel's own revenue and compensation for administrative services, overhead, and operational costs associated with the Event. The service charge is not a gratuity, tip, or compensation to service staff, and Group acknowledges that the Hotel retains the entire service charge amount for its own account. Hotel will not add a gratuity or service charge to meeting room rental fees or to any rented equipment that also carries a labor fee.
findings.quoted_text: The service charge, calculated as twenty-two percent (22%) of the subtotal of food and beverage charges before tax, constitutes the Hotel's own revenue and compensation for administrative services, overhead, and operational costs associated with the Event. The service charge is not a gratuity, tip, or compensation to service staff, and Group acknowledges that the Hotel retains the entire service charge amount for its own account.

findings.headline: Finance charge exceeds cap, dispute window too short, and no-credit prepayment is a lump sum
findings.finding_text: The finance charge is set at 1.3% per month, exceeding CD's 1% cap; the invoice dispute window is only 12 days rather than the 30 days CD requires before finance charges accrue on disputed amounts; and where credit is not approved, Group must prepay 75% of estimated charges as a lump sum rather than the staged 25%/25%/50% schedule CD calls for. The contract is also silent on extending credit automatically if Hotel fails to send or follow up on a credit application.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge capped at 1% per month or legal max, whichever is less; 30-day dispute window before finance charges accrue; if credit denied, staged prepayment of 25% within 14 business days of denial, 25% one month out, 50% three days before event; automatic credit if Hotel fails to send/follow up on a credit application.
findings.proposed_language: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date. Any invoice dispute must be submitted in writing to The Monarch's Accounting Department within thirty (30) days of invoice receipt before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. Where the Group has not received credit approval from The Monarch prior to execution of this Agreement, the Group shall pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event. If The Monarch fails to send Group a credit application, or fails to send a written reminder to complete it, The Monarch will extend credit to Group.
findings.quoted_text: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge of 1.3% on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date. This finance charge shall accrue monthly on the outstanding balance until paid in full and shall be in addition to all other remedies available to The Monarch under this Agreement or applicable law. The Group waives any defense based on the rate or application of such finance charge and acknowledges that this charge represents a reasonable pre-estimate of harm.

findings.headline: No per-night master account rebate, attrition exemption, or bulk-walk compensation
findings.finding_text: The relocation clause covers comparable accommodations, transportation, messages (implicitly through concierge coordination is not explicit for messages), upgrade, and pickup credit — but it does not credit Group's master account a per-room-night rebate for each walked guest, does not state that Group is exempt from attrition liability for any night a guest is walked, and includes no additional compensation trigger if 10 or more guests or 10%+ of the peak-night block is walked.
findings.cd_standard: Group should receive a per-room-night rebate to its master account for each walked guest, no attrition liability for any night a guest is walked, and additional compensation if the hotel walks 10+ guests or 10%+ of the peak-night block.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated, regardless of that guest's rate. Group shall not be liable for attrition damages for any night on which a guest is relocated under this clause. If Hotel relocates ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: Any night spent at the alternative accommodation shall be credited to Group's room pickup and shall count toward all occupancy and pickup thresholds stated in this Agreement, and shall be credited to all commissions or rebates calculated on the basis of room pickup, occupancy, or other similar metrics. In all other respects, Group shall not be entitled to credit, rebate, or reduction of charges for the relocated night, and all food and beverage minimums, event space charges, and other Hotel obligations shall be calculated without reduction.

findings.headline: Damages timing tied to cancellation notice, not 30 days after event dates
findings.finding_text: The resale/mitigation obligations are otherwise strong, but the cancellation clause (clause 4) requires Hotel to calculate and demand final damages within 30 days of receiving Group's cancellation notice, which can occur long before the event dates. CD's standard requires that cancellation damages not fall due until 30 days after the meeting dates, once mitigation efforts and unsold inventory are demonstrated.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should not fall due until 30 days after the meeting dates, and only once Hotel demonstrates mitigation effort and that rooms/space went unsold.
findings.proposed_language: Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the Event's original meeting dates of November 9-12, 2027, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its resale and mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall calculate the final damages due within thirty (30) days of receiving Group's cancellation notice and shall provide Group with a written accounting that itemizes the damages calculation, resale credits applied, and any remaining amount due.

findings.headline: No 7-day surrounding-dates protection and no carve-out for qualified rates
findings.finding_text: The parity clause is strong on retroactive adjustment and protecting commission/pickup credit, but it omits the requirement that Group's rate be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days before or after the block dates, and it fails to exempt legitimate qualified rates (government, airline, contracted corporate rates) from the parity comparison — an omission that could make routine discounted rate categories trigger a full retroactive rate cut for the Hotel, which the Hotel would likely resist honoring in practice, leaving ambiguity for Group.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel guarantees no lower rate during event dates except qualified rates (government, airline, contracted corporate), with retroactive adjustment, and guarantees Group's rate is no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days before/after the block dates.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel agrees that during the Event dates of November 9 through November 12, 2027, the Hotel shall not advertise, offer, book, or sell any room accommodations to the general public, any individual guest, any tour operator, any travel agent, any online travel agency, any corporate account, or any other third party at a nightly rate lower than the rate extended to the Institute of Certified Actuarial Analysts under this Agreement, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel agrees that during the Event dates of November 9 through November 12, 2027, the Hotel shall not advertise, offer, book, or sell any room accommodations to the general public, any individual guest, any tour operator, any travel agent, any online travel agency, any corporate account, or any other third party at a nightly rate lower than the rate extended to the Institute of Certified Actuarial Analysts under this Agreement.

findings.headline: Post-cutoff group rate left to yield management, and no held/refund/release procedure for unassigned rooms
findings.finding_text: The cutoff is set at 32 days before arrival, later than CD's 21-day floor. After cutoff, pricing and availability are determined solely by 'Hotel's yield management practices and current market conditions,' with only a 'commercially reasonable efforts' promise rather than a guaranteed group rate for as long as Hotel sells the same room type to the public. The clause also lacks any provision for holding unassigned rooms on prepayment, refunding attendees who later pay for them, or releasing them only after consultation with Group to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff no earlier than 21 days before arrival; group rate continues post-cutoff for as long as Hotel sells rooms to the public (same room type once block sold); unassigned rooms held on prepayment/refunded, or released only after consultation with Group to reduce attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the reservation deadline, Group may request additional reservations or modifications after the cutoff, and such requests shall continue to be offered at the group rate, subject to availability, provided that Hotel makes no representation that rooms shall remain available at that rate once the cutoff has passed. Pricing and room type availability following the cutoff shall be determined solely by Hotel's yield management practices and current market conditions. Hotel shall exercise commercially reasonable efforts to honor Group's requests at the negotiated rate, but Group acknowledges that Hotel's primary obligation after the cutoff is to maximize occupancy and revenue across all guest segments.

findings.headline: No remedy stated if Hotel cancels without contractual right
findings.finding_text: The contract addresses Hotel's ability to terminate for Group's material breach and various Group termination rights, but contains no provision obligating Hotel to pay Group's damages — staff time, rebooking costs, rate/airfare differentials, attorney's fees, printing costs — if Hotel cancels the agreement without any right to do so under its terms.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.headline: No named function rooms, square footage, rental waiver, or in-room equipment guarantee
findings.finding_text: The contract nowhere identifies the specific function rooms held for Group, their minimum square footage or ceiling height, whether room rental is waived, or a change-consent requirement, and it does not guarantee complimentary in-room equipment such as a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC.
findings.cd_standard: Function rooms should be named with minimum square footage and ceiling height, changeable only by mutual written consent, with room rental waived for program agenda space and complimentary in-room microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement in this Agreement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power (including existing power outlets), proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.headline: Facility/service reduction threshold set at 30%, looser than CD's 25%
findings.finding_text: CD's standard triggers Hotel's obligation to offer alternatives (or Group's termination right) once a facility or service reduction exceeds 25% of published capacity or scope. This contract sets that trigger at 30%, meaning Group has less protection and Hotel can reduce facilities or services further before any remedy is available.
findings.cd_standard: Trigger for equal-alternative offer or termination right should be a reduction of more than 25% of published capacity or offering.
findings.proposed_language: In the event that circumstances beyond the Hotel's reasonable control necessitate the temporary or permanent reduction, limitation, or discontinuation of any facility or service by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its stated capacity or scope, the Hotel shall immediately notify Group in writing and propose alternative facilities or services of substantially equal quality, functionality, and utility, such alternatives to be provided at no additional charge to Group.
findings.quoted_text: In the event that circumstances beyond the Hotel's reasonable control necessitate the temporary or permanent reduction, limitation, or discontinuation of any facility or service by more than thirty percent (30%) of its stated capacity or scope, the Hotel shall immediately notify Group in writing and propose alternative facilities or services of substantially equal quality, functionality, and utility, such alternatives to be provided at no additional charge to Group.

findings.headline: Annual rate increase cap and rate-lock deadline both looser than CD's benchmark
findings.finding_text: CD caps future room rate increases at 2% per year and requires final rates to be confirmed no later than 12 months before the event. This contract allows increases up to 3% per year and locks final rates only 11 months before the event, both giving Hotel more room to raise rates and less lead time for Group's budgeting than CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Maximum yearly rate increase of 2%, with rates finalized in writing no later than 12 months before arrival.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall not increase the group room rates from year to year by more than two percent (2%) on an annual basis. The Group shall confirm all room rates as final twelve (12) months prior to the event dates of November 9-12, 2027, at which time no further modifications to pricing shall be permitted except as expressly set forth in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not increase the group room rates from year to year by more than three percent (3%) on an annual basis. Should the Hotel offer lower rates to its transient guests in the market in which The Monarch on Fifth, New York, New York is located before the arrival of the Institute of Certified Actuarial Analysts, the group rate shall be adjusted downward by the same percentage reduction applied to such market rates. The Group shall confirm all room rates as final eleven (11) months prior to the event dates of November 9-12, 2027, at which time no further modifications to pricing shall be permitted except as expressly set forth in this Agreement.

findings.headline: No individual reservation confirmation, cancellation, no-show, or deposit terms
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provisions on sending individual reservation confirmations within a set window, allowing name changes at the group rate, permitting individual cancellations without charge until a defined time before arrival, reinstating no-shows at the same rate, or refunding individual deposits with short notice and crediting any retained individual cancellation money against Group's attrition liability.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival); name changes at group rate up to arrival; individual cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival; no-show reinstatement at same rate; individual deposit refund with 3 working days' notice; individual cancellation money credited against attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.headline: Damage percentages tied to full ADR rather than 70% lost-profit formula, and rebooking credit window too short
findings.finding_text: CD's damages formula limits recovery to 70% lost-profit of the group's single net rate applied against the block less allowable attrition, with a 3-year rebooking credit. This contract's sliding scale (35%-70% of room revenue/rate) is not stated as a lost-profit percentage against a net rate net of allowable attrition, and its rebooking credit only covers rebookings within 12 months rather than CD's 3-year benchmark.
findings.cd_standard: Damages should be 70% lost room profit of the single net group rate applied to the block less allowable attrition, with a 3-year rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group cancel the Event, Group shall pay liquidated damages to the Hotel calculated as a percentage of room profit on a sliding scale, where one hundred percent (100%) of room profit is defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition. Should Group execute a definitive agreement with the Hotel to book another event at the Hotel at any time within three (3) years of the cancellation, the revenue the Hotel generates from Group's rebooking shall be credited against the damages paid, up to the full amount of damages owed for the cancelled Event.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group cancel the Event, Group shall pay liquidated damages to the Hotel, which the parties acknowledge are not penalties but a reasonable pre-estimate of harm, calculated as a percentage of lost room profit based on the average daily room rate for the negotiated block, the number of room nights in the block, and the number of days' notice given prior to the Event's opening day.

findings.headline: No staffing ratio guarantees for servers or bartenders
findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision guaranteeing minimum server-to-guest or bartender-to-guest ratios at plated or buffet meal functions, and no cap limiting labor fees to only very small functions.
findings.cd_standard: Minimum staffing ratios (1:25 plated breakfast, 1:20 plated lunch/dinner, 1:40/1:30 buffet, 1:75 hosted bar, 1:100 cash bar) with no labor fee except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.

findings.headline: No provisions for new-build or reopening-after-closure scenarios
findings.finding_text: The clause addresses existing-facility renovation disclosed after signing with 30-day notice and termination rights, but is silent on the separate CD requirement for a new build or hotel reopening after closure: a committed fully-operational date, 5-business-day notice of any change to that date, Group's right to terminate if the change interferes with its meeting, and Hotel's obligation to cover Group's damages if no suitable alternative venue can be found.
findings.cd_standard: For a new build or reopening hotel, Hotel commits to a fully-operational date, gives 5 business days' notice of any change, Group may terminate without liability if the change affects its meeting, and Hotel covers Group's damages if no suitable alternative venue is found.
findings.proposed_language: For a new build or a hotel reopening after closure, Hotel confirms that all facilities will be open and fully operational no later than ninety (90) days before Group's arrival, and will notify Group in writing within five (5) business days of any change to that date or to the project's planned scope. If Group, at its sole discretion, determines the change will interfere with its meeting or fail to meet its requirements, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice; should Group be unable to find a suitable alternative location, Hotel will pay Group's direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs arising from those circumstances.

findings.headline: Commission rate below standard, paid later, and silent on key protections
findings.finding_text: CD requires 10% commission paid within 30 days of departure, 10% of any cancellation damages collected, non-cancelable/non-transferable status, upward adjustment if Hotel's or brand's standard commission rises, survival through brand/management change, and an acknowledgment that Group could not have negotiated better terms directly. This contract sets commission at only 9%, remits it within 35 days (later than CD's 30-day standard), and is silent on all of the cancellation-damages commission, non-cancelable/non-transferable, rate pass-through, brand-change survival, and direct-negotiation acknowledgment terms.
findings.cd_standard: 10% commission on all actualized room revenue, paid within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable/non-transferable, rising with brand standard commission, surviving brand/management change, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected, and an acknowledgment Group could not have negotiated better terms directly.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall pay to Group a sales commission equal to ten percent (10%) of all room revenue actualized in connection with the Event, whether such rooms are booked as part of the blocked allocation or otherwise procured by Group members through independent channels. The Hotel shall remit the commission payment within thirty (30) days following the completion of the Event. Hotel agrees that Group could not have negotiated more favorable room rates, terms, and concessions had Group negotiated directly with Hotel rather than through ConferenceDirect, and Hotel and Group agree that commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Should the standard hotel or brand commission percentage increase before the Event, the higher percentage will apply; should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.
