findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall pay to Group a sales commission equal to nine percent (9%) of all room revenue actualized in connection with the Event, whether such rooms are booked as part of the blocked allocation or otherwise procured by Group members through independent channels. Commission shall be calculated on the gross room rate charged to the guest, including all taxes, service charges, and mandatory resort fees, and shall be based on the Hotel's actual folio records for the Event dates.

findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment or discriminatory-legislation termination right
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause committing Hotel and its staff to nondiscrimination against attendees, and no corresponding right for Group to terminate without liability if the state or city adopts legislation permitting discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel and staff should commit not to discriminate against attendees on listed protected grounds, with Group able to terminate without liability if local legislation allows such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city in which Hotel is located adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, or prohibits the adoption of nondiscrimination measures on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.headline: No AV pricing or internet bandwidth commitment anywhere in the contract
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause honoring a quoted AV price, no discount for additional AV needs, no internet bandwidth minimum guarantee, and no statement that using the in-house AV provider is not a condition of discounted or complimentary services.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should honor attached AV and internet bandwidth quotes (minimum 10 Mbps down / 1 Mbps up), give a stated discount on additions, and never condition discounted or complimentary services like internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

clause_review.basis: CD requires pricing locked no earlier than 12 months out and shortfall billed at 35%; this contract locks pricing 14 months out and bills shortfall at 40% (subject to Hotel's discretion to waive), and is silent on affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting toward the minimum.
Group may use outside vendors, but a surcharge is imposed (stated as $0.00 in this instance but structured as a chargeable surcharge clause), contrary to CD's 'no additional fee' requirement.

CD requires 70% threshold and 70% lost-profit damages with rebooking credit; contract sets threshold at 75% (worse for Group), damages at 75% of ADR (higher than 70%), has no F&B-to-attrition dollar-for-dollar credit, and no rebooking credit provision (rebooking credit exists only in cancellation clause, not attrition).

Broad FM clause covers epidemics, travel restrictions, etc., but is silent on the 20% attendee cancellation trigger, silent on Group's right to invoke regardless of knowledge at signing, and silent on waiving attrition/F&B/rental fees and lowest-rate offer if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling entirely.

Disclosure and waiver of undisclosed fees meets standard; resort fee is waived (meets); but contract is silent on written approval before post-signature add-on charges, and silent on early check-in/checked-bag fee waivers.

CD requires 1:40 ratio, counting miscoded rooms and no-show/cancellation fee nights, and complimentary internet regardless of loyalty status; contract sets ratio at 1:45 and is silent on miscoded room credit, no-show/cancellation night credit, and complimentary internet.
Group may assign to successor/affiliated management entity without Hotel consent if assignee assumes obligations and notice given; other assignment requires consent not unreasonably withheld.
Indemnification is mutual and limited to own negligence (meets); but insurance obligation is imposed only on Group ($2.5M CGL), not mutual as CD requires.

Termination for cause addresses Hotel's termination of Group, not Group's ability to terminate for causes like epidemic determination, labor dispute, brand change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, or discriminatory legislation as a unified walk-away right; these exist scattered in other clauses (labor, brand change, construction, facilities) but convention center/overflow hotel unavailability is missing entirely, and no single consolidated termination-for-cause-by-Group clause referencing force majeure epidemic judgment exists apart from FM clause itself.
CD requires 30-day hotel notice and 30-day Group termination window; contract gives Hotel up to 35 days to notify and Group only 25 days to terminate, both worse than CD standard.
No deposit charged; damage liability handled via itemized documentation within 30 days, refund of any deposit within 30 days, not commingled with attrition/F&B.

No 24/12 month block review with adjustment rights; pickup reports begin only 8 weeks (56 days) before event rather than starting well before cutoff; no post-event report detail on AV/bandwidth/exhibitor spend; audit is at Group's own expense rather than no-cost; no miscoded-room credit provision (brand-associate/business rate rooms).

Hotel warranty and mutual indemnification meet; but auxiliary aid cost allocation is to be negotiated/divided rather than Group funding function-space aids and Hotel funding guest room/common area aids as CD requires.
Governed by law/venue of Group's principal offices, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees.
Separate named storm clause with 60-hour cancellation window covering the event dates.
Hotel barred from using attendee data for own marketing or selling/sharing to third parties without consent.

CD requires 1-year advance notice of CBA expirations and cancellation right if dispute arises within 90 days of event; contract gives only 9 months advance notice (short of 1 year) and cancellation window is 75 days after Group becomes aware, not tied to the 90-day pre-event window CD specifies.

Gratuity/service charge are separately defined and gratuity distributed to staff (meets); but service charge is 22%, well above CD's 6% benchmark figure, and no confirmation that neither is added to room rental/equipment with labor fee already included.

Finance charge is 1.3%/month, exceeding CD's 1% cap; dispute window is only 12 days rather than 30; no-credit prepayment is a flat 75% rather than staged 25/25/50 schedule; no provision for automatic credit extension if Hotel fails to send a credit application.

Relocation covers comparable/better accommodations, transportation, upgrade/amenity, and pickup credit for relocated nights (meets much of standard); but no per-room-night rebate to Group's master account (CD specifies $200/night), no explicit exemption from attrition liability for walked nights, and no additional compensation trigger for walking 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak night block.

Active resale duty, tracking, and monthly statements meet much of the standard; but damages are due within 30 days of cancellation notice (via clause 4) rather than 30 days after the meeting dates, and clause 4's damages calc timing conflicts with the 30-days-post-event standard.

Rate parity is absolute with retroactive adjustment and no reduction to commission/pickup credit (meets much); but contract does not include the no-higher-than-other-groups' rate within 7 days before/after protection, and lacks the qualified-rate carve-out (government/airline/corporate) leaving Hotel unable to offer legitimate discounted rates at all.

CD requires cutoff no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, continued group rate post-cutoff for same room type while selling to public, and held/refunded/released-with-consultation treatment of unassigned rooms; contract sets cutoff at 32 days prior (earlier than CD's floor is fine but wait—cutoff earlier than 21 days is stricter, that's a deviation) and post-cutoff pricing is discretionary via Hotel's yield management with no guaranteed rate continuation, and no provision on holding/refunding/releasing unassigned rooms.
No clause addresses Hotel's liability if Hotel cancels the agreement without contractual right; only Group cancellation and Hotel termination-for-cause (Group's breach) are addressed.
No clause naming function rooms, minimum square footage/ceiling height, room rental waiver, or complimentary in-room AV basics (microphone, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
CD threshold is more than 25% reduction triggering equal alternatives/termination; contract uses a 30% threshold, a looser (worse for Group) trigger than CD's standard.

CD caps future rate increases at 2%/year and requires rates finalized no later than 12 months before event; contract caps increase at 3%/year and finalizes rates only 11 months before event, both worse than CD standard.
No provisions on confirmation timing, name changes, individual cancellation deadline (6pm day of arrival), no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund/crediting toward attrition.

Sliding scale disclosed and mitigation/rebooking credit present (partially meets); but damages based on 75%/70%/etc of ADR without stating 70% lost-profit-of-net-group-rate methodology tied to allowable attrition offset, and rebooking credit window is 12 months rather than 3 years as CD specifies.
No staffing ratio guarantees for servers or bartenders, and no cap on labor fees for small functions.

Covers existing-facility renovation with 30-day notice and Group termination right (meets much); but is silent on new-build/reopening scenarios (fully-operational date commitment, 5-business-day change notice, damages if no alternative venue found).

CD requires 10% commission, payment within 30 days, 10% of cancellation damages, non-cancelable/non-transferable, rising with brand standard, and confirmation Group could not have negotiated better direct; contract pays only 9% commission, remits within 35 days (later than 30), and is silent on cancellation-damages commission, non-cancelable/non-transferable status, rate-increase pass-through, and the direct-negotiation acknowledgment.
No nondiscrimination commitment or termination right tied to discriminatory state/local legislation appears anywhere in the contract.
No AV or internet bandwidth quote, discount on additional needs, or bandwidth minimum is addressed anywhere in the contract.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is well-organized with numbered sections generally corresponding one-to-one with standard clause types, which aided review. A few CD standard clause types (function space, reservation procedures, banquet service levels, nondiscrimination, AV/internet, hotel cancellation) have no corresponding section anywhere in the document and are marked missing. Some figures in the contract (e.g., outside vendor surcharge of "$0.00", insurance minimum of "$2,500,000.00") appear in quotation marks in the source text, suggesting they may be template placeholders filled in for this specific deal; they were treated as the operative figures for this review. Section 8 (Termination for Cause) addresses only Hotel's right to terminate for Group's breach, not a consolidated Group-side termination-for-cause right, so Group's termination rights had to be cross-referenced across the force majeure, labor, brand-change, construction, and facilities clauses.

findings.headline: Pricing locked 24 months out and full shortfall owed, not 35%
findings.finding_text: The contract locks menu pricing for 24 months from signature (well beyond CD's 12-month standard) and requires Group to pay the entire shortfall between actual F&B revenue and the 80%-of-projection guarantee, rather than the 35% fraction CD negotiates. It also does not count affiliate or exhibitor F&B spend toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Menu pricing should be locked no earlier than 12 months before the event, and any shortfall billed at 35% of the gap, not the full difference; affiliate/exhibitor F&B should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will be confirmed at the Hotel's pricing in effect on the date of this Agreement, or established not earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If the Group's actual food and beverage charges, when totaled for the entire Event Period, fall short of the guaranteed minimum amount, the Group shall pay to the Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, within thirty (30) days of final invoice. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide to the Group a menu and pricing proposal that shall remain binding as to pricing for a period of twenty-four (24) months from the date of this Agreement, and any adjustments to menu items, portion sizes, or pricing thereafter shall be subject to mutual written consent of both parties or shall be implemented only upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the Group.

findings.headline: Outside vendors barred and subject to a $2,500 surcharge
findings.finding_text: Group must use Hotel-approved vendors for catering, AV, floral, entertainment and all other services, and any outside vendor use — even if permitted — triggers a $2,500 per-service/category surcharge, contrary to CD's position that Group should be free to use its chosen vendors at no additional fee.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge; in-house vendors should not be mandatory.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to catering, audiovisual equipment, floral arrangements, entertainment, and all other services provided in connection with the Event. Hotel's in-house or designated vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage only the Hotel's in-house vendors or those exclusively appointed by the Hotel for catering, audiovisual equipment, floral arrangements, entertainment, and all other services provided in connection with the Event, except as expressly waived in writing by the Hotel's Director of Sales. Group's use of outside vendors not approved in advance by the Hotel shall be subject to a surcharge of $2,500.00 per outside vendor service or vendor category, which surcharge shall be assessed in addition to any other charges imposed under this Agreement and shall be due and payable to the Hotel within thirty (30) days of the end of the Event.
findings.exposure_basis: Surcharge per outside vendor service/category as stated in the contract

findings.headline: Night-by-night measurement, 80% threshold, full-rate damages, no audit
findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively, the liability threshold is 80% instead of CD's 70%, damages are calculated at 80% of the full nightly room rate rather than 70% lost profit on the net group rate, no night below 100% occupancy gets credit (CD's standard is 95%), and Group is explicitly denied any right to audit or challenge the Hotel's occupancy determinations. There is also no rebooking credit for CD clients.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be cumulative across the block, trigger only below 70% pickup, damages capped at 70% lost profit on the net group rate, full credit for nights at 95%+ occupancy, audit rights, and a rebooking credit.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) (lost profit) of Group's single confirmed net group rate of $189.00, calculated as the lesser of the number of unsold rooms in the Hotel that night or the shortfall between Group's minimum block and actual pickup. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. At Group's request, Hotel will provide a copy of its city ledger or daily report showing the information needed to verify the calculation. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and Group's block commitment is calculated as the total number of room nights reserved under the block minus attrition, if any. The Hotel will measure Group's room-night usage against the block on each night of the Event and will track any shortfall between the committed room nights and the room nights actually occupied by Group members. If Group's actual occupancy falls below the attrition threshold of eighty percent (80%) of the committed room nights for the Event, Group shall be liable for liquidated damages as set forth herein. Group's liability for attrition shall be calculated at eighty percent (80%) of the nightly room rate for each unoccupied committed room night. The Hotel will apply this liability rate to determine the total amount due from Group for any shortfall in occupancy. Group shall receive no credit toward its block commitment for any night on which the Hotel sells out all available rooms in the Hotel, regardless of whether Group's occupied rooms on such night fall below the threshold percentage. Nights on which the Hotel achieves one hundred percent (100%) occupancy shall be excluded from the attrition calculation for purposes of determining whether Group has met its commitment. The Hotel's calculation of attrition damages shall be final and binding on Group, and Group shall have no right to inspect, audit, or challenge the Hotel's occupancy records or the Hotel's determination of room nights sold, occupied, or available on any night during the Event. All determinations regarding room availability, resale of Group rooms, and occupancy levels shall rest solely with the Hotel and shall not be subject to Group's review, verification, or dispute.
findings.exposure_basis: 275-room block x $189 rate x 100% (80% vs 70% liability rate) as a rough per-unsold-room-night comparison across the block

findings.headline: Excludes travel restrictions/advisories and forfeits deposits entirely
findings.finding_text: The clause requires performance to be 'physically impossible' (a much higher bar than commercially impracticable or inadvisable), expressly carves out government travel restrictions and advisories as non-qualifying events, has no 20% attendee-cancellation trigger, provides no fee waiver if Group holds a reduced-size meeting, and states deposits/prepayments are retained by the Hotel in their entirety with no refund right.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should excuse performance for illegality, impossibility, impracticability, or inadvisability (including health/safety), include government travel advisories/restrictions as qualifying causes, apply even for known conditions, waive fees for reduced meetings, and refund deposits promptly.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including, but not limited to, acts of God; war; curtailment or interruption of transportation facilities; strikes; threats or acts of terrorism; disease or epidemic; a CDC advisory, or a State Department or other governmental or international agency travel advisory; full or partial government closure; declaration of a national, state, or local emergency; prohibition or limitation of travel by any government employees; corporate or educational institution travel restrictions; civil disturbance; or any other cause beyond the parties' control — in that party's reasonable judgment: make it commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including for health or safety reasons), illegal, or impossible for either party to perform, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel their attendance. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances, Hotel will waive any fees related to a reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Neither party shall be deemed in breach of this Agreement if performance becomes physically impossible due to an event beyond that party's reasonable control, including but not limited to acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, labor strikes, or material failure of utilities or infrastructure. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither government-imposed travel restrictions nor government travel advisories of any kind, whether mandatory or advisory in character, shall be deemed a force majeure event excusing or limiting the obligations of Group under this Agreement. In the event that performance is excused by force majeure, the affected party shall provide written notice to the other party within seven (7) business days of the force majeure event or of the discovery of such event, whichever is earlier. The Agreement shall be terminated or suspended as the parties shall mutually agree, provided that Group's deposits and prepayments made to the Hotel shall be retained by the Hotel in their entirety, and Group shall have no claim against the Hotel for the return of any funds, whether characterized as deposits, prepayments, or advances, notwithstanding the invocation of force majeure.

findings.headline: Undisclosed fees and non-waivable $35 resort fee remain chargeable
findings.finding_text: The contract allows Hotel to assess new fees at any time post-execution at its sole discretion and expressly states that failure to disclose a fee before signing does not relieve Group of liability. A mandatory $35/night resort fee is imposed with no waiver and no early check-in/bag fee protection.
findings.cd_standard: All charges must be disclosed in writing before signature; any undisclosed charge is waived; resort fees should be waived while resort services are still honored, and attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges that may be associated with the Event, including but not limited to resort fees, surcharges, facility fees, administrative costs, and technology fees. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived. Should Group require additional services after signature, Hotel must obtain Group's written approval before providing the service and before posting the charge to the master account. Hotel will waive the resort fee for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee services, and will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel reserves the right to assess additional fees, surcharges, and service charges against Group's account at any time following execution of this Agreement, in Hotel's sole discretion. Such additional charges may include but are not limited to facility fees, administrative costs, technology fees, and other ancillary charges that Hotel determines necessary or appropriate for the Event. Notwithstanding any other provision, Group remains liable for all charges assessed by Hotel, whether or not such charges were disclosed in writing prior to execution of this Agreement. Hotel's failure to disclose any fee or surcharge before signature shall not relieve Group of its obligation to pay such charge upon invoice. Group shall pay a resort fee in the amount of $35.00 per occupied room per night for the duration of the Event. This resort fee is non-negotiable, applies to all room types and rate categories, and shall be added to Group's final invoice without regard to any occupancy or package arrangements.
findings.exposure_basis: $35/night x 275 rooms x 1 peak night as an illustrative baseline of the mandatory resort fee exposure

findings.headline: 1:80 ratio, forfeiture on any shortfall, entirely discretionary award
findings.finding_text: The complimentary room ratio is 1:80 rather than CD's 1:40, is described only as a 'guideline' with no commitment, is entirely at Hotel's discretion and forfeited entirely if Group's pickup falls short of the block (rather than calculated cumulatively regardless of block performance), and does not count miscoded rooms, no-show fees, or cancellation fees toward pickup, nor address complimentary internet.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear cumulative formula of 1 per 40 occupied room nights regardless of attrition, counting miscoded rooms and no-show/cancellation fee nights, plus complimentary in-room internet.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block (total room nights divided by 40), regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met. All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit, and each no-show fee and cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall consider providing complimentary guestroom accommodations to Group at a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every eighty (80) occupied rooms successfully billed during the Event, provided Group achieves full pickup of its contracted room block. The complimentary room ratio stated herein is a guideline only and does not constitute a commitment or guarantee of any specific number of complimentary rooms. Any complimentary rooms awarded under this clause shall be determined entirely at Hotel's sole discretion, and Hotel may withhold, reduce, or decline to honor any portion of complimentary room credit for any reason, including but not limited to operational constraints, rate disputes, or Group's failure to maintain satisfactory payment status. Group acknowledges that the award of complimentary rooms is a courtesy benefit subject to Hotel's exclusive control. Complimentary room credit is forfeited entirely in the event Group's actual room pickup falls short of its contracted block as set forth in the room block addendum attached hereto. No partial complimentary room credit shall accrue for shortfalls, and no make-good or alternative compensation shall be owed to Group if complimentary room benefit is forfeited due to attrition.

findings.headline: No carve-out for successor management company assignment
findings.finding_text: The assignment clause requires the Hotel's sole and absolute discretion consent for any assignment, with no exception for assignment to a successor association management company or affiliated entity as CD's position requires, and no unreasonable-withholding standard applies even to other assignments.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without the hotel's consent being unreasonably withheld, where the event is unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment, transfer, or delegation of Group's rights or obligations under this Agreement requires Hotel's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Neither Group nor any officer, agent, or representative of Group shall assign, transfer, delegate, or otherwise convey any right, obligation, or interest under this Agreement to any other person, entity, or organization, whether by operation of law, merger, consolidation, acquisition, or voluntary act, without the prior written consent of the Hotel. Any attempted assignment, transfer, or delegation in violation of this provision shall be void and of no effect, and shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement entitling the Hotel to immediate cancellation of the room block and any related accommodations or services. The Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment or transfer shall be entirely within the Hotel's sole and absolute discretion, and the Hotel may withhold consent to an assignment for any reason whatsoever or for no reason stated.

findings.headline: One-way indemnity covering Hotel's own negligence, no mutual insurance
findings.finding_text: Group must indemnify Hotel even for the Hotel's own ordinary and gross negligence, while the Hotel has no reciprocal indemnification obligation to Group whatsoever. Insurance is required of Group only, with no corresponding obligation on the Hotel to carry adequate coverage for its own activities.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct, with each party's attorney's fees, surviving termination; the group should never indemnify the hotel for the hotel's own negligence. Insurance should be a mutual obligation.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party and its respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and independent contractors against all claims, losses, or damages to persons or property, governmental charges or fines, and costs (including reasonable attorney's fees), arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party, its employees, agents, or contractors. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence. This provision survives the termination or expiration of this Agreement. Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect their own activities against claims arising out of the Event, and Group shall obtain and maintain comprehensive general liability insurance with limits not less than $5,000,000.00 per occurrence and $10,000,000.00 in the aggregate, naming the Hotel as an additional insured.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall indemnify, defend with counsel reasonably acceptable to the Hotel, and hold harmless the Hotel, its owners, officers, employees, and agents from and against any and all claims, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from Group's use of the Hotel's facilities, the Event, or Group's breach of this Agreement. The Hotel shall not be obligated to indemnify Group under any circumstances, and Group assumes all risk of loss or injury to Group, its guests, participants, or third parties in connection with the Event. Group's indemnity obligations extend to and include claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence, ordinary or gross, provided that Group shall not be obligated to indemnify the Hotel for claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.headline: Any termination is treated as cancellation and triggers full damages
findings.finding_text: Regardless of the cause of termination — including material breach by Hotel — the contract deems any Group termination a cancellation subject to the full liquidated-damages scale, and provides no walk-away right for force majeure-adjacent causes such as labor disputes, facility reductions, or brand/ownership changes as CD's position requires.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should allow the group to walk away with no liability, separate from the cancellation damages scale, for causes including force majeure, pandemic, labor disputes, ownership/brand change, renovation interference, facility reductions, dependent-venue unavailability, and discriminatory legislation.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; or (g) material breach by Hotel not cured within the cure period. None of the foregoing will be treated as a cancellation by Group or trigger the liquidated-damages calculation set forth in Article 8.
findings.quoted_text: Any termination of this Agreement by the Group, irrespective of the cause or justification asserted by the Group, shall be treated as a cancellation by the Group under the cancellation damages scale set forth in Article 8, and the Group shall pay to the Hotel the cancellation damages calculated in accordance with that scale based on the date on which the termination notice is delivered.

findings.headline: Termination window too short and bankruptcy/foreclosure excluded
findings.finding_text: Group's termination window following notice of a brand/ownership change is only 10 days (CD calls for 30), and the clause explicitly excludes bankruptcy, receivership, and foreclosure from triggering any notice or termination right at all.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel must notify Group within 30 days of a brand/ownership/management change or bankruptcy/foreclosure, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice, with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Following receipt of such notice, Group shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without penalty if Group provides written notice of termination to Hotel within ten (10) days after receiving notice of the ownership or brand change, and such termination shall be effective upon the date specified by Group, provided that Group shall remain liable for payment of all room charges and event charges accrued through the termination date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither bankruptcy, receivership, foreclosure, assignment for benefit of creditors, nor any other proceedings or event arising from the financial distress or insolvency of Hotel or its parent, affiliate, or operating company shall trigger any notice obligation or afford Group any right of termination, cancellation, or offset, and Group's obligations hereunder shall remain in full force and effect regardless of any such development.

findings.headline: Deposit commingled with attrition/F&B charges and refunded in 90 days
findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit may be applied at Hotel's sole discretion against attrition charges, F&B shortfalls, and other unrelated master account items, contrary to CD's position that a deposit should not offset attrition or F&B minimums. The refund window is also 90 days rather than CD's standard 30 days.
findings.cd_standard: A security deposit should be refundable within 30 days absent documented itemized damage, and should not be commingled with or offset unrelated charges like attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: Any security deposit collected under this Agreement will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless the Hotel provides Group with an itemized accounting of specific, documented damage to Hotel property caused by Group or its attendees beyond normal wear and tear. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall apply the deposit, in its sole discretion, against attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damage to Hotel property, unpaid room charges, cancellation fees, or any other amounts owed by Group to Hotel under this Agreement or otherwise. Group shall have no right to offset or withhold payment of other invoiced amounts pending reconciliation of damage deposit claims. Following the Event and reconciliation of all charges and damage claims, Hotel shall return any unused portion of the deposit to Group within ninety (90) days.
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit amount stated in the contract

findings.headline: No block review checkpoints, pickup reports, or audit rights at all
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no 24/12-month block review process, no weekly pickup reports, and expressly bars Group from any audit right, stating pickup information is a purely voluntary service and that Group has no right to independently verify room block or billing records.
findings.cd_standard: Group should get 24/12-month block reviews with adjustment rights, weekly pickup reports, final and post-event reports within set windows, and a no-cost audit right comparing guest lists with miscoded rooms credited to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival, at which points Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at the group rate. Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date, and final room pickup reports with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure. Within thirty (30) days of departure, Hotel will provide a full post-event report including rooms actualized, pace, food and beverage revenue, outlet spend, audio-visual spend, internet bandwidth usage, and exhibitor fees and revenue. At Group's request and at no cost, Hotel will compare its in-house guest list against Group's registration list, either jointly with a representative of Group or by permitting a ConferenceDirect or Group representative to do so independently, and any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: Group may request pickup information from the Hotel at any time, provided that the Hotel shall furnish such reports at its sole discretion and convenience, and Group acknowledges that the provision of pickup information is a voluntary service not required under this Agreement.

findings.headline: Auxiliary aid cost split is vague, not the standard event-space/guest-room division
findings.finding_text: The contract requires costs of auxiliary aids to be 'shared' with the Hotel providing only 'baseline' aids and Group bearing incremental/specialized costs, without the clear division CD requires (Group funds function space aids; Hotel funds guest room and common area aids), and there is no mutual ADA indemnification provision.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should warrant ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation, with mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations, and a clear division of funding: Group funds function-space aids, Hotel funds guest room/common area aids.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA. Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: To the extent that Group's Event requires auxiliary aids or services—including but not limited to interpreters, assistive listening devices, accessible transportation, modified equipment, or other accommodations—the costs of such auxiliary aids shall be shared between Group and the Hotel. The Hotel shall provide baseline auxiliary aids that are considered standard for its operations, while Group shall bear responsibility for the incremental cost of specialized or unusual accommodations tailored specifically to the Event and its participants' particular needs, with the parties to confer in advance regarding the nature and allocation of such costs.

findings.headline: Hotel's home venue governs, and Hotel alone can collect punitive damages/fees
findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are set in the Hotel's own state and county (Indiana, Marion County) rather than Group's location, and the Hotel is entitled to punitive, exemplary, and consequential damages plus prevailing-party attorney's fees, contrary to CD's position of no punitive damages and each side bearing its own fees.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law and venue should be the group's state/city, with punitive damages excluded and each party bearing its own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the state in which Group is located. Any unresolved controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement will be settled by a court of law in the city in which Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will be responsible for its own attorney's fees and expenses.
findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which the Hotel is located, and the parties expressly exclude from application the United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods and any principles of conflicts of law. The Group consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Marion County, Indiana, and waives any objection to venue or claim of inconvenient forum in any action or proceeding arising from or relating to this Agreement or the Event. In any dispute between the parties concerning the performance or interpretation of this Agreement, the prevailing party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorney's fees, court costs, and all other expenses incurred in prosecution or defense of the claim, and such recovery shall be in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity. The Hotel shall be entitled to recover punitive damages, exemplary damages, and all consequential and incidental damages available under applicable law, in addition to actual damages, in any action arising out of the Group's breach or willful misconduct.

findings.headline: Only a 24-hour cancellation trigger window, not 72 hours
findings.finding_text: The named storm clause only allows cancellation if a warning remains in effect as of 24 hours prior to arrival, and requires Group's written notice by that same 24-hour mark — far narrower than CD's 72-hour trigger — reducing Group's practical ability to invoke the clause in time.
findings.cd_standard: A named storm clause should allow cancellation without liability when a named storm is forecast to affect the location within 72 hours of any event date.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm, or equivalent National Weather Service-designated event) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within seventy-two (72) hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the Event without liability upon written notice to the other party, and Hotel shall refund Group's deposits in full within thirty (30) days of such cancellation.
findings.quoted_text: If the National Weather Service issues a named storm warning for the geographic area in which the Hotel is located at any time during the period commencing twenty-four (24) hours before the start of the Event and continuing through the final day of the Event, and if such warning remains in effect as of twenty-four (24) hours prior to the scheduled arrival date of Group, then Group shall have the right, at its sole election and upon written notice to the Hotel delivered no later than twenty-four (24) hours before the Group's scheduled arrival, to cancel this Agreement without penalty, and the Hotel shall refund Group's deposits in full within thirty (30) days of such cancellation.

findings.headline: Hotel may market to attendees and share data without Group's consent
findings.finding_text: The Hotel is expressly permitted to use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes and to share it with affiliates and marketing partners, deeming that sharing automatically permitted without Group's advance approval — contrary to CD's position that rooming list/attendee data should not be used for the Hotel's own marketing or shared without consent.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list and attendee data should be used only to fulfill reservations, not for the hotel's own marketing or disclosed to third parties without the group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and Attendee Information solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations and performing its obligations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email, and telephonic solicitation of the attendees who registered for the Event. Except as permitted herein, the Hotel shall not use Attendee Information for purposes unrelated to performance of this Agreement without the prior written consent of Group. The Hotel may share Attendee Information with its affiliates and marketing partners engaged to assist the Hotel in its promotional activities, provided that the Hotel shall require any such recipient to maintain the confidentiality of Attendee Information and use it solely for the purposes for which it is shared. Group acknowledges that such sharing constitutes a permitted use under this clause and does not require Group's advance approval or consent.

findings.headline: No CBA notice and no cancellation right for strikes or lockouts
findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation to disclose CBA expiration dates or notify Group of labor disputes, and the contract expressly denies Group any cancellation right, damages, or credit for a labor dispute, strike, work stoppage, or lockout affecting the Hotel, contrary to CD's standard allowing liability-free cancellation for disputes arising within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of disputes; if a strike, lockout, or expired contract arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability.
findings.proposed_language: One (1) year in advance, or within thirty (30) days of signing this Agreement if that is later, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year. Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform, and any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have no obligation to provide Group with advance notice, periodic reports, or any information concerning the expiration dates, renewal status, or negotiation schedule of any collective bargaining agreement, labor agreement, or labor arrangement applicable to Hotel's employees or operations, and Group hereby waives any right to receive such notice or information. Group acknowledges that the period, if any, within which a labor dispute, labor action, strike, work stoppage, labor slowdown, or related labor disturbance at the Hotel would entitle Group to cancel this Agreement shall be determined solely by Hotel and communicated, if at all, at Hotel's discretion, and no specific cancellation window or remedy period is established by this Agreement. In the event of any labor dispute, labor action, labor disruption, strike, work stoppage, lockout, or labor disturbance affecting the Hotel or its operations during the Event or in the days immediately preceding the Event, such occurrence shall not relieve Group of any obligation under this Agreement, shall not entitle Group to damages or credits, and shall not furnish grounds for termination or cancellation, and Group shall remain fully liable for all room charges, food and beverage minimums, and other charges under this Agreement.

findings.headline: Gratuity and service charge conflated, entirely retainable by Hotel
findings.finding_text: The 24% combined charge conflates gratuity and service charge as interchangeable terms, and the Hotel has sole discretion to retain the entire amount as its own revenue rather than distributing any of it to staff who worked the event, with no separate percentages disclosed as CD requires.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be separately defined with both percentages disclosed; gratuity should go fully to staff, while any separate service charge is disclosed as hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: Eighteen percent (18%) of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of six percent (6%), plus applicable tax, is not distributed as a tip and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: A service charge and gratuity shall be applied to all food and beverage charges incurred by Group during the Event and shall be assessed at the rate of twenty-four percent (24%) of the total charges. The terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' are used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and do not constitute separately defined charges. The Hotel retains sole discretion to determine the allocation and distribution of any gratuity or service charge collected, including the right to retain all or any portion thereof as Hotel revenue rather than directing such amounts to service staff. The Hotel's retention of gratuity or service charge shall not be deemed a modification of this Agreement or a breach of any obligation owed to Group.

findings.headline: No dispute window, above-cap finance charge, unlimited prepayment demand
findings.finding_text: Invoices allow 'no period in which Group may dispute a charge' before payment is due in 15 days, the finance charge is 1.5% compounded monthly (above CD's 1% simple cap), and if credit is not approved the Hotel may demand prepayment 'in whatever amount it determines,' rather than a defined staged schedule.
findings.cd_standard: Master account should be payable on invoice with a real dispute window before finance charges apply, finance charges capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, and a defined staged deposit schedule (or capped prepayment) if credit is denied.
findings.proposed_language: If Group's credit is approved, the master account is payable upon receipt of invoice. If payment of all undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of the final invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit is denied, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: All invoiced amounts shall be due and payable in full when due, with no period in which Group may dispute a charge. Invoices shall be submitted by Hotel to Group's designated billing contact within thirty (30) days following the Event, and payment shall be due within fifteen (15) days of invoice date. Hotel shall identify on each invoice the specific charges being billed, the date charges were incurred, and the room number or function space to which charges relate. If any amount owed by Group remains unpaid following the due date, Hotel shall have the right to charge a monthly finance charge of 1.5% on the outstanding balance, compounded monthly, until such amount is paid in full. Such finance charges shall accrue on the principal balance whether or not Hotel pursues other remedies available at law or in equity. Where Hotel has not approved credit for Group under this Agreement, Hotel may require prepayment in whatever amount it determines prior to Event.

findings.headline: Guests bear walk costs, no rebate, relocated nights excluded from pickup
findings.finding_text: Displaced guests must arrange and pay for their own alternate lodging and transportation, receive no upgrade or amenity on return, and Group receives no per-room-night rebate; relocated nights are expressly excluded from pickup and commission credit rather than credited, contrary to CD's position across every element of this clause.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should get comparable-or-better accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, and an upgrade/amenity on return at the hotel's expense; Group should get a per-room-night rebate and pickup/commission credit, with no attrition liability for walked nights.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate any member of Group holding a confirmed reservation, Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable hotel as close as possible, at no charge to the guest, for each night the guest is displaced; (b) provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel for each day the guest is displaced; (c) forward the displaced guest's telephone messages, mail, and packages; and (d) when the guest returns, provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity. Hotel will credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable at the group rate, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages if any guest is walked on any night.
findings.quoted_text: In the event of a walk, Hotel shall make a reasonable effort to find alternative lodging for the affected guest, provided that any such alternative accommodation shall be at the guest's own expense and shall be arranged by the guest rather than by Hotel. The affected guest shall bear full responsibility for all transportation costs to and from any alternative hotel arranged pursuant to a walk relocation. Hotel shall not provide, arrange, or reimburse transportation between the Hotel and any substitute facility, and guests shall make their own arrangements for such travel at their sole cost and expense. Upon the guest's return to Hotel following relocation, Hotel shall provide standard room accommodation with no room upgrade, no amenity credit, no complimentary services, and no compensation other than the refund or credit of the room rate for the night(s) of relocation. No welcome gift, resort credit, or other amenity shall be provided to a relocated guest upon return. For purposes of calculating Group's room pickup and Hotel's commission computation under this Agreement, a room night on which a guest was relocated shall not be counted as a room night stayed at Hotel. Such relocated night shall not be credited toward Group's total room pickup commitment, nor shall it be counted in any calculation of Hotel's revenue or commission base.

findings.headline: No duty to mitigate; resale proceeds kept entirely by Hotel
findings.finding_text: The Hotel has no obligation whatsoever to attempt to resell released rooms or function space, retains any resale proceeds entirely without crediting them against Group's damages, and Group is barred from auditing or reviewing the Hotel's resale efforts or records.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to try to resell canceled rooms/functions and credit proceeds against what the group owes, with records available for verification.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Hotel will document in writing its efforts to market the dates proactively through all group and transient channels. All Hotel records relating to mitigation, including actual occupancy reports, will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of rooms or function space by Group, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory, and Group waives any right to require the Hotel to undertake resale efforts or to mitigate damages through the placement of such space with alternative guests or groups. The Hotel's discretion in determining whether and to what extent to market released rooms or function space shall be absolute and shall not be subject to challenge by Group on any ground, including alleged failure to use commercially reasonable efforts or to act in good faith. Any proceeds received by the Hotel from the resale of released rooms or function space shall be retained entirely by the Hotel and shall not be credited against Group's remaining payment obligations under this Agreement. Such resale proceeds shall be the Hotel's property without obligation to share, rebate, or account for such amounts to Group, and the retention of resale proceeds shall not reduce or offset the charges and fees Group remains obligated to pay. Group shall have no right to inspect, audit, or otherwise review the Hotel's resale efforts, pricing strategies, marketing activities, or records related to the resale of any released inventory. The Hotel's books and records with respect to resale transactions shall be confidential to the Hotel, and Group waives any contractual or statutory right to obtain such information or to challenge the Hotel's representation of resale activity or proceeds.

findings.headline: Lower rates not retroactive and excluded from pickup/commission
findings.finding_text: The Hotel may sell rooms at any rate without restriction, any relief for Group applies only prospectively (no retroactive adjustment for existing reservations), and any adjusted lower rate is deemed non-commissionable and excluded from Group's pickup and rebate calculations — contrary to CD's requirement that Group keep both commission and pickup credit.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should guarantee it won't undercut the group's rate; if it does, the group's rate should adjust (including retroactively) or all attendee rooms count in the block regardless of rate, with Group keeping commission and pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (government, airline, and contracted corporate negotiated rates). If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees. Commission will be paid on the contracted rate regardless of any rate adjustment, and such rooms remain creditable toward Group's pickup, complimentary-room credits, attrition, and any other concession based on pickup.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel expressly reserves the right to offer rooms to the general public, corporate accounts, and other groups at rates lower than, equal to, or higher than Group's negotiated rate for the Event, without restriction or obligation to adjust Group's rate or to honor any "most favored customer" clause, price-matching commitment, or rate guarantee of any kind. Hotel's inventory allocation, pricing strategy, and distribution across customer segments shall be within Hotel's exclusive business judgment. In the event Hotel identifies an opportunity to sell rooms at a rate lower than Group's negotiated rate, any rate reduction or adjustment offered to Group shall apply only to new reservations made by Group after such lower rate has been identified and communicated in writing to Group. Previous reservations made by Group members at the higher rate shall not be retroactively adjusted or repriced, and Group shall have no right to demand modification of reservations already confirmed in Hotel's system. Any adjusted rate made available to Group following identification of a lower public rate shall be treated as a non-commissionable rate and shall not be credited toward Group's room block pickup, occupancy targets, or performance metrics for purposes of calculating complimentary rooms, rebates, or other volume-based benefits under this Agreement. Such adjusted reservations shall be tracked separately in Hotel's booking records and shall have no impact on Group's achievement of contracted minimums.

findings.headline: Post-cutoff rooms revert to rack rate with no hold/release protections
findings.finding_text: After the 45-day cutoff, reservations lose the group rate entirely and are offered only at rack rate, with no continuation of group rate while the hotel sells to the public, no option to hold unassigned rooms on prepayment, and no consultation with Group before releasing unsold rooms to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: After cutoff, attendees should still get the group rate as long as the hotel is selling to the public (or for that room type once the block is sold), and unassigned rooms should be held on prepayment, refunded, or released only after consultation with Group.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public.
findings.quoted_text: All room reservations on behalf of Group must be requested and confirmed by the Hotel no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the Event check-in date of July 13, 2027. This deadline is firm and applies to all reservations claimed to be within the block, whether such reservations are made directly with the Hotel or through a third-party reservation service. Reservations submitted or confirmed after this cutoff date shall not be deemed part of Group's room block and shall not receive the negotiated group rate, regardless of room availability. Any reservation requested after the cutoff date shall be offered only at the Hotel's prevailing rack rate then in effect for the dates requested, and Group shall have no claim that such reservations constitute attrition avoidance or that they reduce any liability Group may have under the attrition clause. The Hotel reserves the right to decline any reservation request made after the cutoff date if rooms are not available at rack rate, and Group shall have no recourse against the Hotel for any inability to secure accommodations for late-arriving attendees.

findings.headline: No remedy stated if Hotel wrongfully cancels the agreement
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing the Hotel's liability if the Hotel cancels the agreement without a contractual right to do so; only Group's cancellation liability is addressed, leaving Group without a stated remedy for a Hotel-caused cancellation.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe the group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.headline: No function space rooms, square footage, or complimentary terms specified
findings.finding_text: The contract identifies only a guest room block; it names no specific meeting/function rooms, minimum square footage or ceiling heights, and contains no commitment that meeting space is complimentary or that basic in-room equipment (mic, podium, power, HVAC) is provided at no charge.
findings.cd_standard: The contract should name each function room with minimum square footage/ceiling height, prohibit reassignment without consent, provide complimentary meeting space with room rental waived, and include basic in-room equipment at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power, proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.headline: No protection if Hotel closes or reduces facilities/services
findings.finding_text: There is no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially limits restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, or reduces staffing ratios for key services, leaving Group without a remedy or termination right for such reductions.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes/limits facilities by more than 25% or materially reduces service staffing, it should first offer equal alternatives at its own expense; absent resolution within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, or security services in a material manner, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to Hotel, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.headline: No rate-decline protection or increase cap for unconfirmed future charges
findings.finding_text: While the $189 group rate for 2027 appears fixed, the contract contains no clause capping any future rate increase at 2% or reducing Group's rate if market or published rates decline before arrival, which CD's standard calls for whenever any pricing is not yet locked at signing (e.g., for any later-added dates or room types).
findings.cd_standard: Where future-year rates are not yet confirmed, increases should be capped at 2% per year, with a decrease if market/published rates decline, and rates fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over the rates quoted in this Agreement for any room rates not yet confirmed as of the date of this Agreement. Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.headline: No individual reservation confirmation, cancellation, or no-show terms
findings.finding_text: The contract addresses only the block cutoff date and contains no provisions on confirmation timing for individual reservations, name changes, a 6pm-day-of-arrival cancellation window, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing.
findings.cd_standard: Reservation confirmations should go out within set timeframes, name changes should be allowed at the group rate up to arrival, individual cancellation should be free until 6pm day of arrival, no-shows reinstated the following night, and individual deposits refundable with 3 days' notice.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival.

findings.headline: Damages based on gross revenue, no mitigation credit, no rebooking credit
findings.finding_text: Liquidated damages are calculated on gross room revenue rather than the 70%-lost-profit formula CD requires, the Hotel is expressly not obligated to credit resale proceeds against damages, there is no rebooking credit for a returning CD client, and the schedule's top tier (80% at 30 days or fewer) combines with the separately-stated 'no liability-free cancellation window' language to make cancellation liability apply from the moment of signature.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale of lost room profit (70% of net group rate), with active mitigation duty and credited resale proceeds, and rebooking credit if a CD client rebooks within three years.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit on the sliding scale stated in this Agreement, where one hundred percent (100%) of room profit is defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate of $189.00 at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition. Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues against the cancellation damages, not to exceed the full amount of such damages. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group cancel this Agreement in whole or in part at any time following the date of signature, Group shall be liable to the Hotel for liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled room nights. Liquidated damages shall be assessed on a sliding scale that varies according to the number of days remaining before Group's check-in date at the time cancellation notice is provided to the Hotel. In calculating liquidated damages, the Hotel shall deduct from the gross room revenue only such actual costs as are directly attributable to the cancelled rooms and demonstrably unrecoverable by the Hotel as of the cancellation date. The Hotel shall retain any revenue earned by reselling cancelled rooms to other guests, and such resale revenue shall not be credited against Group's liquidated damages obligation in any manner or to any extent. Group shall receive no credit whatsoever against damages already assessed if Group subsequently rebooks cancelled dates with the Hotel, whether at group rate or rack rate, and any such rebooking shall be treated as a new and separate reservation unrelated to Group's damages liability.
findings.exposure_basis: 275 rooms x $189 rate x 80% top-tier liquidated damages percentage as an illustrative peak-night exposure

findings.headline: No staffing ratio guarantees for servers or bartenders
findings.finding_text: The contract does not specify any minimum server-to-guest or bartender-to-guest staffing ratios for banquet functions, nor any cap on labor fees for small functions, leaving service levels entirely undefined.
findings.cd_standard: Minimum staffing should be guaranteed (1 server per 25 for plated breakfast, 20 for plated lunch/dinner, 1 per 40/30 for buffets, 1 bartender per 75 hosted/100 cash), with no labor fee except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.

findings.headline: Hotel may renovate anytime with no notice and no remedy for Group
findings.finding_text: The Hotel makes no representation about current renovation plans, may begin construction at any time including during the Event without any advance notice, and Group waives any right to terminate or claim damages for resulting disruption — squarely contrary to CD's notice, non-interference, and termination requirements.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should represent no current renovation plans affecting the group's space, commit to 30 days' notice of confirmed work with scope/schedule/mitigation, and let the group terminate without liability if it determines the work will interfere with its event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the planned scope, schedule, anticipated impact on areas Group will use, and Hotel's plan for minimizing that impact. Hotel promises that any such construction or remodeling will not interfere with Group's use of the Hotel. If Group determines the construction or remodeling will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's plans.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel makes no representation or warranty regarding the scope, timing, or nature of any construction, renovation, alteration, or maintenance work that may be planned, scheduled, or undertaken at the Hotel during the Event dates or at any other time, and Group acknowledges that such work may or may not occur and that the Hotel's plans are subject to change at the Hotel's sole discretion.
