Hotel shall have the right to commence renovation work at the Hotel at any time, including during the Event, without providing Group advance notice of any kind, and Group shall have no right to object to or restrict such work based on timing, noise, dust, disruption, or any other impact on Group's event or its attendees. Renovation work, construction, maintenance activities, or any related disruption shall not constitute grounds for Group to terminate this Agreement or claim any damages, refund, credit, abatement, or other remedy, whether based on interference with event programming, reduction in hotel amenities, diminished guest experience, or any other theory, and Group waives any claim arising from such activities.

findings.headline: No ConferenceDirect commission provision anywhere in the contract
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no clause providing for a 10% commission to ConferenceDirect on actualized room revenue, its timing, non-cancelability, survival through a change of brand/management, or commission on cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable/non-transferable, surviving brand/management change, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment or related termination right
findings.finding_text: The contract has no clause committing the Hotel and its staff to nondiscrimination against attendees, and no termination right if state or local legislation permits discrimination against attendees.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should commit to nondiscrimination against attendees on stated protected grounds, with a termination right if legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city in which Hotel is located adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.headline: No AV/internet pricing or bandwidth commitment in the contract
findings.finding_text: The contract does not attach or reference an AV or internet bandwidth quote, contains no minimum bandwidth guarantee, no discount on later AV/internet additions, and no prohibition against tying discounted internet to use of the in-house AV vendor.
findings.cd_standard: The hotel should honor attached AV/internet quotes with minimum 10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up bandwidth, a discount on later additions, and no tying of discounted internet to use of the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

clause_review.basis: CD wants pricing locked no earlier than 12 months out and only 35% of shortfall owed; this contract locks pricing for 24 months and requires payment of the full 80%-of-projection shortfall (effectively 100% of any gap below the guarantee), with no affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting toward the minimum.
Contract mandates in-house/Hotel-approved vendors only, imposing a $2,500 surcharge per outside vendor service or category rather than allowing free vendor choice at no fee.

Measured night-by-night (not cumulative), threshold is 80% (not 70%), damages are 80% of full room rate (not 70% lost profit on group rate), no credit for high-occupancy nights except 100% sellout, and Group has no audit rights and no rebooking credit.

Excuses performance only if 'physically impossible,' explicitly excludes government travel restrictions/advisories as qualifying events, has no 20% attendee-cancellation trigger, no waiver of fees for reduced-size meetings, and deposits/prepayments are forfeited entirely rather than refunded.

Hotel may assess undisclosed fees anytime post-signature and Group remains liable even if not disclosed pre-signature; resort fee of $35/night is mandatory and non-waivable, with no early check-in/bag fee protections.

Ratio is 1:80 (not 1:40), full pickup of block is a precondition (forfeited entirely on any shortfall), award is entirely discretionary, no counting of miscoded rooms or no-show/cancellation fees, and no mention of complimentary internet.
No carve-out for assignment to a successor management company/affiliated entity; all assignment requires Hotel's sole and absolute discretion with no unreasonable-withholding standard.

Indemnification is one-directional (Group indemnifies Hotel, including for Hotel's own ordinary/gross negligence), Hotel has no indemnification obligation to Group, and insurance is required of Group only, not mutual.

Termination for cause requires Group to pay full cancellation damages regardless of cause (Article 8/termination clause treats any termination as cancellation); no carve-outs for force majeure-adjacent causes, labor disputes, facility reductions, etc. triggering liability-free termination.

Notice is 90 days (not 30) before the change (rather than after), termination window is only 10 days after notice, and bankruptcy/receivership/foreclosure explicitly excluded from triggering notice or termination rights.

Deposit ($25,000) is expressly commingled and applied at Hotel's sole discretion against attrition, F&B shortfalls, damages, and other charges; refund window is 90 days, not 30, and no itemized-damage requirement for the applied portion.
No 24/12-month block review, no weekly pickup reports, and Group is expressly denied any audit right or ability to verify pickup records (Sections 2 and 24 bar review/audit entirely).

Warranty on compliance is present, but auxiliary aid costs are to be shared/negotiated rather than split with Group funding only event-space aids and Hotel funding guest room/common area aids; no mutual indemnification tied to each party's own ADA obligations is stated.

Governing law/venue is the Hotel's state and county (Indiana/Marion County), not Group's location; Hotel may recover punitive/exemplary damages and prevailing party attorney's fees rather than each side bearing its own fees with punitive damages excluded.

Clause exists but requires the warning to remain in effect as of 24 hours before arrival and requires notice by Group 24 hours before arrival — a narrower window than CD's 72-hour standard, and it only allows cancellation by Group upon a narrow definition, not either party.
Hotel is expressly permitted to use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes and to share it with affiliates/marketing partners without Group's consent.

Hotel has no obligation to provide CBA expiration notice or labor dispute notice, and Group is explicitly barred from any cancellation right or damages relief for labor disputes, strikes, or lockouts.

Gratuity and service charge are conflated (used interchangeably) at 24% combined, with Hotel having sole discretion to retain the entire amount as revenue rather than distributing to staff, and no split percentages disclosed.

No dispute window before charges are due ('no period in which Group may dispute a charge'), finance charge is 1.5% compounded monthly (exceeds CD's 1% simple cap), and no credit-denial staged-deposit schedule -- Hotel can require prepayment 'in whatever amount it determines.'

Guest bears own cost/arrangement for alternate lodging and transportation, no upgrade/amenity on return, no per-room-night rebate to Group, and relocated nights are expressly excluded from pickup/commission credit rather than credited.

Hotel has no obligation to mitigate by reselling; resale proceeds (if any) are retained entirely by Hotel with no credit against Group's damages, and Group has no audit right over mitigation efforts (Section 5).

Hotel may sell at any rate without restriction; any lower rate offered to Group applies only prospectively (no retroactive adjustment) and is treated as non-commissionable and not counted toward pickup/rebates -- contrary to CD's requirement that Group keep commission and pickup credit.

Cutoff is 45 days prior to arrival (later cutoff than CD's no-earlier-than 21-day floor is fine directionally, but CD requires no earlier than 21 days — 45 days is earlier/tighter than CD's floor, so it falls short); post-cutoff reservations get rack rate only, not group rate for as long as hotel is selling to public, and no provision for holding/refunding or consultation before release.
No provision addressing Hotel's liability if Hotel cancels the agreement without contractual right; the contract's termination provisions instead impose damages liability only on Group.
No clause identifies specific function rooms, square footage, ceiling heights, complimentary meeting space, or in-room amenities (mic, podium, power, HVAC) at no charge.
No provision addressing hotel facility/service closures or reductions, remedy, or Group's right to cancel/renegotiate if reductions occur.
Room rate for 2027 is already fixed at $189, but no cap-on-increase or rate-decline protection clause is included for any portion of rates not yet confirmed or for subsequent years.

No provisions on confirmation timing, name changes, 6pm-day-of-arrival cancellation, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing; the cutoff section only addresses the block cutoff, not individual reservation handling.

Sliding scale is based on gross room revenue (not 70% lost-profit formula), no mitigation/resale credit against damages, no rebooking credit for CD clients, and Hotel can layer this with the additional termination-for-cause damages under Section 8.
No staffing ratios for servers or bartenders, and no cap/exclusion on labor fees for small functions are specified anywhere in the contract.

Hotel makes no representation regarding current or planned renovations, may commence work anytime including during the Event with no notice, and Group has no termination or damages remedy for disruption -- directly contrary to CD's required notice, non-interference promise, and termination right.
No commission clause for ConferenceDirect appears anywhere in the contract -- no 10% commission on actualized room revenue, no timing, non-cancelability, or commission-on-damages provisions.
No nondiscrimination commitment regarding attendees, nor any termination right tied to discriminatory state/local legislation.
No AV or internet bandwidth quote-honoring provision, no discount on additions, and no prohibition tying discounted internet to use of in-house AV vendor.

analysis.document_notes: This contract is drafted overwhelmingly in the Hotel's favor and departs sharply from CD's standard positions across nearly every clause category, including several one-sided provisions (e.g., Group waiving all audit rights, Hotel retaining sole discretion over damages calculations, no-fault Hotel indemnification exclusion) that go well beyond typical negotiated deviation. Section numbering has an apparent internal inconsistency: Section 4 (Cancellation) refers to "Article 7" for service charge/tax, and Section 8 (Termination for Cause) refers to "Article 8" for the cancellation damages scale, but the cancellation damages schedule actually appears in Section 4. These cross-references appear to be drafting errors but are quoted as they appear. No exhibits (Appendix A schedule is inline as a table; Exhibit B for F&B projections referenced in Section 9 is not included in the provided text) were supplied for review, limiting verification of some referenced figures.

findings.headline: F&B shortfall pegged to room revenue, not the F&B gap itself
findings.finding_text: CD's standard requires any F&B shortfall to be billed at 35% of the difference between actual F&B revenue and the F&B minimum. This contract instead calculates the shortfall as 35% of Group's total room revenue for the event period — an entirely different (and likely far larger and less predictable) base with no logical connection to the F&B minimum itself. There is also no provision counting affiliate organization or exhibitor F&B spend toward the minimum.
findings.cd_standard: Shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap between actual F&B revenue and the stated minimum, with affiliate/exhibitor F&B spend counting toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: If the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the minimum commitment, Group shall pay the Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual food and beverage revenue and the minimum commitment, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the minimum. Payment of the shortfall is due within thirty (30) days of the Event's conclusion, and the Hotel shall provide an itemized accounting of the food and beverage revenue and the resulting shortfall calculation to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: If the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the minimum commitment, Group shall pay the shortfall amount to the Hotel. The shortfall shall be calculated as thirty-five percent (35%) of the Group's total room revenue for the Event period.
findings.exposure_basis: Shortfall base is tied to total room revenue (rate $372 x 230 rooms x multiple nights) rather than the F&B minimum gap; the F&B minimum dollar figure itself is not stated in the contract so the exact exposure cannot be calculated, but the mismatch materially inflates potential liability.

findings.headline: Mandatory in-house vendors with a $3,200 opt-out surcharge per vendor
findings.finding_text: CD's position is that Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee. This contract instead mandates use of the Hotel's in-house or exclusively-appointed vendors for AV, telecom, floral, décor, and entertainment, and imposes a $3,200 per-vendor surcharge for any Hotel-unapproved outside vendor, with the Hotel retaining unilateral discretion to decline approval.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for AV, decorating, security, floral, transportation, and similar services.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services including but not limited to audiovisual, telecommunications, floral arrangements, décor, and entertainment. Hotel's in-house or exclusively-appointed vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall engage the Hotel's in-house vendors or vendors with whom the Hotel maintains exclusive appointments for all ancillary services required in connection with the Event, including but not limited to audiovisual services, telecommunications, floral arrangements, décor, and entertainment. Any request by Group to retain an outside vendor not approved by the Hotel in writing shall be subject to a surcharge of $3,200.00 per outside vendor, which surcharge shall be payable by Group to the Hotel within ten (10) days of invoice.
findings.exposure_basis: Stated per-outside-vendor surcharge in the contract.

findings.headline: No 20% attendee-cancellation trigger and no reduced-meeting fee waiver
findings.finding_text: The clause covers many qualifying causes (terrorism, epidemics, government travel restrictions, health/safety inadvisability) but never includes the trigger for anticipated or actual cancellation by 20% or more of attendees. It also lacks any provision that if Group holds a smaller meeting instead of cancelling outright, the Hotel will waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer its lowest available rate.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should include a 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger, and if Group holds a reduced-size meeting instead of cancelling, Hotel should waive attrition, F&B, and rental fees and offer the lowest rate offered to anyone.
findings.proposed_language: Force majeure events shall also include circumstances that cause twenty percent (20%) or more of Group's attendees to cancel their attendance, or cause Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances at a reduced size, Hotel will waive any fees related to the reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental, and will offer Group's attendees any lower room rate offered to other guests over the contracted dates.
findings.quoted_text: Force majeure events shall also include conditions that render it unsafe or imprudent for meeting attendees to travel to or gather at the Hotel, whether due to health risks, infrastructure damage, or other circumstances beyond the parties' reasonable control.

findings.headline: No waiver of early check-in or checked-bag fees for attendees
findings.finding_text: Disclosure requirements and waiver of undisclosed fees are covered, and no resort fee applies, but the contract is silent on early check-in fees and checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in or departing after check-out, which CD's standard requires the Hotel to waive.
findings.cd_standard: Attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.

findings.headline: No credit for miscoded rooms, no-show fees, or complimentary internet
findings.finding_text: The 1-per-40 comp room formula is cumulative and protected from attrition reduction, which is favorable, but the contract does not provide that miscoded rooms found in an audit, or room nights represented by no-show/cancellation fees charged, count toward the pickup used for this calculation, nor does it guarantee complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: Every occupied room should count toward pickup, including miscoded rooms and no-show/cancellation fee nights, and attendees should get complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: All occupied rooms will be counted toward Group's pickup for purposes of this complimentary room calculation, including rooms credited to Group through a room block audit. Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup and used in calculating complimentary rooms. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.

findings.headline: Insurance obligation runs one-way against Group only
findings.finding_text: Indemnification is properly mutual and limited to each party's own negligence, but the insurance requirement (general liability minimum $1,000,000 with Hotel as additional insured) is imposed only on Group, with no corresponding obligation for the Hotel to carry its own insurance to protect its own activities.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will each carry adequate insurance to protect their own activities against claims arising out of the Event. Group shall maintain general liability insurance with minimum limits of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, with the Hotel named as additional insured, and shall provide certificates of insurance to the Hotel at least thirty (30) days prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall maintain general liability insurance with minimum limits of $1,000,000.00 per occurrence, with the Hotel named as additional insured, and shall provide certificates of insurance to the Hotel at least thirty (30) days prior to the Event.

findings.headline: Termination-for-cause not tied to CD's full list of no-liability triggers
findings.finding_text: Termination for cause is properly separated from the cancellation damages scale, but the Agreement never enumerates the causes CD requires as walk-away triggers with no liability — most notably it never lets Group terminate for a labor dispute without liability (the labor clause expressly says the opposite), never lets Group terminate for discriminatory legislation (no nondiscrimination clause exists), and doesn't reference facility/service reductions or unavailability of a convention center/overflow hotels as termination triggers.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should be available, without liability, for force majeure, Group's own pandemic judgment, labor disputes within 90 days, brand/ownership change, interfering renovation, facility/service reductions, unavailability of a relied-upon convention center or overflow hotels, and discriminatory state/local legislation.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) the convention center or overflow hotels on which the Event depends not being open, available, and fully operational over the Event dates; or (h) the adoption of state or local legislation that permits discrimination against attendees on any basis protected under this Agreement. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement for cause without liability to the other party. If the Hotel terminates for cause, the Hotel shall refund all deposits paid by Group within fourteen (14) days of termination. If Group terminates for cause, Group shall receive prompt refund of all deposits held by the Hotel.

findings.headline: No 24-/12-month block review, and weekly reports start later than CD standard
findings.finding_text: Post-event reporting (30 days), final documentation, and a no-cost audit right are present. But there is no provision for reviewing the room block in writing at 24 months and 12 months before arrival with a right for Group to adjust the block size, and no explicit credit for miscoded rooms at brand-associate/business rates or via internet channels. Weekly pickup reports start 8 weeks (56 days) before the event rather than the standard 60-day window, and there's no reservation-pace report requirement.
findings.cd_standard: Room block should be reviewed in writing at ~24 and ~12 months out with a set percentage adjustment right; weekly pickup reports should start 60 days before cutoff; miscoded rooms including brand-associate/business rate rooms should be credited to pickup.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival. At Group's sole discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at each review and twenty percent (20%) cumulatively, at the group rate. Beginning sixty (60) days prior to the cutoff date, the Hotel shall provide the Group with a written pickup report each week showing current room reservations, cancellations, and projected occupancy against the agreed room block. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system — including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates or through Internet distribution channels — will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.
findings.quoted_text: Beginning eight (8) weeks prior to the Event dates of April 26-29, 2027, the Hotel shall provide the Group with a written pickup report each week showing current room reservations, cancellations, and projected occupancy against the agreed room block.

findings.headline: Hotel's ADA warranty is conditioned, and indemnification isn't mutual
findings.finding_text: CD requires mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations. Here only the Hotel warrants compliance and bears remedy obligations, and that warranty is expressly conditioned on Group's timely notice — there is no reciprocal indemnification for Group's own ADA obligations (e.g., auxiliary aids it is responsible for funding).
findings.cd_standard: Each party should indemnify the other only for its own ADA obligations, with a clear division of who funds auxiliary aids in event space (Group) versus guest rooms/common areas (Hotel), unconditioned on notice for the core warranty.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other party from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA. Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's warranty of ADA compliance is conditioned upon the Group's timely notification of any accessibility needs or modifications required for the Event.

findings.headline: Hotel disclaims CBA notice, and Group stays liable despite a labor dispute
findings.finding_text: CD requires advance notice of CBA expiration and, critically, that Group be able to cancel with NO liability at all if a labor dispute arises within 90 days of the event. This contract expressly disclaims any obligation to give advance notice of CBA expirations, and although Group can cancel within 30 days of a disruption, the contract explicitly states such cancellation does not relieve Group of financial obligations under the Agreement — directly contrary to CD's no-liability standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expirations, and Group should be able to cancel with no liability at all if a labor dispute arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One (1) year in advance, or within thirty (30) days of signing this Agreement if that is later, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days after becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform, and any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel does not undertake to provide advance notice to Group regarding the expiration dates of any collective bargaining agreement to which the Hotel or its management company is a party, or of any negotiations, disputes, or other labor relations matters involving the Hotel's employees or any union or other employee representative.

findings.headline: Gratuity and service charge merged, undisclosed split, hotel keeps it all
findings.finding_text: CD requires gratuity and service charge to be separately defined and disclosed, with gratuity fully distributed to staff. This contract collapses the two into a single undefined 25% charge, expressly states the Hotel has sole discretion over allocation, may retain the entire amount as Hotel revenue with no obligation to distribute any of it to staff, and admits the Agreement does not disclose the staff/hotel split.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be separately defined with both percentages confirmed; gratuity should be fully distributed to staff, and any service charge disclosed as Hotel revenue rather than left ambiguous.
findings.proposed_language: Eighteen percent (18%) of the food and beverage total, plus applicable tax, will be added to Group's account as a gratuity and fully distributed to the servers, and where applicable, bussers and bartenders assigned to the Event. A separate service charge of seven percent (7%), plus applicable tax, is not distributed as a tip and is retained by Hotel to cover the discretionary costs of the Event. Both percentages are confirmed in this Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains sole discretion to determine the allocation and distribution of any gratuity collected on behalf of Group, and the Hotel may retain such gratuity as Hotel revenue without obligation to distribute it to service staff. The Hotel is not required to use gratuity amounts for tip pooling, staff bonuses, or any other specific purpose, and gratuity collected shall be the property of the Hotel.

findings.headline: Finance charge doubles CD's cap and dispute window is far too short
findings.finding_text: CD caps late-payment finance charges at 1% per month (or legal max, whichever is less) and requires a genuine 30-day dispute window before charges apply. This contract charges 2% per month, compounded, and deems any invoice not disputed within just 7 days as final and binding. It also requires a flat 50% prepayment if credit is denied, rather than CD's staged 25%/25%/50% schedule.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge should be capped at 1%/month or legal maximum, whichever is less, with a 30-day dispute window; if credit is denied, Group should pay on a staged 25%/25%/50% schedule.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of each invoice to notify the Hotel in writing of any disputed charges; invoices not disputed within this thirty (30) day window shall be deemed accepted by Group. Any amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date shall accrue a monthly finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, on the outstanding undisputed balance. In the event credit approval cannot be granted to Group, Group will pay twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days before the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have seven (7) days from receipt of each invoice to notify the Hotel in writing of any disputed charges; invoices not disputed within this seven (7) day window shall be deemed accepted by Group and shall be final and binding.

findings.headline: No per-room-night rebate, do-not-walk list, or penalty for mass walks
findings.finding_text: Relocation terms cover comparable/superior lodging, transportation, message handling by omission, upgrade, and a $50/night amenity, and pickup/commission credit, which is favorable. But the contract omits a per-room-night master account rebate to Group (CD standard: $200/night), omits any do-not-walk list mechanism or requirement that transient guests/other groups be walked first, and includes no additional compensation trigger if the Hotel walks 10 or more guests or 10% or more of the peak night block.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should trigger a per-room-night rebate to Group (e.g. $200), a do-not-walk list, walking Group only after transient/other groups, and additional compensation for walking 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak block.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall contact Group in advance of any relocation, shall not walk members of Group before transient guests and other groups, and will review Group's attendee list with Group to identify those who cannot be walked under any circumstances. Hotel will credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated, regardless of that guest's rate. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: In the event the Hotel is unable to provide accommodations to any Group member holding a guaranteed reservation due to an operational, maintenance, or occupancy situation, the Hotel shall secure alternative accommodations at a comparable or superior hotel within the San Francisco metropolitan area at the Hotel's sole cost and expense.

findings.headline: Cancellation damages not conditioned on payment timing tied to mitigation proof
findings.finding_text: The Hotel has a genuine mitigation duty, keeps records, and credits proceeds, meeting most of CD's standard. But CD's position also requires cancellation damages not to fall due until 30 days after the event dates and only once the Hotel demonstrates its mitigation effort and that the space went unsold — this contract's cancellation clause (Section 4) does not tie the payment due date to the demonstration of mitigation evidence as a precondition.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should not fall due until 30 days after the meeting dates, and only once the Hotel shows reasonable evidence of mitigation effort and that rooms/space went unsold.
findings.proposed_language: Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the Event dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.location_section: 5. Resale of Released Inventory / 4. Cancellation and Liquidated Damages

findings.headline: No rate-parity protection for the days surrounding the event
findings.finding_text: Rate parity, retroactive adjustment, and preserved commission/pickup credit during the event dates are all present and strong. But CD's standard also requires Group's rate be no higher than any other group's rate for 7 days before and after the block dates, which this contract does not address.
findings.cd_standard: Group's rate should also be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days either side of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel further agrees that Group's rate will be no higher than the group rate given to any other group over the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the room block dates.

findings.headline: Cutoff set at 30 days, block released in full, no post-cutoff group rate
findings.finding_text: CD requires a cutoff no earlier than 21 days before arrival; this contract sets it at 30 days. Worse, the footer states the room block is released in full at cutoff, with no continuing group rate for as long as the Hotel sells to the public, and no prepayment-hold or consult-before-resale mechanism for unassigned rooms as CD's standard requires.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, with continuing group-rate access after cutoff and a hold/refund or consult-before-resale mechanism for unassigned rooms.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to hold any rooms in Group's block not assigned to a specific attendee if Group pays for them in full at that time, and will refund those advance payments after the Event for any such rooms later paid for by Group attendees; alternatively, after consultation with Group, Hotel will offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause. Group members may continue to reserve rooms at the group rate for as long as Hotel is selling rooms to the general public, regardless of room type; once the room block has sold, Hotel will honor the group rate for as long as it is selling the contracted room type to the general public.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the Block must be submitted no later than thirty (30) days prior to the arrival date of April 26, 2027, unless a later deadline is expressly agreed in writing by the Hotel.

findings.headline: No remedy stated if Hotel cancels without contractual right to do so
findings.finding_text: The contract addresses termination for cause by either party and force majeure, but nowhere addresses the scenario where the Hotel simply cancels the Agreement without a contractual right to do so. CD's standard requires the Hotel to be liable for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages in that scenario, not merely a refund of deposits.
findings.cd_standard: If the Hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe Group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, including costs of finding a new venue, rate/airfare differentials, function space rental, attorney's fees, and communication/printing costs.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel cancels this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such cancellation, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs.

findings.headline: No function space assignments, square footage, or complimentary meeting room terms
findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no clause naming function rooms, specifying minimum square footage or ceiling height, restricting changes to space assignments without written consent, providing meeting space complimentary with rental waived, or guaranteeing standard in-room amenities (mic, podium, power, lighting, HVAC) at no charge.
findings.cd_standard: Function space should be named with minimum square footage and ceiling height, changes require both parties' written consent, meeting space should be complimentary with rental waived, and each room should include a wired mic, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in this Agreement, with room rental charges waived, and will specify each function space assignment, minimum square footage, and ceiling height requirement in this Agreement. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power (including existing power outlets), proper lighting, and HVAC.

findings.headline: No protection if hotel reduces facilities, services, or staffing levels
findings.finding_text: There is no clause addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or materially limits restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, contracted meeting space, or reduces staffing ratios for housekeeping, food service, banquets, engineering, or security — nor any right for Group to cancel or renegotiate if no alternative is reached.
findings.cd_standard: If the Hotel closes or limits facilities/services by more than 25%, or materially reduces staffing ratios, it should first offer equal alternatives at its own expense; absent resolution within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or limits, restricts, or reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, safety and security, or any other service in a manner a hotel industry executive would agree is material, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services, mutually agreeable and solely at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to Hotel, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.headline: No protection against rate increases or market rate declines before arrival
findings.finding_text: While the group rate is stated as a fixed $372, there is no provision capping any later increase to that rate, no mechanism to lower the rate if the market average or the Hotel's own published rate declines before arrival, and no commitment on when rates would be finalized in writing — protections CD's standard calls for whenever a rate isn't locked in as fully guaranteed against later adjustment.
findings.cd_standard: Rate increases should be capped at 2%/year over quoted rates, the group rate should decrease if market/published rates decline before arrival, and final rates should be fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over the rates quoted in this Agreement. Should the market average rate for same-tier hotels, or Hotel's published transient rate over the same pattern, decline between the signing of this Agreement and Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.headline: No individual reservation, no-show, or name-change protections stated
findings.finding_text: The contract is silent on confirmation timing for individual reservations, name changes at the group rate up to arrival, a no-charge cancellation window until 6pm on arrival day, no-show reinstatement at the same rate, individual deposit refund timing, and crediting of individual cancellation money against Group's attrition liability.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days), free name changes up to arrival, no-charge cancellation until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement, 3-day deposit refund window, and individual cancellation money credited against attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.headline: Rebooking credit window is only 1 year, and rate condition added
findings.finding_text: CD's standard calls for a 3-year rebooking credit window with no rate qualifier. This contract limits the rebooking credit to bookings within only one year of the original event, and adds a condition forfeiting the credit if the new event's rate is materially below market, an extra condition not found in CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Damages paid should be credited back if a ConferenceDirect client rebooks the hotel within 3 years, without additional rate conditions.
findings.proposed_language: If Group books another event at the Hotel within three (3) years following the original Event dates, the revenue earned by the Hotel from such rebooking shall be credited against the damages paid pursuant to this clause, up to 100% of the damages paid, applied first against any remaining balance owed.
findings.quoted_text: If Group books another event at the Hotel within a year following the original Event dates, the revenue earned by the Hotel from such rebooking shall be credited against the damages paid pursuant to this clause, applied first against any remaining balance owed. Group shall forfeit the right to rebooking credit if the new event is booked at a rate materially lower than market rate for the applicable dates.

findings.headline: No minimum server or bartender staffing ratios guaranteed
findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no guarantee of minimum server-to-guest ratios for plated or buffet meals, no minimum bartender-to-guest ratios for hosted or cash bars, and no cap limiting labor fees to only functions under 25 guests.
findings.cd_standard: One server per 25 (plated breakfast) / 20 (plated lunch/dinner) guests, one per 40/30 for buffets, one bartender per 75 (hosted)/100 (cash) guests, with no labor fee except for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.

findings.headline: Hotel disclaims renovation assurance and gives short notice/response windows
findings.finding_text: CD requires the Hotel to represent it has no current plans affecting Group's space, promise future work won't interfere, give 30 days' written notice with scope/schedule/mitigation detail, and give Group 30 days to terminate. Here the Hotel affirmatively disclaims any warranty or representation about construction, gives only 14 days' notice of interference, and Group has only 7 days to terminate after receiving notice. There is also no separate new-build/reopening provision (operational date commitment, 5-day change notice, damages if no alternative venue).
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans, commit that future work won't interfere, give 30 days' notice with mitigation detail, and give Group 30 days to terminate without liability; new-build/reopening scenarios need their own operational-date and damages protections.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the planned scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and Hotel's mitigation plan. Hotel promises that any such construction or remodeling will not interfere with Group's use of the Hotel. If Group determines the construction or remodeling will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's notice.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no warranty, representation, or undertaking with respect to any construction, renovation, alteration, or other work that may be planned or under way at the Hotel during the event dates. Group acknowledges that the Hotel's operations may be subject to such work at any time, and Group has not relied on any promise from the Hotel concerning the absence or scheduling of such work.

findings.headline: No commission provision for ConferenceDirect anywhere in the contract
findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no clause obligating the Hotel to pay ConferenceDirect commission on actualized room revenue, addressing timing, rate applicability, survivability through brand/management change, or commission on cancellation damages collected.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, non-cancelable/non-transferable, surviving brand/management changes, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable to another party or agency. Should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment or related termination right
findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no clause committing the Hotel or its staff to nondiscrimination against attendees on protected grounds, and no right for Group to terminate without liability if the state or city adopts legislation permitting such discrimination.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should commit to nondiscrimination against attendees on a broad list of protected grounds, with a termination right for Group if discriminatory legislation is adopted.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city in which Hotel is located adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, or prohibits the adoption of nondiscrimination measures on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.headline: No AV/internet quote lock, bandwidth minimum, or discount for additions
findings.finding_text: The Agreement contains no clause honoring any AV quote, guaranteeing minimum internet bandwidth (10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up), providing a discount on additional AV/internet needs, or barring use of the in-house AV provider as a condition of discounted or complimentary internet.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should honor attached AV/internet quotes with a 10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up bandwidth minimum, apply a discount to additions, and never condition discounted/complimentary internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of twenty percent (20%) to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of twenty percent (20%) on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

clause_review.basis: CD requires shortfall billed at 35% of the gap between actual F&B revenue and the minimum, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue to count toward the minimum. Here the shortfall is calculated as 35% of total room revenue (not F&B revenue gap), which is a fundamentally different and likely much larger number, and there's no affiliate/exhibitor credit provision.
CD requires the group be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee. Contract mandates in-house/exclusive vendors and imposes a $3,200 per-vendor surcharge for using an outside vendor.
Cumulative measurement, 70% threshold, 70% of ADR for shortfall, 95% occupancy credit, and audit rights are all present and align with CD's position.

CD requires either party to invoke FM for a broad list including inadvisability/health-safety and 20% attendee cancellation threshold, plus a waiver of fees if a smaller meeting is held instead and prompt deposit refund. Contract covers most triggers and impossibility/impracticability/illegality but omits the 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger, omits the reduced-meeting fee waiver/rate accommodation, and disclaims consequential damages broadly but doesn't specify refund timing beyond 'promptly'.
Disclosure and waiver-if-undisclosed requirements are met, and no resort fee is charged. However, there is no provision addressing early check-in or checked-bag fee waivers for attendees.

One comp room per 40 formula is present and doesn't get reduced by attrition, meeting most of CD's position, but the contract doesn't address crediting miscoded rooms or no-show/cancellation fee nights toward pickup, nor complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
Group may assign to successor/affiliated entity with assignee assuming obligations, and Hotel consent not unreasonably withheld for other assignments.

Indemnification is mutual and limited to own negligence, matching CD's position, but insurance is imposed only on Group ($1M GL, Hotel as additional insured) with no reciprocal insurance obligation on Hotel.

Termination for cause exists and is separate from cancellation damages, but the contract doesn't enumerate the required causes (epidemic/pandemic by Group's own judgment, labor dispute, brand/ownership change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) as termination-for-cause triggers tied to no-liability walk-away; several of these are handled in separate clauses with their own (sometimes narrower) terms rather than as unified termination-for-cause rights, and nondiscrimination legislation termination right is entirely missing.
30-day hotel notice and 30-day group termination window with refund are present, matching CD's position.
No security deposit required; damage charges separately documented/invoiced and not commingled with attrition or F&B minimum shortfalls.

Weekly pickup reports start 8 weeks out (CD wants 60 days, roughly similar) and post-event report and no-cost audit are present, but there is no 24-month/12-month block review with right to adjust the block up/down, and no explicit crediting of miscoded rooms at brand-associate/business rates.

Hotel warrants ADA compliance and cost allocation is addressed, but the warranty is conditioned on Group's timely notice of accessibility needs, and there's no mutual indemnification for each party's own ADA obligations (only a unilateral hotel warranty/remedy obligation).
Governed by law and venue of Group's principal-office state, no punitive damages, each party bears own attorney's fees.
Named storm clause exists with 72-hour notice window and cancellation right, deposit refund within 10 business days.
Hotel barred from using attendee data for its own marketing and from selling/sharing with third parties without consent.

CD requires advance notice of CBA expiration dates and that a labor dispute within 90 days lets Group cancel with NO liability at all. Contract explicitly disclaims any advance CBA notice obligation and states cancellation for labor disruption does NOT relieve Group of financial obligations, contradicting CD's no-liability requirement.

CD requires gratuity and service charge be separately defined with percentages disclosed and gratuity distributed to staff. Contract merges the two into one undefined 25% charge, explicitly reserves full discretion to the Hotel to retain it as revenue with no obligation to distribute to staff, and does not disclose the staff/hotel revenue split.

CD caps finance charges at 1%/month; contract charges 2%/month compounded. CD requires a real dispute window before finance charges apply (30 days) and a 25/25/50 staged deposit schedule if credit denied; contract gives only 7 days to dispute invoices (deemed accepted after) and requires a flat 50% prepayment if credit is denied rather than the staged schedule.

Relocation terms (comparable/superior hotel, transportation, upgrade, $50 amenity, pickup/commission credit) are largely present and generous, but there is no per-room-night rebate to Group's master account, no do-not-walk list mechanism, no explicit hotel-contact-in-advance/walk-order-priority requirement, and no additional compensation trigger for walking 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak night.

Hotel has a real mitigation duty with records and dollar-for-dollar credit, largely meeting CD's position, but cancellation damages are due at the schedule in Exhibit A without a stated 30-days-after-event due date tied to demonstrated mitigation evidence as a precondition to payment.

Rate parity, retroactive adjustment, and preserved commission/pickup credit are all present, meeting most of CD's position, but there is no requirement that Group's rate be no higher than any other group's rate within 7 days before/after the event dates.

CD requires cutoff no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival; this contract sets cutoff at 30 days prior to arrival, and after cutoff the room block is released in full (per footer) rather than continuing to honor the group rate for as long as the hotel sells to the public, and there's no prepayment-hold or resale-after-consultation mechanism for unassigned rooms.

No clause addresses the Hotel's liability if it cancels the Agreement without a contractual right to do so; only 'termination for cause' by either party is addressed, with no provision for consequential/direct damages owed by Hotel for a wrongful hotel cancellation.
No clause names function rooms, minimum square footage, ceiling heights, complimentary meeting space with rental waived, or in-room amenities (mic, podium, power, lighting, HVAC).
No clause addresses closure or limitation of hotel facilities/services (restaurants, spa, staffing ratios) or Group's right to cancel/renegotiate if no alternative is reached.

Room rate for the single contracted year is fixed at $372; no clause addresses a rate cap or decrease mechanism for a future/undetermined year's rate, since this appears to be a single-year booking; however CD's standard calls for this to be addressed regardless when rates are not yet confirmed — here rates are already confirmed, but no fallback protection for a rate not yet fixed is present, and no clause exists at all.

No provisions found on confirmation timing (4 days/2 business days), name changes, cancellation without charge until 6pm day of arrival, no-show reinstatement, individual deposit refund timing (3 working days), or crediting individual cancellation money against attrition.

Sliding scale, mitigation/resale credit, and rebooking credit are present, largely matching CD's position, but the rebooking credit is limited to only 1 year (CD wants 3 years) and forfeits the credit if the new event's rate is 'materially lower than market' — an extra condition CD's standard doesn't impose — and damages are based on ADR generally rather than expressly stated as the group's single net rate multiplied by block less allowable attrition.
No clause addresses minimum server-to-guest or bartender-to-guest ratios, or labor fee thresholds for small functions.

Contract disclaims any warranty of no current renovation plans (opposite of CD's position), gives only 14 days' notice (not 30) if interference is determined, gives Group only 7 days (not 30) to terminate after notice, and contains no separate provisions for a new-build/reopening scenario (operational date commitment, 5-business-day change notice, damages if no alternative venue found).
No commission clause appears anywhere in the contract addressing payment of commission to ConferenceDirect on room revenue.
No clause commits the Hotel or its staff to nondiscrimination against attendees, nor a termination right if discriminatory legislation is adopted.
No clause addresses honoring AV/internet quotes, bandwidth minimums, discount on additions, or barring in-house AV as a condition of discounted/complimentary internet.

analysis.document_notes: The contract references an "Exhibit A" containing the cancellation liquidated-damages schedule, which is reproduced as a table in the body text; no separate exhibit document was supplied for independent verification. The F&B minimum dollar amount is referenced as being provided in a "menu and pricing statement" but that statement was not included in the text provided, so the actual minimum dollar figure and full F&B pricing terms could not be verified. No exhibits or addenda beyond the main body were supplied.

findings.headline: Group pays full F&B shortfall instead of a fraction
findings.finding_text: The contract requires Group to pay the entire gap between actual F&B spend and the minimum ('a shortfall fee equal to the difference'), rather than a fraction of the shortfall. It is also silent on whether affiliate organization or exhibitor F&B revenue counts toward the minimum, which would help Group meet it.
findings.cd_standard: Any shortfall should be billed at a fraction (CD uses 35%) of the gap, not dollar-for-dollar, and affiliate/exhibitor F&B revenue should count toward the minimum.
findings.proposed_language: Should the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the Minimum F&B Commitment, the Group shall pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between the Minimum F&B Commitment and actual charges incurred, not the full shortfall. Food and beverage revenue from all affiliate organizations and exhibitors meeting in conjunction with Group's event will count toward the Minimum F&B Commitment.
findings.quoted_text: Should the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the Minimum F&B Commitment, the Group shall be obligated to pay the Hotel a shortfall fee equal to the difference between the Minimum F&B Commitment and the actual charges incurred.

findings.headline: Night-by-night measurement with 85% trigger, no rebooking credit-back
findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, the liability trigger is 85% pickup rather than the 70% CD standard, the no-liability occupancy threshold is set at 100% rather than 95%, and there is no provision crediting attrition damages back if a ConferenceDirect client rebooks the hotel within three years. Night-by-night measurement plus an 85% threshold materially increases Group's attrition exposure across a 465-room, 5-night block.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively, triggered only below 70% of the block, with full credit for any night at 95%+ occupancy, and damages paid should be credited back on a CD-client rebooking within three years.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For any night the Hotel achieves ninety-five percent (95%) occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the attrition damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid; if the rebooking group is not the group that paid, the credit will be refunded directly to the group that paid.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis and applies to the total room nights committed by Group under this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: 465-room block over 5 nights at $279/night group rate; precise exposure depends on actual pickup shortfall which is not yet known.

findings.headline: Force majeure requires actual impossibility, excludes safety concerns
findings.finding_text: The clause requires performance to be 'physically impossible,' a far narrower standard than CD's requirement of illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable including for health/safety reasons. It explicitly excludes attendee safety concerns and reluctance to travel absent a specific government order, and has no 20%-attendee-cancellation trigger. There is no provision waiving attrition/F&B/rental fees if Group holds a reduced-size meeting instead of canceling, and the refund is reduced by the Hotel's own documented costs rather than being a prompt full refund.
findings.cd_standard: Either party should be able to cancel without liability when a cause makes performance illegal, impossible, commercially impracticable, or inadvisable (including health/safety reasons) or leads to 20%+ attendee cancellations; safety concerns should qualify; deposits should be refunded promptly and in full.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to the other party should any cause beyond the control of Hotel or Group — including acts of God, war, terrorism, civil unrest, government-imposed travel restrictions and advisories, epidemics and pandemics, natural disasters, utility failures, and transportation disruptions — in that party's reasonable judgment make it commercially impracticable, inadvisable (including from a health or safety standpoint), illegal, or impossible to perform, or cause or lead Group to reasonably anticipate that twenty percent (20%) or more of its attendees will cancel their attendance. If Group elects to hold the Event despite such circumstances at reduced size, Hotel will waive any fees related to a reduced-size Event, including room and food and beverage attrition and function space rental. In the event this Agreement is terminated in its entirety by either party on account of force majeure, the Hotel shall promptly refund to Group any deposits or prepayments received in full within thirty (30) calendar days of the force majeure event that grounds the termination.
findings.quoted_text: Neither party shall be liable for failure or delay in performance under this Agreement when such failure or delay results from causes beyond the reasonable control of that party, provided that performance has become physically impossible as a direct result of such cause and not merely more difficult, costly, or inconvenient.

findings.headline: Attendee safety concerns are expressly excluded from force majeure
findings.finding_text: The contract expressly carves out attendee safety concerns and reluctance to travel as non-qualifying, requiring an actual governmental restriction directed at the hotel's or attendees' location. CD's position requires that inadvisability for health or safety reasons qualify on its own.
findings.cd_standard: Qualifying causes should include inadvisability including for health or safety reasons, without requiring a specific government order.
findings.proposed_language: Concerns regarding attendee safety, including a party's reasonable judgment that performance is inadvisable from a health or safety standpoint, shall constitute a force majeure event and shall excuse the affected party's performance, whether or not accompanied by an actual governmental restriction or specific order.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the above, concerns regarding attendee safety or the unwillingness or reluctance of attendees to travel, in the absence of an actual governmental restriction or specific order directed at the Hotel's location or at the attendees' originating location, shall not constitute a force majeure event and shall not excuse the Group's performance or obligation to pay.

findings.headline: Resort fee not waived, and hotel can add fees after signing
findings.finding_text: The contract discloses a $26/night resort fee but does not waive it for attendees as CD requires (or offer a discounted/fixed alternative), and is silent on early check-in and checked-bag fees. It also opens by allowing the Hotel to add new fees and surcharges after execution at its sole discretion without Group's written approval, directly contradicting the later sentence waiving undisclosed charges.
findings.cd_standard: Resort fees should be waived for attendees (services still honored) or discounted/fixed; attendees should not pay early check-in or checked-bag fees; post-signature add-ons require Group's written approval before being charged.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel may not introduce additional fees, surcharges, or service charges after this Agreement is executed without Group's prior written approval, and no such charge will be posted to the master account without that approval. Any charge or surcharge not specifically disclosed in writing to Group prior to the execution of this Agreement is waived. Hotel will waive the nightly resort fee of $26.00 per room for all attendees while continuing to honor the resort fee services. Hotel will not charge attendees an early check-in fee when their room type is available, and will waive checked-bag fees for attendees arriving before check-in time or departing after check-out time.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel may, at its sole discretion and without prior notice to Group, introduce additional fees, surcharges, and service charges after this Agreement is executed, and all such charges shall be binding upon Group as modifications to the schedule of fees set forth herein.
findings.exposure_basis: Undiscounted resort fee of $26/room/night across the block if not waived.

findings.headline: No-show/cancellation fees and internet access not addressed in comp room formula
findings.finding_text: While the 1-per-40 complimentary room ratio itself meets CD's standard, the contract does not credit no-show or cancellation fees charged to Group as room nights toward the complimentary room count, and does not guarantee complimentary in-room internet for attendees regardless of loyalty status.
findings.cd_standard: Every occupied room, plus one room night for each no-show or cancellation fee charged, should count toward pickup for rebate purposes, and attendees should receive complimentary in-room internet regardless of loyalty status.
findings.proposed_language: Each no-show fee and each cancellation fee charged will be credited as one (1) room night toward Group's pickup and used in calculating complimentary rooms. Hotel will provide complimentary internet in attendees' guest rooms, regardless of brand loyalty program participation.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive complimentary room credit accruing at the ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) paid rooms reserved and occupied by Group attendees during the Event Period of August 2-7, 2027.

findings.headline: Only Group must carry insurance; Hotel has no matching obligation
findings.finding_text: The indemnification language is appropriately mutual, but the insurance obligation runs one way: only Group is required to obtain and maintain $3,000,000 general liability coverage naming Hotel as additional insured. CD requires each party to carry adequate insurance to protect its own activities.
findings.cd_standard: Insurance should be a mutual obligation, with each party carrying adequate insurance to protect its own activities, not a requirement imposed on Group alone.
findings.proposed_language: The Group shall obtain and maintain, at its own expense, comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of $3,000,000.00 per occurrence and $3,000,000.00 in the aggregate, naming the Hotel as an additional insured. The Hotel shall likewise obtain and maintain, at its own expense, comprehensive general liability insurance adequate to protect its own activities against claims arising out of the Event. All insurance policies shall be issued by carriers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best and shall be primary and non-contributory to any insurance carried by the other party. Each party shall provide certificates of insurance to the other at least thirty (30) days before the event.
findings.quoted_text: The Group shall obtain and maintain, at its own expense, comprehensive general liability insurance with a minimum limit of $3,000,000.00 per occurrence and $3,000,000.00 in the aggregate, naming the Hotel as an additional insured.

findings.headline: No consolidated group termination right covering CD's standard causes
findings.finding_text: The contract's only 'Termination for Cause' provision (Section 8) is a unilateral hotel right to terminate at its sole discretion, not a Group right. While several individual causes are scattered elsewhere (force majeure, brand change, labor disputes, construction), the contract lacks a consolidated Group termination right covering a pandemic determination by Group itself, convention center/overflow hotel unavailability, and discriminatory state/local legislation, each triggering termination without liability and separate from the cancellation damages schedule.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability for force majeure, Group's own pandemic determination, labor disputes, ownership/brand change, renovation interference, facility/service reductions, unavailability of a relied-upon convention center/overflow hotels, or discriminatory legislation — entirely separate from the cancellation damages schedule.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) days, upon any of the following: (a) force majeure as defined in this Agreement; (b) Group's determination that an infectious disease outbreak, epidemic, or pandemic is affecting Group's ability to hold the Event as intended; (c) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within ninety (90) days of or during the Event; (d) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or Hotel's bankruptcy or foreclosure; (e) renovation or remodeling that Group determines will interfere with its meeting; (f) a reduction in Hotel's facilities or services for which no mutually agreeable alternative is reached within thirty (30) days; (g) any convention center or overflow hotel on which the Event depends not being open, available, and fully operational over the Event dates; or (h) the adoption of state or local legislation that permits discrimination against attendees on any protected basis. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the Cancellation clause.

findings.headline: Deposit refund window is 45 days, exceeding the 30-day standard
findings.finding_text: The deposit is correctly restricted to documented damage only, but the refund window for unused amounts is 45 days after checkout rather than the 30 days CD's standard calls for.
findings.cd_standard: Any unapplied deposit should be refunded within 30 days absent documented, itemized damage.
findings.proposed_language: Any portion of the deposit not applied to documented damage claims shall be refunded to Group within thirty (30) days of Group's final checkout, provided all rooms have been inspected and the master account has been reconciled.
findings.quoted_text: Any portion of the deposit not applied to documented damage claims shall be refunded to Group within forty-five (45) days of Group's final checkout, provided all rooms have been inspected and the master account has been reconciled.
findings.exposure_basis: Full $30,000 security deposit subject to the extended 45-day hold.

findings.headline: No 24/12-month block review, no final report within 10 days of departure
findings.finding_text: The contract provides weekly pickup reports starting 12 weeks out and a 30-day post-event report, but has no mechanism for Group to review and adjust the block size at 24 and 12 months prior to arrival, no requirement for a final pickup report with supporting documentation within 10 days of departure, and the audit clause doesn't address crediting miscoded rooms (including brand-associate or business rate bookings) to Group's pickup.
findings.cd_standard: Room block should be reviewed at 24 and 12 months with adjustment rights; final pickup reports with documentation due within 10 days of departure; audit should credit miscoded rooms, including brand-associate/business rate bookings, to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel and Group will review the room block in writing twenty-four (24) months prior to arrival and again twelve (12) months prior to arrival; at Group's sole discretion, Group may increase or decrease the room block by up to ten percent (10%) at each review at the group rate.
