Hotel will provide Group final room pickup reports with supporting documentation within ten (10) days of departure, in addition to the post-event report described below. Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system — including rooms booked at qualified brand-associate or business rates — will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of the rate paid or reservation method.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have the right to conduct an audit of the room block records and reservations maintained by the Hotel at Group's sole cost and expense, without charge to the Hotel.

findings.headline: Auxiliary aid cost split is vague, not divided by space type
findings.finding_text: The clause splits auxiliary aid costs 'in accordance with the parties' respective legal obligations' and ties Hotel's share only to 'facilities and operations' rather than clearly assigning event/function-space aids to Group and guest room/common area aids to Hotel as CD's standard requires, and does not include mutual ADA indemnification.
findings.cd_standard: Group should fund auxiliary aids in event/function space; Hotel should fund auxiliary aids in guest rooms and common areas; each party should indemnify the other only for its own ADA obligations.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid and accessible-guest-room needs to the other in advance. Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA.
findings.quoted_text: To the extent that the Group's event requires auxiliary aids or services, including but not limited to sign language interpreters, real-time captioning, accessible transportation, or specialized technology, the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be shared between the Hotel and the Group in accordance with the parties' respective legal obligations under applicable accessibility law.

findings.headline: Cancellation right voided if hotel says it can still perform
findings.finding_text: CD's standard gives Group an unconditional cancellation right if a strike, lockout, or expired CBA arises within 90 days of the event, regardless of the hotel's ability to perform. This contract instead voids Group's cancellation right if the Hotel determines full services will be available, and further conditions the right on the dispute 'materially affecting' services essential to the event.
findings.cd_standard: If a strike, lockout, or expired contract with union employees arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability regardless of whether Hotel can still perform.
findings.proposed_language: Should a labor dispute, strike, lockout, work stoppage, or material labor disruption occur at the Hotel, or should negotiations for renewal of a collective bargaining agreement result in an existing or impending strike or lockout, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform. Any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: Group's right to cancel without liability under this clause shall not apply if the labor dispute is resolved to the satisfaction of Group and the Hotel determines that full Hotel services will be available for the Event dates, and Group shall have had a reasonable opportunity to assess the impact of any labor action.

findings.headline: Finance charge set above the 1% cap, and prepayment percentage left undefined
findings.finding_text: The contract sets a 1.5% monthly finance charge on unpaid balances, above CD's 1%-or-legal-maximum cap, and compounds monthly. It also leaves the prepayment percentage for non-credit-approved groups to the Hotel's unilateral designation rather than the defined staged schedule (or a fixed percentage) CD's standard requires.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge should be capped at 1% per month or the legal maximum, whichever is less; non-credit groups should pay a defined staged schedule (e.g., 25%/25%/50%) rather than an open-ended, hotel-designated percentage.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group fail to pay any undisputed invoice balance in full by the due date specified on the invoice, the Hotel shall assess a finance charge of one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower, calculated on the unpaid, undisputed balance. Where Group has not been approved for credit terms, Group shall remit twenty-five percent (25%) of estimated charges within fourteen (14) business days of the credit denial, twenty-five percent (25%) one (1) month prior to the Event, and fifty percent (50%) three (3) days prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to pay any undisputed invoice balance in full by the due date specified on the invoice, the Hotel shall assess a finance charge of 1.5% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower, calculated on the unpaid principal balance and compounded monthly until payment is received in full.

findings.headline: No upgrade, no per-night rebate, no pickup credit for walked guests
findings.finding_text: The contract affirmatively denies several protections CD's standard requires: it explicitly states relocated guests get no upgrade and no complimentary amenities on return, no rebate is paid to Group, and relocated nights are expressly excluded from room pickup, commission eligibility, and future rate negotiation. There is also no additional-compensation trigger if 10 or more guests, or 10%+ of peak-night block, are walked.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive an upgrade and welcome amenity on return; Group should receive a per-room-night rebate; relocated nights should count toward pickup and commission with no attrition liability for those nights; additional compensation should apply if 10+ guests or 10%+ of peak-night block are walked.
findings.proposed_language: When the guest returns, the Hotel will provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity from the General Manager. Hotel will credit Group's master account $200 for each night a guest is relocated, regardless of that guest's rate. The relocated night or nights shall be credited toward Group's room pickup, commission eligibility, and attrition calculations under this Agreement, and Group shall not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is walked. If Hotel walks ten (10) or more guests, or ten percent (10%) or more of the contracted peak-night block, Hotel will owe Group reasonable additional compensation.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the Hotel's provision of alternative accommodation and transportation, the relocated guest shall return to the Vantage Point Hotel and Convention Center in a standard room assignment of the original booked category, with no room upgrade, no complimentary amenities beyond those included in the original rate agreement, and no additional services or concessions as compensation for the relocation. The relocated night or nights shall not be credited toward Group's room pickup for purposes of calculating minimum room guarantees, commission eligibility, or future rate negotiation under this Agreement or any successor agreement.

findings.headline: Hotel's resale records are shielded from Group's review entirely
findings.finding_text: Section 5 explicitly states the Hotel's resale efforts, pricing decisions, and related records 'shall not be subject to disclosure to Group, audit by Group, or review by Group's representatives,' which directly conflicts with CD's requirement that mitigation records be available to Group to verify the effort actually happened. Additionally, cancellation damages are due 30 days after Hotel's own calculation rather than being contingent on Hotel showing evidence of mitigation and that space went unsold.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have a documented duty to mitigate with records available to Group to verify the effort, and damages should not fall due until Hotel shows reasonable evidence of mitigation and that rooms/space went unsold.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, and pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation, shall be made available to Group upon request to verify the Hotel's mitigation efforts. Cancellation damages, if any, are due thirty (30) days after the meeting dates, provided Hotel supplies reasonable evidence of its mitigation efforts and that the rooms and space held for Group went unsold.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation shall remain the sole property and responsibility of the Hotel and shall not be subject to disclosure to Group, audit by Group, or review by Group's representatives.

findings.headline: Lower rates found aren't applied retroactively, and no 7-day buffer
findings.finding_text: The rate parity guarantee only covers the Event Period itself and explicitly bars retroactive application of a discovered lower rate to reservations already confirmed. CD's standard requires either retroactive adjustment for prior reservations or full block-wide crediting, plus parity extending 7 days before and after the block dates.
findings.cd_standard: If a lower rate is found, Group's rate should be adjusted retroactively for reservations already made, or the group should get pickup/commission credit on all rooms; parity should also extend 7 days before and after the event.
findings.proposed_language: In the event the Hotel identifies or discovers that a lower rate has been offered or made available to the general public or any third party during the period from seven (7) days before through seven (7) days after the Event Period, the Hotel shall adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees, retroactively as well as prospectively.
findings.quoted_text: Any rate adjustment or modification resulting from such discovery shall apply only to reservations made after the lower rate is identified and communicated to Group in writing, and shall not apply retroactively to any reservations confirmed prior to such identification.

findings.headline: Cutoff set at 40 days, nearly double the 21-day standard
findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 40 days prior to arrival, well beyond CD's 21-day floor, shrinking the window during which attendees can book at the group rate as part of the committed block. The Hotel also may release block rooms to general inventory at its sole discretion at cutoff without first consulting Group to reduce attrition exposure.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival, and rooms unassigned at cutoff should be released for resale only after consultation with Group to reduce attrition damages.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's major arrival date. After consultation with Group, Hotel may offer unassigned rooms to other individuals or groups to reduce any damages Group may owe under the attrition clause.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms in the Group block must be requested and confirmed with Hotel no later than forty (40) days prior to the first date of the Event, which shall be August 2, 2027.

findings.headline: Hotel can terminate at will refunding only deposits, no damages owed
findings.finding_text: Section 8 allows the Hotel to terminate the entire agreement 'without cause,' at its sole discretion, whenever it determines performance 'impossible or commercially impracticable' in its own judgment, with the only remedy to Group being a refund of deposits and prepayments. This falls well short of CD's requirement that a hotel-initiated cancellation without contractual right trigger liability for Group's full direct, indirect, and consequential damages.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel cancels without a contractual right to do so, it should owe Group all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, not just a deposit refund.
findings.proposed_language: In the event Hotel terminates this Agreement other than as permitted under this Agreement, Hotel will pay Group for all direct, indirect, and consequential damages, expenses, attorney's fees, and costs incurred by Group on account of such termination, including but not limited to staff time and travel expenses to secure an alternate location for the Event, incremental room rate and airfare differentials, function space rental, and long distance telephone, postage, and printing costs, in addition to refunding all deposits and prepayments made hereunder within ten (10) business days of such termination notice.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may terminate this Agreement immediately and without cause upon written notice to the Group if the Hotel determines in its sole discretion that circumstances render performance impossible or commercially impracticable.

findings.headline: No square footage, ceiling height, rental waiver, or change-consent terms
findings.finding_text: Exhibit A lists only function names, rooms, and estimated attendance, with no minimum square footage or ceiling height specifications, no statement that room rental is waived/complimentary for program agenda space, no requirement of both parties' written consent before changing space assignments, and no guarantee of in-room AV/power/lighting/HVAC basics at no charge.
findings.cd_standard: Function space should be named with minimum square footage and ceiling height, unchangeable without both parties' written consent, complimentary with rental waived for program agenda space, and each room should include a wired microphone, podium, power, lighting, and HVAC at no charge.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will hold the meeting and function space set out in Exhibit A, with room rental charges waived, and specifies each function space assignment, minimum square footage of [X], and ceiling height of [X]. No change will be made to the function space assignments without the written consent of both parties. Meeting space outlined in Group's program agenda will be provided on a complimentary basis. Hotel will provide in each meeting room, at no charge, one wired microphone, a podium, power (including existing power outlets), proper lighting, and HVAC.
findings.location_section: Exhibit A — Function Space and Catering

findings.headline: No remedy if hotel reduces facilities, services, or staffing ratios
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no provision addressing what happens if the Hotel closes or limits restaurants, spa, fitness facilities, or contracted meeting space, or reduces service staffing ratios, leaving Group without a cure period or termination/renegotiation right if hotel services or amenities are materially reduced before the event.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel closes/limits facilities by more than 25% or reduces service staffing ratios, it should first offer equal alternatives at its own expense; absent resolution within 30 days, Group should be able to cancel without liability or renegotiate.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel closes or limits the hours of service of any current restaurant, health club, spa, fitness facility, contracted meeting space, or other hospitality venue or facility by more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its published capacity or full-service offering, or reduces the guest-to-staff service ratio of its housekeeping, restaurant, banquet, maintenance and engineering, or safety and security services in a manner a hotel industry executive would agree is material, Hotel will first have the option to provide equal alternative facilities or services, mutually agreeable and solely at Hotel's expense. Should no mutually agreeable alternative be reached within thirty (30) days, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability upon written notice to Hotel, or the parties may instead modify this Agreement on mutually agreed terms.

findings.headline: No cap or protection if any future-year rates were left unconfirmed
findings.finding_text: The contract fixes the group rate at $279 for the 2027 event, but includes no fallback protection — such as a 2% annual increase cap or market-decline discount mechanism — in case any portion of pricing is later revisited or adjusted, which CD's standard calls for as a general safeguard.
findings.cd_standard: Where room rates for a future year are not yet confirmed, increases should be capped at 2% per year, with a matching discount if market rates decline, and rates fixed in writing no later than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Should any room rate under this Agreement remain unconfirmed as of twelve (12) months prior to arrival, Hotel guarantees a maximum yearly increase of two percent (2%) over the rates quoted in this Agreement, and should the market average rate for same-tier hotels decline before Group's arrival, the group rate will be discounted by the same percentage.

findings.headline: No individual reservation confirmation, name-change, or no-show terms
findings.finding_text: The contract does not address timely reservation confirmations to attendees, name changes at the group rate, individual cancellation deadlines (e.g., 6pm day of arrival), no-show reinstatement, or refund timing for individual deposits — all of which CD's standard requires to protect attendees and Group's pickup credit.
findings.cd_standard: Confirmations should go out within 4 days (2 business days inside 30 days of arrival); name changes allowed at group rate up to arrival; individual cancellations free until 6pm day of arrival; no-shows reinstated next night; individual deposits refundable with 3 working days' notice, with cancellation money credited against attrition.
findings.proposed_language: Upon request, Hotel will send each registered guest confirmation of their reservation, and of any change to it, at no charge within four (4) days of receiving the information, or within two (2) business days if the request is received within thirty (30) days of arrival. Name changes may be made to room reservations at the group rate at any time up to and including the arrival date. No cancellation fee will be assessed for any room cancelled before 6:00 p.m. on the day of arrival. Hotel will reinstate no-shows for the following night at the rate of their existing reservation unless Group directs otherwise. Any individual reservation deposit will be refunded if notice of cancellation is received at least three (3) working days before arrival, and any individual cancellation money Hotel receives will be credited toward any attrition damages owed by Group.

findings.headline: Damages based on gross revenue at up to 90%, plus conflicting tables
findings.finding_text: Damages are calculated on gross room revenue (not 70% lost room profit) at tiers reaching up to 80% in the narrative text and up to 90% in the accompanying table — the two schedules also directly conflict with each other (e.g., 20%/40%/60%/80% in text versus 68%/81%/90% in the table), creating ambiguity as to which applies, and both exceed CD's profit-based, mitigation-credited approach. There is also no rebooking credit-back provision.
findings.cd_standard: Damages should be calculated as a percentage of room profit (70% of net group rate) on a sliding scale with mitigation credit and a rebooking credit-back within three years, not a percentage of gross revenue.
findings.proposed_language: In the event of cancellation, liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit on a sliding scale based on the date written notice of cancellation is received, and the dollar amount owed at each tier will be stated in this Agreement. One hundred percent (100%) of room profit is defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed single net group rate at the time of cancellation, multiplied by the final adjusted room block less allowable attrition. Should a ConferenceDirect client rebook the Hotel for another meeting within three (3) years, Hotel will credit up to 100% of the cancellation damages paid toward the new booking's room revenue, not to exceed the damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: If cancellation notice is provided one hundred eighty (180) days or more before the Event start date, liquidated damages shall equal twenty percent (20%) of gross room revenue. If notice is provided between one hundred twenty (120) and one hundred eighty (180) days before the Event start date, damages shall equal forty percent (40%) of gross room revenue. If notice is provided between sixty (60) and one hundred twenty (120) days before the Event start date, damages shall equal sixty percent (60%) of gross room revenue. If notice is provided fewer than sixty (60) days before the Event start date, damages shall equal eighty percent (80%) of gross room revenue.
findings.exposure_basis: Gross room revenue basis calculable as 465 rooms x 5 nights x $279 = $648,675 total block value, against which the 20-90% tiers would apply, substantially higher than a 70%-lost-profit calculation.

findings.headline: No staffing ratio guarantees for servers or bartenders
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no minimum staffing ratio commitments for plated or buffet meal service, no bartender ratios for hosted or cash bars, and no cap limiting labor fees to only functions under 25 people.
findings.cd_standard: Contract should guarantee minimum server ratios (1:25 plated breakfast, 1:20 plated lunch/dinner, 1:40/1:30 buffet) and bartender ratios (1:75 hosted, 1:100 cash bar) at no extra charge, with a labor fee only for functions under 25 people.
findings.proposed_language: At all meal functions, Hotel will provide at least one server for every twenty-five (25) guests at a plated breakfast and every twenty (20) guests at a plated lunch or dinner, and one server for every forty (40) guests at a buffet breakfast and every thirty (30) guests at a buffet lunch or dinner, with no extra service or labor charge for these ratios. At all functions where alcohol is served, Hotel will provide no fewer than one (1) bartender for every seventy-five (75) guests at hosted bars and one (1) bartender for every one hundred (100) guests at cash bars, with no bartender or service fees. There will be no special labor or service fees for any Group food or beverage function, except that functions of fewer than twenty-five (25) people will incur a labor fee of $150.

findings.headline: Renovation notice omits required scope/schedule/mitigation details
findings.finding_text: The 30-day notice and 7-day termination window are present, but the notice requirement doesn't specify that it must describe the planned scope, schedule for commencement/completion, anticipated impact, and Hotel's mitigation plan, as CD's standard requires. The contract also entirely omits provisions for a new build or reopening-after-closure scenario, including a fully-operational date commitment and damages if no suitable alternative venue is found.
findings.cd_standard: Renovation notice should include scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan; new-build/reopening scenarios should include a committed operational date, 5-day change notice, termination right, and hotel-paid damages if no alternative venue is found.
findings.proposed_language: Should the Hotel determine, after execution of this Agreement, that renovation or construction work must be undertaken in areas that would materially interfere with Group's use and enjoyment of its reserved space or the conduct of the Event, the Hotel shall provide written notice to Group of such planned work at least thirty (30) days prior to the date such work would commence, describing: (a) the planned scope of the project; (b) the schedule for commencement and completion; (c) the anticipated impact on areas Group will use; and (d) Hotel's plan for minimizing that impact.
findings.quoted_text: Should the Hotel determine, after execution of this Agreement, that renovation or construction work must be undertaken in areas that would materially interfere with Group's use and enjoyment of its reserved space or the conduct of the Event, the Hotel shall provide written notice to Group of such planned work at least thirty (30) days prior to the date such work would commence.

findings.headline: Contract contains no ConferenceDirect commission clause at all
findings.finding_text: There is no provision anywhere in the Agreement addressing commission payable to ConferenceDirect on actualized room revenue, timing of payment, treatment of miscoded or walked rooms, survival through a change of ownership/brand, or commission on cancellation damages.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should pay ConferenceDirect 10% commission on all actualized room revenue within 30 days of departure, including rooms outside the block, miscoded rooms, walked rooms, and no-show/cancellation credited nights, non-cancelable and non-transferable, plus 10% of any cancellation damages collected.
findings.proposed_language: All rates confirmed in this Agreement are commissionable at ten percent (10%) to ConferenceDirect, LLC. Hotel will pay commission to ConferenceDirect on all actualized room revenue, regardless of rate paid and including all rooms outside the block, within thirty (30) days of Group's departure, whether or not the master account has been paid in full. Commission for this booking is non-cancelable and non-transferable. Should the standard hotel or brand commission percentage increase before the Event, the higher percentage will apply; should Hotel change management company or brand affiliation, the new management will honor the existing commission, or the new brand's commission if higher. Hotel will pay ConferenceDirect ten percent (10%) of any liquidated damages paid by Group within ten (10) days of receiving them.

findings.headline: No nondiscrimination commitment or related termination right
findings.finding_text: The contract contains no commitment from the Hotel that it and its staff will not discriminate against attendees on protected grounds, and no corresponding right for Group to terminate without liability if the state or city adopts legislation permitting such discrimination.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should commit to nondiscrimination against attendees on listed grounds, with a termination right if state/local legislation permits such discrimination.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel agrees that Hotel and its employees and agents will not discriminate against any of Group's attendees on the basis of sex, actual or perceived gender, age, race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, genetic information, or parental, marital, domestic partner, civil union, military, or veteran status, notwithstanding that such discrimination may be allowed under state or federal law. Should the state or city in which Hotel is located adopt legislation that affirmatively allows discrimination on any of these bases, or prohibits the adoption of nondiscrimination measures on any of these bases, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability.

findings.headline: No AV/internet pricing honor or bandwidth guarantee provisions
findings.finding_text: The contract has no provision honoring a pre-contracted AV or internet bandwidth quote, no discount commitment for add-on AV/internet needs, no minimum bandwidth guarantee, and no statement that use of the in-house AV provider is not a condition for discounted or complimentary internet.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should honor AV/internet quotes attached at contracting, guarantee minimum bandwidth of 10 Mbps down/1 Mbps up, discount later add-ons, and not condition discounted/complimentary internet on using the in-house AV provider.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will honor the pricing of the attached audio-visual quote, prepared from Group's specifications at the time of contracting, and will apply a discount of [X]% to any additional audio-visual needs, regardless of which provider is in place during the Event. Hotel will likewise honor the attached internet bandwidth quote, which provides a minimum of 10 Mbps download and 1 Mbps upload speed, with a discount of [X]% on any additional needs. Use of Hotel's in-house audio-visual provider, exclusively or otherwise, will not be a condition of any discounted or complimentary service, such as internet.

clause_review.basis: CD requires 35% of shortfall billed and affiliate/exhibitor revenue counted; contract charges full dollar-for-dollar shortfall and is silent on affiliate/exhibitor revenue counting toward minimum.
Group may retain outside vendors for AV, decorating, security, transportation at no surcharge ($0.00 stated).

CD requires cumulative measurement, 70% threshold, 95% occupancy credit, audit rights, formula-based damages, credit-back on rebooking; contract uses night-by-night measurement, 85% threshold, and has no rebooking credit-back provision, and 100% occupancy (not 95%) triggers no-credit exception.

CD requires broad list of triggers including reasonable-judgment standard, 20% attendee cancellation trigger, right to invoke regardless of foreknowledge, waiver of fees for reduced meeting, prompt refund; contract requires 'physically impossible' standard (narrower than commercially impracticable/inadvisable), excludes attendee safety concerns absent government order, has no 20%-cancellation trigger, no reduced-meeting fee waiver, deducts hotel's costs from refund, and requires 10-day notice of claim not present in CD standard.

CD requires resort fee waived for attendees (or discounted/fixed) and no early check-in/bag fees; contract discloses resort fee but sets it at $26/night with no waiver, and is silent on early check-in/bag fees; also allows hotel to add fees post-signing unilaterally in first sentence, contradicting the waiver-if-undisclosed sentence.

CD requires no-show/cancellation fees to count as room nights and complimentary internet regardless of loyalty status; contract sets 1:40 ratio (meets that part) but is silent on no-show/cancellation credit and internet, and expressly denies attrition-related recalculation protections only, not addressing these other elements.
Group may assign to successor/affiliated entity without unreasonable withholding of consent, assignee assumes obligations.
CD requires mutual insurance obligation; contract requires only Group to obtain/maintain $3M liability insurance, silent on Hotel's own insurance obligation.

CD requires group-side termination-for-cause rights across many causes with no liability; contract's Section 8 'Termination for Cause' is actually a hotel-side unilateral termination right, not a group termination right; it does not give Group the enumerated termination causes (pandemic determination, labor dispute, ownership change, renovation, facility reduction, convention center unavailability, discriminatory legislation) as a consolidated no-liability termination right independent of cancellation schedule, though some appear scattered in other clauses.
30-day notice of change, 30-day window to terminate without liability; refund timing not explicitly stated as 5 days but generally meets core requirement (silent on refund timing).
CD requires refund within 30 days; contract sets 45-day refund window, exceeding standard, though it does correctly restrict use to documented damage only.

CD requires 24/12-month reviews with adjustment rights, weekly pickup reports from a set lead time, final reports within 10 days of departure, 30-day post-event report, and audit rights including miscoded rooms at brand rates credited; contract provides weekly reports from 12 weeks out and 30-day post-event report but has no 24/12-month block review/adjustment mechanism, no final pickup report within 10 days of departure, and audit right exists but doesn't address miscoded-room crediting at brand/business rates.

CD requires clear division: Group funds auxiliary aids in event space, Hotel funds in guest rooms/common areas; contract instead splits cost 'in accordance with respective legal obligations' without a clear division, and ties Hotel's share only to facilities/operations rather than guest rooms and common areas explicitly, and lacks indemnification allocation for ADA obligations.
Governing law and venue set to Group's home state; no punitive/consequential damages; each party bears own fees.
Separate named storm clause with 75-mile/72-hour trigger and no-penalty cancellation.
Hotel barred from using attendee data for own marketing or selling/sharing to third parties without consent.

CD requires cancellation right regardless of whether hotel can still perform if strike/lockout/expired CBA arises within 90 days; contract conditions the cancellation right on the dispute 'materially affecting' services and voids the right if hotel determines full services will be available, contrary to CD's no-liability-regardless-of-performance standard.

CD's fallback uses 18% gratuity/6% service charge as example figures but core requirement is clear separation and full distribution of gratuity to staff, which contract meets; however service charge is set at 22% with no cap guidance in CD position beyond disclosure—this is not itself a deviation since CD doesn't cap service charge, so verdict reconsidered.

CD caps finance charge at 1% per month or legal max, whichever less; contract sets 1.5% per month; also CD requires staged deposit schedule for no-credit groups (25/25/50) or defined prepayment %, but contract just says 'percentage designated by the Hotel' at hotel's discretion with no defined %.

CD requires walked guests get an upgrade and welcome amenity on return, per-room-night rebate to Group ($200), pickup/commission credit for relocated nights, no attrition liability for walked nights, and extra compensation if 10+ guests/10%+ walked; contract explicitly denies upgrade, denies rebate to Group, denies pickup/commission credit, and has no extra-compensation trigger for large walks.

CD requires documented mitigation efforts available to Group and damages due 30 days after event contingent on evidence of mitigation; contract's Section 5 explicitly makes Hotel's resale records NOT subject to disclosure or audit by Group, and cancellation damages are due 30 days after Hotel's calculation (15 days from notice), not tied to proof of mitigation.

CD requires retroactive rate matching for prior reservations if a lower rate is found, and parity extended 7 days before/after event; contract explicitly makes any rate adjustment non-retroactive and applies only within the Event Period itself, not the surrounding 7-day window.

CD requires cutoff no earlier than 21 days prior to arrival and post-cutoff group-rate access as long as hotel sells to public, plus rooms released only after consultation to reduce attrition; contract sets cutoff at 40 days (earlier than 21-day floor) and releases block to general inventory at Hotel's sole discretion without consultation, though it does preserve group rate post-cutoff.

CD requires Hotel to pay Group's full direct/indirect/consequential damages if Hotel cancels without contractual right; contract's Section 8 instead lets Hotel terminate 'without cause' at its sole discretion merely refunding deposits/prepayments, with no damages owed to Group at all.

CD requires named function rooms with minimum square footage/ceiling height, no changes without written consent, complimentary space with rental waived, and in-room AV/power basics at no charge; contract's Exhibit A only lists function names, space, and attendance with no square footage, ceiling height, rental-waiver, change-consent, or in-room amenity provisions.
No clause addresses hotel closing/limiting restaurants, spa, fitness, meeting space or reducing staffing ratios with a cure/termination right.

Room rates for the 2027 event are already fixed at $279 with no future-year rate uncertainty language, but CD's standard on rate caps for unconfirmed future rates and market-decline discounts is not addressed at all in the contract.
No provisions on confirmation timing, name changes, individual cancellation deadlines, no-show reinstatement, or individual deposit refund timing appear in the contract.

CD requires damages based on 70% lost room profit (not gross revenue), mitigation credit, and rebooking credit-back; contract calculates damages on gross room revenue at escalating percentages up to 90% (and inconsistently lists both a narrative scale and a conflicting table with different percentages), with no rebooking credit-back provision.
No staffing ratio guarantees for servers or bartenders, and no cap on small-function labor fees, appear anywhere in the contract.

CD requires notice to include scope, schedule, impact, and mitigation plan, and separate new-build provisions with 5-day change notice and damages if no alternative venue found; contract gives 30-day notice and 7-day termination window but omits required notice content details and has no new-build/reopening provisions.
The contract contains no commission clause addressing payment to ConferenceDirect at all.
No nondiscrimination clause protecting attendees, nor termination right for discriminatory state/local legislation, appears in the contract.
No AV or internet bandwidth quote-honoring or discount provisions, and no bandwidth minimums, appear in the contract.

analysis.document_notes: The Cancellation clause (Section 4) contains an internal inconsistency: the narrative text sets a 20/40/60/80% sliding scale tied to 180/120/60-day breakpoints, while the accompanying table sets different breakpoints (181/91/31 days) and different percentages (68%/81%/90%). This conflict should be flagged to the property for clarification independent of the substantive gap against CD's profit-based standard. The document is otherwise clearly organized with numbered sections and one exhibit; no illegible or garbled passages were encountered.
